docs.title: InstantLink
docs.text:
InstantLink is an open-source Rust CLI and native macOS app for printing to Fujifilm Instax Link printers (Mini, Mini Link 3, Square, Wide) over Bluetooth Low Energy.

The Instax Link BLE protocol was reverse-engineered by the open-source community (javl/InstaxBLE, linssenste/instax-link-web). InstantLink packages that protocol into a production-oriented Rust core, CLI, FFI surface, and native macOS UI.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Description instantlink-core BLE protocol, image processing, model detection, device communication instantlink-cli Command-line interface with progress output and JSON for scan, info, and status instantlink-ffi C FFI bindings for Swift and other native frontends bridge Raspberry Pi camera FTP appliance using instantlink-ffi for printer transport, with optional iPhone photo sync (plan 050) ios SwiftUI iPhone app that pairs with the Bridge and pulls camera photos into the Photos library (plan 050)

docs.title: Supported Printers
docs.text: Model Resolution Film Type Instax Mini Link 600x800 Instax Mini Instax Mini Link 3 600x800 Instax Mini Instax Square Link 800x800 Instax Square Instax Wide Link 1260x840 Instax Wide

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Print JPEG, PNG, and other common image formats
  • Crop, contain, or stretch images to the selected printer model
  • Rich and Natural color modes
  • Automatic JPEG quality reduction to model-specific limits: Mini 105KB, Mini Link 3 55KB, Square 105KB, Wide 225KB
  • Battery, film remaining, charging, and print-count queries
  • LED color control with solid, blink, and breathe patterns
  • Native macOS app with camera capture, queue-based editing, film simulation, overlays for text/QR/timestamp/image/location, stage-aware reconnect UI, and experimental LED diagnostics in Settings
  • C FFI with 24 exported functions for native app integrations, including connect-stage progress callbacks
  • Bridge firmware bundles for Raspberry Pi appliances, published by CI and staged into the macOS app for the future Bridge control panel updater
  • Raspberry Pi Bridge appliance with optional iPhone sync: received camera photos can print, sync to the iOS app over a token-authed local HTTP API (Bonjour discovery), or both, plus a virtual LCD that mirrors and drives the Bridge screen from the phone (plans 050 / 054)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
InstantLink mirrors the structure of StatusLight: a reusable async Rust core, a thin CLI, and an FFI layer loaded by the SwiftUI macOS app via dlopen/dlsym.

Unlike StatusLight, there is no daemon crate. Instax printing is a one-shot workflow: connect, transfer, print, disconnect.

docs.title: InstantLink — Engineering Handover (2026-06-13)
docs.text:
This doc is the fast briefing for the next engineer (human or Claude Code session) picking up this repo. It is meant to be self-contained — read this and you can start contributing without having to reconstruct context.

Last verified: 2026-06-13. Main HEAD: 9d00c22 (Plan 048 PR #17 lands on top of this). Bridge HEAD on the test Pi: ad638be (unchanged from the previous handover).

docs.title: 1. What InstantLink is
docs.text:
Three components under one brand:

Component What it is Where it lives App macOS SwiftUI app (InstantLink.app). Sends photos to an Instax Link printer over BLE or to a Bridge over HTTP. macos/InstantLink/ Bridge Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W appliance. Receives camera photos over FTP (hotspot or same-Wi-Fi), prepares them per Instax model, and prints over BLE. Has its own 240×240 LCD + joystick UI. bridge/ Core / CLI / FFI Rust workspace: instantlink-core (BLE + image pipeline), instantlink-cli (terminal binary), instantlink-ffi (C ABI for Swift dlopen). crates/

The App talks to the Bridge over HTTP (when on the same network) and to a printer directly over BLE. The Bridge talks to the printer over BLE via the same Rust core, loaded as libinstantlink_ffi.so on the Pi.

Rules of brand naming (enforced in /CLAUDE.md): - "InstantLink" alone = the umbrella project. Don't use it to mean the App when the distinction matters. - "App" = the macOS app. "Bridge" = the Pi appliance. "Printer" = the Instax device. - The Bridge LCD UI shows compact strings (recent rename: "Searching Printer" — landed in ad638be).

docs.title: 2. Current versions
docs.text:
• App + crates: 0.1.45 (Cargo.toml in all three crates; App built with bash scripts/build-app.sh 0.1.45).
  • Bridge service version is governed by bridge/pyproject.toml and tracked separately.
  • The About sheet in App Settings shows the running App + Core versions side by side — use it to confirm the installed .app is fresh after a rebuild.

Always bump the three Cargo.toml versions in sync when you rebuild. See the rationale in /CLAUDE.md.

docs.title: 3. What just shipped (this session — plan 048, all 17 PRs)
docs.text:
The entire Photos-style editor rebuild scoped in docs/plans/047-photos-style-editor-audit.md / docs/plans/048-photos-style-editor-implementation.md landed across 17 PRs. The legacy EditorViews.swift (1364 lines) is deleted; the useNewEditor feature flag is gone; the new editor is the only editor. See plan 048 §PR Status for per-PR commit hashes.

Shipping summary by surface:

  • Editor shell (PR #1) — top tab bar, HSplitView, active-tab routing, observable EditorViewState, undo/redo with 200 ms debounce, MTKView preview via CIRenderDestination.
  • Crop tab (PR #2) — aspect / straighten / V/H / flip / frame; print-aware Mini / Square / Wide aspect presets.
  • Adjust tab — Light (PR #3), Color (PR #4), Curves + Levels + Histogram (PR #5), Vignette (PR #6), Sharpen (PR #7), Noise Reduction (PR #8), Definition (PR #9), Selective Color (PR #10, 6 user-defined wells via custom CIColorKernel), Red Eye (PR #11, Vision auto-detect + click-to-fix), White Balance + shared Eyedropper infrastructure (PR #12), Black & White mode (PR #13).
  • Annotate tab (PR #14) — ported the legacy overlay system (text / QR / timestamp / image / location) into the new shell; deleted EditorViews.swift; retired the useNewEditor flag.
  • Filter rail (PR #15) — vertical thumbnail strip + FilterThumbnailCache + FilterCatalog with the B&W ↔ Filters interop override from decision Q9.
  • Auto buttons (PR #16) — per-section Auto wired to CIImage.autoAdjustmentFilters + global Enhance (magic-wand) toolbar button.
  • Polish + fidelity pass + version bump (PR #17 — this session's commit):
  • AdjustmentSlider: option-drag extended range (±2× via a simultaneous DragGesture), double-click reset on the row, accessibilityLabel/accessibilityValue plus accessibilityAdjustableAction for VoiceOver.
  • Pipeline coefficients tuned: LightPipeline contrast multiplier 0.6 → 0.5; brilliance composite + Cast scales reconfirmed against the research files. Vignette ramp documented as intentionally linear.
  • Histogram refresh already debounced to 100 ms via Combine (verified, no change needed).
  • Localization backfill for the 7 non-CJK locales (de, es, fr, it, pt-BR, ar, he) on the tab bar, every section title, the 7 Light section slider labels, and the common button verbs (Done / Revert / Undo / Redo / Auto / Reset / Enhance).
  • Stale editor_coming_in_pr_2 and editor_coming_in_pr_3 keys dropped from all 12 locales.
  • PR #14 audit nits cleared: OverlayListRow help-text now describes the action (Lock/Unlock, Hide/Show) using new annotate_overlay_{lock,unlock,show,hide} keys; displayTitle + defaultTitle extracted to OverlayItem and the duplicated copies in OverlayListRow and OverlayInspectorView are gone; "Select an image to print" replaced with the dedicated annotate_select_image_overlay key; film-frame Q4 decision documented in EditorPreview.swift (the editor canvas is pixel-accurate and intentionally does not render the Instax border).
  • Crate versions bumped to 0.1.45 for instantlink-core / instantlink-ffi / instantlink-cli to match the App.

docs.title: 4. Open / partially done
docs.text:
These are the loose threads. None are blockers.

  • Reconnect timing (plan 045 finding F9) — attemptConnection's 3-second deadline may be too short for cold BLE adverts on real hardware. Not measured. Out of scope for 048.

  • PrinterPickerSheet redesign (plan 045 finding F3) — "Switch Printer" opens a sheet that is unhelpful when only the dead saved printer is around. Out of scope; would couple with a broader Printers panel rethink.

  • Bridge venv on the Pi has no pytest — when running the bridge test suite live on the Pi during the LCD work, the deployed venv didn't have pytest installed (it's a runtime venv, not dev). Tests pass logically; not run end-to-end on hardware.

  • App-side test coverage — there is no Swift test harness in this repo. UI changes are verified by build + run + manual test. Document any new behaviour with a steps-to-reproduce comment if it's non-obvious.

  • Editor v2 follow-ups out of plan 048 — HDR / wide-gamut preview (P3 + extended-range), RAW pipeline integration with Apple's neural-engine NR, per-slider numeric input boxes, Lightroom-import preset format, real-time camera-capture editing (Phase 4 of 041). See plan 048 §5 for the full out-of-scope list.

docs.title: Build + install the App
docs.text:
bash scripts/build-app.sh 0.1.46   # bump version per CLAUDE.md
# Always rm before cp — bare `cp -R` over an existing bundle can leave stale files:
pkill -x InstantLink; sleep 1
rm -rf /Applications/InstantLink.app
cp -R target/release/InstantLink.app /Applications/InstantLink.app
open /Applications/InstantLink.app

docs.title: Verify Rust workspace
docs.text: cargo fmt --all && cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Reach the test Bridge
docs.text:
The Pi is reachable over its USB-gadget link at 192.168.7.1 from this Mac's en10 interface. SSH user hongjunwu. Use -B en10 (or BindInterface=en10 for scp) — the /22 netmask on en0 collides with 192.168.7.x otherwise. Diagnostic recipes: 

# Inspect the LCD backlight path on the Pi:
ssh hongjunwu@192.168.7.1 'ls -la /sys/class/backlight/fb_st7789v/'
ssh hongjunwu@192.168.7.1 'cat /sys/kernel/debug/gpio | grep GPIO24'
ssh hongjunwu@192.168.7.1 'sudo cat /etc/InstantLinkBridge/config.toml | grep ^idle_'

docs.title: Deploy bridge code to the Pi (when changing bridge code, not config)
docs.text:
The deploy script needs INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_HOST / _USER env vars: 

INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_HOST=192.168.7.1 INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_USER=hongjunwu \
bash bridge/scripts/deploy-to-pi.sh --restart

docs.title: Run bridge tests
docs.text:
cd bridge && python -m ruff check src tests && python -m mypy src tests && python -m pytest -q
No local venv is set up automatically — use whatever Python ≥3.11 you have, or create one in bridge/.venv.

docs.title: 6. Where the recent stale-doc fixes landed
docs.text:
When picking up this work, treat these as already-current: - /CLAUDE.md (terminology, FFI count corrected, example app version updated). - /README.md (What's Included table reorganised). - bridge/docs/current-context.md (verified date + commit + idle thresholds refreshed). - docs/plans/048-photos-style-editor-implementation.md (PR Status table is the source of truth for what landed in each PR of the editor rebuild).

If you discover further staleness, fix it in the same PR — don't leave it for next time. The audit pattern for this is: 

grep -rn --include='*.md' \
  --exclude-dir=.claude --exclude-dir=references --exclude-dir=tmp \
  --exclude-dir=.pytest_cache --exclude-dir=plans --exclude-dir=node_modules \
  -E "<keyword>" .
Keywords worth sweeping any time you change a UX string, a config default, or a public symbol.

Paste the following as your first message in a new Claude Code session to bring the assistant up to speed cold:

The Photos-style editor rebuild scoped in plans 047/048 is complete (all 17 PRs landed); the legacy EditorViews.swift is deleted and the useNewEditor flag is gone. Bridge HEAD on the test Pi is still ad638be (riverps-rpi-zero-2w, reachable at 192.168.7.1 over en10). Open threads listed in §4 of the handover. For LCD/Bridge work, the bridge/docs/current-context.md doc is the freshest picture of what's deployed.

docs.title: LCD rendering evidence
docs.text:
Plan 086 records the source, hardware and independent acceptance for cac3318.

  • host-packing.json: producer host conversion samples (host timing is not Pi timing).
  • independent-source-review.json: exhaustive RGB and input/UI frame oracle results.
  • source-validation.json: normal source and independent affected test gates.
  • live-render-benchmark.json: per-frame Pi spans, CPU clocks and exact framebuffer hashes.
  • gpio-validation.json: 11 cases per variant through owned kernel mockup edges, production input/controller and actual LCD. Queue durations exclude contact latency and include CPU wake.
  • status-reconnect-validation.json: no-film startup, subsequent fresh polling and locked recovery.
  • independent-hardware-review.json / independent-installed-review.json: fresh reviewer acceptance.
  • cleanup.json / final-health.json / running-log-review.json: restored production state and logs.
  • independent-final-review.json: independent restored-device, log and documentation signoff.

Full raw journals and observer traces are retained privately under /tmp/instantlink-lcd-*086*. No image/print commands, battery lifetime measurement, panel scanout timing or physical button actuation occurred. Framebuffer byte equivalence is the display quality gate.

docs.title: LCD text and layout evidence
docs.text:
Plan 087 validates clean source 06bbe86 on Pi Zero 2 W/ST7789 with no film.

  • source-validation.json, host-text-benchmark.json, baseline-pi-profile.log: source gates and profiling. Host timings are not Pi timings.
  • independent-source-review.json, independent-cache-probes.json: frozen original renderer comparisons, clipping/font/cache cases and concurrent rendering acceptance.
  • live-render-benchmark.json: actual framebuffer spans and exact accepted frame hashes; the mixed-clock initial trial is excluded explicitly.
  • cold-warm-drawing.json: original RGB oracle and glyph-cache-cold/immediate-warm spans with fonts already loaded, separate from actual framebuffer timing.
  • pi-pixel-matrix.json: all modes, both themes/languages and three font sizes, using Pi font files; preview immutability and RGB equality against original source.
  • gpio-validation.json, status-reconnect-validation.json: production input/controller/LCD through kernel mockup, same-button unlock/timeout/CPU tiers and status-only reconnect.
  • independent-hardware-review.json, independent-installed-review.json, independent-final-review.json: independent acceptance at each stage.
  • final-health.json, cleanup.json, running-log-review.json: restored production state, exact source/native provenance, removed fixtures and retained historical faults.

Raw observer traces and full journals are retained privately under /tmp/instantlink-lcd-text-*087*. No image/print commands, film, panel scanout/contact latency or battery-runtime measurement. Mask pixel storage is capped below 3 MiB; metadata, strings and font overhead are additional.

docs.title: RGB565 packing evidence
docs.text:
Plan 088 validates 398dde5 on Pi Zero 2 W/ST7789 without film.

  • packing-options-pi.json / packing-options-host.json: exact strategy comparisons; Pi measurements select uint16 output/scratch. Host timings are not Pi timings.
  • numpy-import-cost.json: fresh subprocess import and peak RSS with pagecache already warm; module import dominates retained-memory tradeoff, separate from local per-frame buffers.
  • source-validation.json / independent-source-review.json: gates, exhaustive scalar oracle, fallback/concurrency/memory and owned-loader lifecycle checks. Arithmetic exhaustive run preceded the final scheduling-only delta; report records both hashes.
  • live-render-benchmark.json / first-paint-validation.json: settled actual framebuffer spans/hash equality and explicit paint-before-loader-start order in warm service restarts.
  • gpio-validation.json: production queue/controller/actual LCD via kernel mockup edges; physical contacts and scanout not measured.
  • status-reconnect-validation.json: fresh status and locked automatic recovery, no images.
  • independent-hardware-review.json, independent-installed-review.json, independent-final-review.json: independent staged acceptance.
  • cleanup.json / final-health.json / running-log-review.json: normal state, exact provenance, fixture removal and retained historical faults. Raw journals are private.

Preliminary/unsettled measurements and a fixture call before Booting completed were excluded from accepted results and retained privately under /tmp/instantlink-rgb565-*088*. No image/print commands, film, battery-runtime or contact-to-photon measurement.

docs.title: Plan 094 validation evidence
docs.text:
Three agents investigated, implemented and independently reviewed the transient Bluetooth fixes. No raw journal, pairing key or private configuration content is included here.

The investigation suggested earlier escalation. The final reviewed policy allows two exact native setup drops at INFO, matching the existing two-retry recovery burst, then warns on the third unresolved drop. Same-target absence and other failures do not reset that allowance.

The final full Bridge suite passed 2,451 tests, with eight expected Mac GPIO fallback warnings. Ruff formatting (158 files), lint, strict mypy (68 source files), diff checks and strict MkDocs passed. The independent reviewer ran 370 affected checks after the recovery logging amendment.

docs.title: Initial evidence and rejected probes
docs.text: installed-health.json records the initial aa852e1 installation, before Printer availability. Its readiness probes timed out before Disconnect. initial-live-health.json records a later connected attempt whose observer timed out on identical status logged only at DEBUG. That observability gap was fixed and independently reviewed; this probe is not an accepted reconnect.

docs.title: Accepted installed checks
docs.text:
reconnect-1.json and reconnect-2.json measure external Disconnect dispatch to accepted fresh controller status: 11.159 and 7.367 seconds. All 32 samples retained PID13213, 600 MHz/powersave, backlight GPIO24 low and FTP220/200; film zero unchanged. The second encountered an actual setup drop, preserved with native stage/detail at INFO before automatic recovery.

accepted-health.json records clean 7c312ad with reviewed hashes, connected/fresh Printer, active services/backup socket and no warnings/errors in its complete 132-record current-PID journal. No film, image or actuator commands. No manual internal lock-state/physical-contact/Printer power-cycle test or matched speedup claim. Transient physical drops have not been eliminated.

Independent final evidence review passed (live-review.json). Root then removed both owned remote helper files and confirmed Bridge, manager and the production backup socket remained active.

docs.title: Plan 095 evidence
docs.text:
native-discovery-cadence.json measures production controller/provider/Rust FFI on the Pi with an unmatched synthetic Printer name and NullDisplay. Bridge service was stopped for the probe and restored by an EXIT trap. No real Printer connection, key change, print, image or film command.

Awake starts were 1.378–1.392 seconds apart, including a one-second scan plus driver overhead. Dark discovery started after 30.002 seconds with a five-second window at 600 MHz. First unlock input woke the scan in 40.8 ms; CPU was at 1 GHz when that press completed. The scan can start while the CPU helper is warming, before the remaining two presses complete unlocking.

lcd-preview.png shows candidate rendering with synthetic credentials and Mac font fallbacks, not photographs of the physical panel. Both empty-film modes and English/Chinese large text were visually reviewed; Network and Screen groups fit the 240×240 viewport.

Local final source gate: 2,481 Bridge tests, eight expected Mac GPIO fallback warnings; 602 focused checks, Ruff lint/format (159 files), strict mypy (68 files) and strict MkDocs. Unrelated preexisting App localization failures were observed during read-only contract review; App sources/resources were not changed and those checks are not included in this Bridge validation claim.

Installed automatic boot/reconnect checks passed after Printer power-on:

  • boot-result.json: UI ready 14.138 s, FTP/core ready 14.152 s, fresh Printer status 20.041 s from kernel startup, without a button action. Pre-kernel firmware time is excluded; this is not a matched availability-controlled speedup comparison. Film 10→10.
  • reconnect.json: external BlueZ Disconnect → fresh automatic status 8.885 s with the normal service's screen off. All 14 samples retained PID 502, 600 MHz/powersave, backlight low and FTP 220/200. One canonical GATT setup drop recovered through a prompt retry. Film 10→10.
  • accepted-health.json: Bridge/manager active with zero automatic restarts, Printer connected, throttle 0x0, backup socket active and reviewed source/unchanged FFI hashes. Complete Bridge PID journal had 83 records and zero warning/error matches at capture.
  • running-log-review.json: wider Bridge/manager/Bluetooth review retained two BlueZ notices and one manager hotspot-bind retry, which became listening after 1.004 s. Hotspot HTTP answered afterward. System boot has 22 platform warning-priority records; no global warning-free claim. No image, print or Printer actuator commands were used.

The initial boot observer mistakenly classified GPIO initialization as button input. Rechecking the retained journal's actual ui.input action= events accepted the same reboot; no second reboot was needed. Production service stayed running. These checks verify normal automatic screen-off idle; internal manual-lock flags and physical button contacts were not inspected.

handoff-health.json records the final docs-only deployment of clean c1aa432, preserving Bridge 502/manager661 and zero automatic restarts. The Printer subsequently disconnected at 17:12:29, about five minutes after recovery, and the next scan found no advertisement. The Bridge received the disconnect event and resumed discovery with no warning/error records. Physical Printer power-off was not observed; the final connected state is false, distinct from the accepted live checks above. FTP, 600 MHz/powersave/backlight low, backup socket and throttle0x0 remained healthy.

docs.title: Plan 096 evidence
docs.text:
Hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0, ST7789 framebuffer LCD, X306 2300 mAh; Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82. Saved Printer: Link Square INSTAX-52006924. No Printer image-transfer, print or actuator commands; no film used. The isolated FTP fixture never dispatches to a Printer.

  • import-cost.json: fresh Python app imports with warm filesystem cache in powersave/performance/performance/powersave order, retaining the production service and restoring powersave. Includes runuser/process startup. Isolates import CPU cost, not full boot.
  • baseline-core.json: normal installed 0d79921 reboot with Printer unavailable. Kernel monotonic timings exclude pre-kernel firmware time; no injected input. SSH sampling starts after SSH becomes available and does not prove the governor during interpreter imports.

Three subagents investigated startup, implemented the changes and independently reviewed them. Primary review found a pending trust-snapshot race, independently confirmed and corrected before installation. Changed/invalidated trust now forces the existing bounded fresh retry. Final review accepted the correction; 166 independent focused tests passed. Initial corrected Bridge gate: 2,497 tests, eight expected host GPIO warnings, Ruff/format (161 files), strict mypy (68 source files), strict docs.

candidate-core.json and candidate-core-repeat.json are rejected CPU pre-start experiments, with the trust optimization also installed. They reached UI14.306/13.918 s and core14.930/14.640 s, versus baseline UI14.045/core14.059 s. The extra CPU hook did not demonstrate a clear readiness benefit and was removed, together with its two tests. Service startup ordering now matches the baseline; final no-hook hardware results must be evaluated separately. In the experiments, FFI-loaded→first discovery policy fell from baseline0.722 s to0.104/0.104 s, consistent with removing redundant inventory/trust processes. That is pre-discovery setup, not a connected-time result.

At the initial handoff, connected-time and installed reconnect acceptance were pending the Printer advertising. The attempted connected baseline timed out before reboot or Disconnect; it is not a passing connection result. A later reconnect readiness observer was interrupted by the repeat reboot before it could obtain status or issue Disconnect; it is not a reconnect test. Current verified measurements are scoped explicitly above.

docs.title: Final installed runtime
docs.text:
Clean 4049bcd, without the CPU pre-hook, passed the final 2,495-test Bridge gate (eight expected host GPIO warnings), Ruff, format (160 files), mypy (68 files) and strict docs.

final-core.json records normal boot: LCD13.742 s, FTP13.728 s, core13.756 s and hotspot receive-ready19.995 s. Baseline was LCD14.045/FTP14.036/core14.059/receive20.178 s. First discovery policy moved from15.013 to14.035 s; native-library-loaded→discovery setup from0.722 to0.072 s. These are single final/baseline reboots with no Printer advertisement or button input; they demonstrate less setup overhead, not a measured full connected-time improvement.

awake-health.json verifies a nonblank 240×240 framebuffer (156 distinct RGB565 values), 1 GHz and backlight high. installed-health.json verifies subsequent normal screen-off idle at600 MHz/ powersave/backlight low; its uniform cleared framebuffer is expected. Both retain Bridge475/ manager639, zero automatic restarts, FTP220/200, services/backup socket active, throttle0x0, reviewed installed source hashes and unchanged native FFI. Full current-boot Bridge PID journal has26 records and zero warning/error matches at the dark capture. Physical panel quality and button contacts were not observed.

isolated-ftp.json records an on-Pi production FTP service receiving a valid JPEG into its ReceivedImage queue with matching SHA256, authenticated STOR226 and NOOP200. It uses a temporary directory/credentials and high port with no application consumer or native backend, so it cannot use film. It does not test a physical camera or normal print dispatch. The first fixture inherited an unreadable login-home cwd; retry used the deployed service's normal /opt/InstantLinkBridge working directory. No production FTP change was required. Temporary files/server were cleaned up.

Full automatic boot-to-Printer and installed reconnect were pending at that checkpoint. The live follow-up below completes them; the earlier offline results remain separately scoped.

docs.title: Live follow-up — accepted
docs.text:
After Printer power-on, the unchanged production source booted automatically to fresh Printer status at 19.186 s, LCD at13.911 s and core at13.924 s, with no button action. Film 10→10. boot-connected.json records clean manifest40e0911 (docs over production4049bcd). Kernel startup clock excludes firmware latency. Earlier plan095 measured20.041 s; this individual run was0.855 s lower, not a controlled radio/bond/cache comparison or a general percentage speedup.

This live cached-but-untrusted device needed the retained trust command and guarded startup bond reset: FFI-loaded→first discovery was 0.874 s. The offline absent-target0.072 s result does not describe every connection. Remaining measured startup costs include process launch→ boot marker3.349 s, trust/reset about0.85 s and BLE-connect→service-discovery1.763 s.

reconnect.json records external BlueZ Disconnect dispatch→accepted fresh status 11.267 s. All21 samples retained Bridge497,600MHz/powersave/backlight low and FTP220/200; film 10→10. Samples begin2.273 s after dispatch because Disconnect blocks initially; no continuous observation claim during that initial interval. Normal automatic screen-off idle was observed; no physical button contacts or internal manual-lock flags were tested. No setup failure or warning/error.

connected-health.json confirms Bridge497/manager655 active, zero automatic restarts, Printer connected/fresh, throttle0x0, active network/Bluetooth/backup socket, reviewed source and unchanged FFI hashes. Complete current-boot Bridge PID journal91records has no warning/error matches. live-log-review.json retains three wider records: BlueZ directory mode, manager hotspot bind pending (listening1.007 s later), and BlueZ's no-matching-connection notice. No whole-system warning-free claim. Independent evidence review accepted both trials. No film or Printer image/ print/actuator commands; physical camera and film output were not tested.

docs.title: Plan 097 evidence
docs.text:
Hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0, ST7789 240×240 framebuffer, X3062300mAh; Debian13.2, kernel6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python3.13.5, BlueZ5.82. Saved Printer: Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924. All Printer checks are status/discovery/disconnect only; no image-transfer, print or actuator command and no film used.

  • import-comparison.json: two warmups then three counterbalanced fresh processes per source; same installed interpreter/dependencies, warm filesystem/precompiled bytecode, observed powersave600MHz throughout, no governor mutation. Baseline app-import median2.108s, candidate2.026s; overlapping ranges and small sample count limit inference. Whole process wall time is recorded separately. Normal Bridge retained; no app run or device operations.
  • image-baseline.json, image-candidate.json: isolated actual image worker prepares retained DSC02821.HIF and an asymmetric EXIF6 JPEG for Square/Mini Link3/Wide. All4 JPEG SHA/bytes/ dimensions/quality/fit/flip fields match exactly. Single timing observations measure worker preparation, not full upload latency or physical print quality; candidate first JPEG includes deferred processing imports. No consumer/backend/Printer exists in this probe.
  • render-comparison.json:92 deterministic offscreen Pi frames covering every mode and3 Post editors, English/Chinese, light/dark. Exact RGB bytes vs baseline, not physical panel/contact observation. No LCD writes or Printer operations.
  • baseline-boot.json: unchanged clean44e6cb4 normal reboot, no buttons before fresh status, LCD13.822s/core13.835s/Printer20.484s, film10→10. Kernel monotonic clock excludes firmware time.

Source079af5a matches every one of the17 production files in the clean temporary benchmark archive. Independent review accepted source and predeployment evidence. Full2527 Bridge tests, eight expected host GPIO fallback warnings, Ruff/format164/mypy70/strict docs pass. Review fixed cancelled-import cleanup and first-editor render import-lock risks; queued input still awaits that first editor activation while the event loop remains responsive.

Initial AppleDouble-containing staging archive was replaced before accepted probes. Concurrent import/image timing attempts were rejected and rerun sequentially. Temporary Pi files were removed by the baseline reboot. No production defect or timing result is inferred from them.

docs.title: Installed acceptance
docs.text:
• installed-boot.json: clean079af5a, automatic reboot without Bridge input. LCD13.665s, FTP13.652s/core13.676s/fresh Printer18.962s, film10→10. Compared with baseline, process launch to boot marker3.340→3.233s; whole connected time20.484→18.962s includes radio/bond variation. Single paired reboots do not attribute the1.522s difference to Python imports or establish a general speedup. Kernel timing excludes firmware startup. Candidate used the retained guarded reset while baseline discovery took longer.
  • awake-health.json, installed-health.json: actual framebuffer populated148RGB565values/ 115200bytes at1GHz/performance/backlight high, then normal idle600MHz/powersave/backlight low (cleared framebuffer expected). PID482/manager640, zero automatic restarts, connected Printer, FTP220/200, active services/backup socket, throttle0x0. Source hashes match079af5a and the archived candidate; unit/FFI unchanged. No physical panel/contact observation.
  • reconnect.json: external BlueZ Disconnect→fresh automatic status12.543s, film10→10. All23samples samePID/600MHz/powersave/backlight low/FTP220+200. First sample2.590s after dispatch; no continuous initial observation claim. First scan absent at INFO; existing prompt retry succeeded. No manual Reconnect or warnings/errors. Normal screen-off idle, not internal manual-lock flag introspection.
  • isolated-ftp.json: installed production FTP service receives JPEG byte-for-byte into its queue, STOR226/NOOP200, temporary directory/credentials/highport, no consumer/backend/Printer calls. Normal port21 retained. Physical camera and normal application print dispatch not tested.
  • live-log-review.json: full current-boot three-service journal124records, current Bridge PID 101records/zero warnings-errors. Retains BlueZ directorymode and requested-disconnect notices, manager bind pending resolves1.006s later. System/kernel outside this snapshot; no global warning-free claim. Raw service journal retained privately and reviewed; remote copy removed.

No film used. Final independent evidence review accepted scope and findings. Source remains 079af5a; the final documentation deployment refreshes the clean manifest without restarting it.

docs.title: Plan 098 evidence
docs.text:
The socket-ordering experiment was rejected. Final production ordering is unchanged from accepted a815fb1. New regression tests protect daemon lifetime ordering and manager recovery.

Hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero2W Rev1.0/ST7789 240×240/X3062300mAh; Debian13.2, kernel6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python3.13.5, BlueZ5.82. Saved Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924. No Printer image-transfer, print or actuator commands; no film used.

docs.title: Experiment and controls
docs.text:
• baseline-core.json: unchanged a815fb1 normal reboot, no input, UI13.605683s, FTP13.582428s/core13.616155s. Printer absent; null status is not a passing Printer check. Initial connected observer timed out after reboot; actual component journal was captured.
  • candidate-core.json, candidate-capture.json: clean80c2c8d orders against active dbus.socket; actual process9.398s < daemonREADY9.866s. UI13.595050s, FTP13.593595s/core13.609813s. No meaningful end-to-end readiness gain demonstrated (single reboots; no general performance inference). The earlier launch did not advance observed readiness. Printer unavailable.
  • candidate-awake-health.json: actual nonblank ST7789 framebuffer115200bytes/156RGB565values, 1GHz/performance/backlight high; no runtime Bridge warnings. Not physical panel/contact testing.
  • before-candidate-reboot.json: candidate deployed/restarted into prior boot asPID1985 before full reboot. Unit SHA identifies actual changed dependency during the recorded shutdown. Its uptime216s milestones describe a service restart and are not boot-time measurements.
  • candidate-shutdown.json: full reboot shutdown6.728s, successful/no forced kill. Daemon stops 235.116s before Bridge239.296s. Retains status-worker cancellation and D-Bus/BlueZ activation refusal warnings, proving the removed reverse dependency matters to lifecycle review.
  • baseline-shutdown.json: prior accepted a815fb1 boot shutdown6.176s/no Bridge warnings; Bridge1499.511s before daemon1499.533s. Nonmatched native-worker/radio phases do not isolate warning causality or shutdown speed. Baseline is a separate prior boot, not baseline-core's subsequent shutdown, which already had the candidate unit installed before restart/reboot.

Both candidate and restored source gates pass2529tests/eight expected Mac GPIO fallback warnings, Ruff/format165/mypy70/strict docs. On-Pi candidate systemd verification passed. Three subagents audited, implemented and independently reviewed. Independent review accepted rejection: tiny/null measured readiness benefit does not justify removing the daemon dependency. No warning suppression, service disabling, CPU-policy change or manager serialization was added.

All timing is kernel monotonic and excludes pre-kernel firmware startup; wall clocks may differ. The first previous-boot observer needed boot-ID hyphens removed for journalctl's accepted ID format; its failed invocation changed no device state or production code.

One native disconnect_failed code=-3 warning when BlueZ stops independently. Not suppressed; no forced kill, native grace expiry or resource failure. Native/agent cleanup algorithms unchanged.

Samples start1.834s after dispatch; no continuous initial observation claim. One absent scan at INFO then prompt retry connects, no warning/error/manual Reconnect. Final independent review accepted the scope, rejection and restored installed validation. No Printer image-transfer, print or actuator commands; film10→10. docs.title: Later handoff availability
docs.text:
After the passing boot/reconnect checks, the Printer link dropped and a subsequent automatic scan reported not advertising. No physical power-state observation was made. The Bridge handled the disconnect without warning/error and remained PID501/600MHz/powersave, FTP220/200, manager659 active/zero automatic restarts, accepted source/unit hashes and clean manifestad72ada. handoff-health.json records this later snapshot; it does not replace or invalidate the earlier passing tests. Do not describe the Printer as connected at final handoff. No further Printer availability is needed to complete the already accepted unit audit; no film used.

handoff-events.json retains the later current-boot journal records after the accepted fresh status. It confirms the subsequent disconnect and not-advertising scan; the older failure array in the health snapshot alone does not prove that event ordering. No physical power inference.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: InstantLink uses a layered Rust core with thin CLI and FFI frontends, plus a native SwiftUI macOS app.

docs.title: Dependency Graph
docs.text:
instantlink-cli ──→ instantlink-core
instantlink-ffi ──→ instantlink-core
macOS app ───────→ instantlink-ffi (device operations, via dlopen, bundled dylib)
macOS app ───────→ bundled instantlink-cli (version metadata only)

docs.title: instantlink-core
docs.text: The core crate owns BLE communication, model detection, protocol encoding, and image preparation. It is fully async with tokio and btleplug.

docs.title: Module Layers
docs.text:
printer.rs     ← High-level API (scan, connect, print_file)
    ↓
device.rs      ← PrinterDevice trait + BlePrinterDevice
    ↓
transport.rs   ← BLE GATT transport (btleplug)
    ↓
commands.rs    ← Command/Response enums
    ↓
protocol.rs    ← Packet build/parse, checksum, fragmentation
    ↓
models.rs      ← PrinterModel enum + per-model specs
error.rs       ← PrinterError + Result alias
image.rs       ← Load, resize, encode, chunk

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text:
• Async throughout: btleplug requires async BLE access, so the core stays async end to end.
  • Model-aware behavior: BlePrinterDevice::new detects the model from IMAGE_SUPPORT_INFO dimensions. Exact ASCII-trimmed DIS FI033 distinguishes Mini Link 3 at 600 × 800; exact FI017 must agree with Square dimensions. Conflicting or ambiguous known hints fail closed; other unknown hints retain dimension matching.
  • Startup query recovery: the BLE transport can resend the read-only capability query once after a one-second ACK wait, within the original ten-second deadline. One command lock and delivery guard span both attempts. Failed delivery retires the connection; print and image transfer commands retain their existing recovery rules.
  • ACK-based transfer: each image chunk is sent only after the previous chunk is acknowledged.
  • Model-specific JPEG limits: quality reduction targets each model's own image-size cap instead of a single global threshold.
  • Transport abstraction: transport::Transport allows mock transports in tests without requiring hardware.

docs.title: instantlink-cli
docs.text:
The CLI is a thin clap frontend around instantlink_core::printer.

  • Commands: scan, info, print, led set, led off, status
  • JSON output is implemented for scan, info, and status
  • Human-readable flows use spinners and progress text rather than mirroring raw protocol events

docs.title: instantlink-ffi
docs.text:
The FFI crate exposes the Rust core through a C ABI.

  • Global tokio runtime via OnceLock<Runtime>
  • Mutex-protected connected device handle
  • catch_unwind on all extern entry points
  • 24 exported functions, including lifecycle, status, printing, LED control, keepalive, printer shutdown / reset, and connection-stage progress callbacks

docs.title: macOS App
docs.text:
The macOS app lives in macos/InstantLink/ and is split by responsibility.

  • App/ holds the SwiftUI app entry point, restart helper, and app delegate
  • Core/ holds shared app state (ViewModel), persisted app models, runtime services, and coordinator/service layers for printer connection, queue editing, and print rendering
  • Features/ groups UI by workflow: Camera/, Editor/, Main/, and Settings/
  • Support/ holds reusable UI primitives such as film frames, preview helpers, overlay canvas rendering, and shared visual styles
  • OverlayModels.swift defines the overlay data model and typed payloads
  • InstantLinkFFI.swift loads libinstantlink_ffi.dylib and resolves the FFI symbols at runtime
  • .lproj/Localizable.strings bundles provide 12-language localization
  • Deployment baseline is macOS 15 (arm64-apple-macosx15.0 in scripts/build-app.sh and LSMinimumSystemVersion 15.0 in macos/Info.plist.template)

The app no longer compiles a Swift CLI wrapper or keeps a CLI fallback path for printer operations. Runtime printer/device work goes through InstantLinkFFI.swift into the bundled libinstantlink_ffi.dylib. The bundled instantlink-cli binary remains in the app only for lightweight metadata lookups such as version display.

docs.title: macOS Editing Model
docs.text:
The macOS app keeps per-photo edits in queue item state rather than one shared editor state.

  • Crop, rotation, flip, fit mode, and film orientation are stored per queue item
  • Overlays are first-class data: text, QR code, timestamp, imported image, and location
  • Preview and print use the same overlay composition pipeline so edited output matches what the user sees
  • New-photo defaults seed future imports without mutating existing queue items

docs.title: No Daemon
docs.text: InstantLink does not need a background daemon. Printing is a short-lived connect-transfer-print-disconnect workflow, and the macOS app talks to the printer directly through the bundled FFI dylib for runtime operations.

docs.title: Bridge Firmware Release Pipeline
docs.text: InstantLink Bridge firmware is packaged as a versioned update bundle for Raspberry Pi OS arm64. The bundle is designed to be published by GitHub Actions, embedded in the macOS app, and installed by the future Bridge control panel after management auth, preflight, backup, and rollback are wired.

docs.title: Version Tags
docs.text:
• App releases use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and build a same-version Bridge firmware bundle into InstantLink.app/Contents/Resources/BridgeFirmware.
  • Bridge-only releases use bridge-vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and publish only the Bridge firmware assets.
  • Workflow dispatch also accepts 0.1.0, v0.1.0, or bridge-v0.1.0; the package normalizes all three to Bridge version 0.1.0.

docs.title: Bundle Contents
docs.text:
bridge/scripts/build-firmware-bundle.sh <version> creates:

target/bridge-firmware/dist/
|-- InstantLinkBridgeFirmware-vX.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.tar.gz
|-- InstantLinkBridgeFirmware-vX.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.tar.gz.sha256
|-- InstantLinkBridgeFirmware-vX.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.manifest.json
|-- InstantLinkBridgeFirmware-vX.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.manifest.sig   # signed builds only
|-- latest.json
`-- latest.json.sig                                                # signed builds only

Inside the tarball:

bridge/                         # Python runtime, configs, systemd, udev, scripts, docs
native/bin/instantlink           # Linux arm64 InstantLink CLI
native/lib/libinstantlink_ffi.so # Linux arm64 FFI backend
native/instantlink-artifacts-manifest.json
install-firmware-bundle.sh       # Pi-side installer
manifest.json                    # Package manifest
SHA256SUMS                       # In-bundle file checksums

The macOS app build copies the staged BridgeFirmware directory into app resources. App code can read latest.json through BridgeFirmwareBundleService, which requires latest.json.sig, the package .manifest.sig, and matching SHA-256 values before returning a bundled package.

Signed release builds add Ed25519 JSON signature sidecars for the package manifest and latest.json. The signature payload is deterministic canonical JSON, not the tarball bytes or shell scripts. The future macOS updater and Bridge manager must verify these signatures against embedded trusted public keys before upload or install.

Package manifests and release indexes are intentionally separate signed document types:

  • Package manifests carry manifest_kind = "instantlink_bridge_firmware_package_manifest" and use signature_kind = "instantlink_bridge_firmware_manifest_signature".
  • Release indexes carry manifest_kind = "instantlink_bridge_firmware_release_index" and use signature_kind = "instantlink_bridge_firmware_release_index_signature".

This prevents latest.json from being accepted where an installable package manifest is required.

docs.title: CI Workflows
docs.text:
• .github/workflows/bridge-firmware.yml runs on bridge-v* tags and manual dispatch. It builds Linux arm64 native artifacts with cargo zigbuild, creates the firmware bundle, uploads it as a workflow artifact, and publishes it on the tag release.
  • .github/workflows/release.yml runs on app v* tags. It builds the same-version Bridge firmware bundle before scripts/build-app.sh, embeds it in the app resources, and uploads the firmware assets beside the DMG, CLI zip, and FFI zip.

docs.title: Local Build
docs.text:
Install zig, cargo-zigbuild, CMake and a C compiler, then run. The prepared-JPEG validator builds and statically links its bundled libjpeg-turbo; the Pi does not need a new shared library. NASM enables SIMD when building for x86; arm64 uses the compiler's NEON support.

cargo install cargo-zigbuild --locked
bridge/scripts/build-firmware-bundle.sh 0.1.0

Local builds are unsigned by default. To produce signed release assets, provide an Ed25519 private key path through the environment:

INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_SIGNING_KEY=/secure/path/bridge-firmware-ed25519.pem \
INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_SIGNING_KEY_ID=bridge-release-2026-05 \
bridge/scripts/build-firmware-bundle.sh 0.1.0

INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_SIGNING_KEY_ID is optional; if omitted, the signer derives an ed25519-sha256:<digest> key id from the public key. Encrypted PEM keys can be used by setting INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD_ENV to the name of an environment variable that contains the password. The private key must live outside the repository and should be injected only by protected release CI.

Tagged Bridge firmware and app releases require the BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_SIGNING_KEY_PEM secret. BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_SIGNING_KEY_ID is optional but recommended so release assets carry a stable key identifier. Workflow-dispatch development builds may remain unsigned; app-side bundle discovery is fail-closed and ignores unsigned bundles.

Bridge-side verification builds its trusted firmware key store from embedded product keys, optional [firmware].trusted_public_keys config entries, and the test/development-only INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEYS JSON environment override. Product install paths must use that trust store and must not rely only on a public key supplied by the caller.

For test keys only:

bridge/scripts/sign-firmware-manifest.py generate-test-key \
  --private-key /tmp/bridge-firmware-test.pem \
  --public-key /tmp/bridge-firmware-test.pub.pem

To reuse already-built Linux arm64 artifacts:

INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_BUILD_NATIVE=0 \
INSTANTLINK_BRIDGE_INSTANTLINK_ARTIFACT_DIR=target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/release \
bridge/scripts/build-firmware-bundle.sh 0.1.0

docs.title: Installation Contract
docs.text:
The package still contains install-firmware-bundle.sh for manual developer recovery installs. The product updater must not run that root shell script. The Bridge manager should install from declarative package metadata into release slots, with backup and rollback controlled by the manager.

The future app updater should:

  1. Verify latest.json.sig as a release-index signature against the trusted firmware key store.
  2. Verify the package manifest .manifest.sig as a package-manifest signature against the same trust store.
  3. Reject release indexes presented as package manifests.
  4. Reject unknown key ids, invalid signatures, malformed SHA-256 digests, or artifact names that are not clean relative paths/basenames.
  5. Verify the package manifest, archive, and checksum sidecar SHA-256 values from latest.json.
  6. Confirm target linux-aarch64, required Bridge API compatibility, clean provenance, and the downgrade policy hook before install.
  7. Confirm the live Bridge manager reports auth, backup, release_slots, rollback, and health_gates capabilities.
  8. Upload and extract the bundle into a staging directory on the Bridge.
  9. Ask the Bridge manager to create a backup, install into a new release slot, restart, and verify.
  10. Mark the update good only after service, FTP, LCD, network, and printer-status checks pass.

This is not yet a complete product updater. One-click updates must remain hidden until the Bridge management API, local authorization, signed package trust chain, automatic backup, and rollback gate from docs/plans/029-bridge-control-panel.md and docs/plans/030-bridge-secure-management-updates.md are implemented.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
Rust builds require CMake and a C compiler for the bundled JPEG validator. Install NASM for x86 SIMD support. On macOS use brew install cmake nasm; on Debian/Ubuntu use sudo apt-get install build-essential cmake nasm. The JPEG library is statically linked.

git clone https://github.com/wu-hongjun/InstantLink.git
cd InstantLink
cargo build --workspace
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Before Every Commit
docs.text:
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
bash scripts/test-macos.sh
python3 scripts/check-localizations.py

Clippy warnings are treated as errors in CI.

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
Use Conventional Commits:

  • feat: new behavior or user-facing capability
  • fix: bug fix
  • refactor: structural cleanup without intended behavior change
  • docs: documentation-only change
  • test: test-only change
  • chore: tooling, CI, or build-system change

docs.title: Build and Release Notes
docs.text:
• Use bash scripts/build-app.sh <semver> to build target/release/InstantLink.app
  • The script requires a semver argument such as 0.1.5 or v0.1.5
  • GitHub Releases are tag-driven via .github/workflows/release.yml
  • Tagged releases publish the macOS DMG plus separate CLI and FFI zip archives

docs.title: Code Standards
docs.text:
• Rust uses snake_case for functions/variables, PascalCase for types, and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants
  • Prefer thiserror-based PrinterError in the core crate
  • Use anyhow with .context(...) in the CLI for user-facing command failures
  • Keep protocol and model knowledge in instantlink-core; avoid duplicating it in CLI or Swift

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
InstantLink/
├── crates/
│   ├── instantlink-core/   # BLE protocol, device logic, image processing
│   ├── instantlink-cli/    # CLI binary
│   └── instantlink-ffi/    # C ABI wrapper for native apps
├── macos/InstantLink/
│   ├── App/                # SwiftUI app entry, app delegate, relaunch helpers
│   ├── Core/               # ViewModel, queue state, print pipeline
│   ├── Features/           # Camera, main window, editor, settings UI
│   ├── Support/            # Shared preview, overlay, and panel components
│   ├── InstantLinkFFI.swift
│   ├── Localization.swift
│   └── OverlayModels.swift
├── docs/                   # MkDocs documentation
├── scripts/build-app.sh    # App bundle + DMG build script
└── .github/workflows/      # CI and release automation

docs.title: Fast Tests
docs.text:
cargo test --workspace
bash scripts/test-macos.sh

This covers protocol encoding/decoding, image preparation, mock transport flows, device-level behavior, and the repo-native macOS unit harness for core Swift logic without real hardware.

CI also enforces:

  • bash scripts/test-macos.sh
  • python3 scripts/check-localizations.py
  • a Rust line-coverage gate via cargo llvm-cov

docs.title: Hardware Verification
docs.text:
Prefer running the local CLI from the repo rather than relying on a separately installed binary:

cargo run -p instantlink-cli -- scan
cargo run -p instantlink-cli -- info
cargo run -p instantlink-cli -- status
cargo run -p instantlink-cli -- print test.jpg

Use a real printer for BLE discovery, status, print, and LED checks.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Docs are built with MkDocs Material:

pip install mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve
mkdocs build

Update docs alongside behavior changes. Reference docs should describe the live codebase, not historical implementation details.

docs.title: Local validation & CI policy
docs.text: InstantLink runs validation locally via a Git pre-commit hook. GitHub CI is reserved for release tagging — it does not run on every push or pull request.

docs.title: CI policy
docs.text:
Workflow Trigger ci.yml (Audit, Check, Bridge, Linux, Rust Coverage) release tags v* / bridge-v*, or manual workflow_dispatch release.yml tags v* bridge-firmware.yml tags bridge-v*, or manual docs.yml push to main touching docs/** or mkdocs.yml (docs site stays current)

So the full CI suite acts as a release gate; everyday correctness is enforced on your machine before each commit.

docs.title: Pre-commit hook
docs.text:
The hook lives at scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit (tracked, so it is shared) and is activated per-machine by pointing Git at it:

git config core.hooksPath scripts/git-hooks

It is path-scoped — each suite runs only when its area has staged changes:

Staged path Checks crates/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace crates/instantlink-ffi/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock scripts/check-ffi-header.sh bridge/ ruff check src tests, mypy src, pytest -q macos/ scripts/test-macos.sh (swiftc build + tests) any *.sh bash -n syntax check bridge/scripts/*.py python -m py_compile always git diff --check (whitespace / conflict markers)

docs.title: Bypassing
docs.text:
For a work-in-progress commit you can skip the hook:

SKIP_HOOK=1 git commit ...     # or
git commit --no-verify

Use sparingly — the next release tag will run the full CI suite regardless.

Note: the hook calls python, cargo, and swiftc from your shell PATH. Run commits from a terminal where your toolchains (pyenv/venv, rustup, Xcode CLT) are available.

docs.title: Reverse Engineering the Instax Link BLE Protocol
docs.text:
Scope

This guide mixes protocol research background with implementation notes. The current InstantLink codebase only implements BLE GATT transport in production. RFCOMM/SPP and USB notes below are reverse-engineering context, not supported runtime transports.

This guide documents how the Instax Link protocol was reverse-engineered by the open-source community, and provides a methodology for adding support for future devices.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: The Instax Link printers (Mini Link, Mini Link 2, Mini Link 3, Square Link, Wide Link) use a proprietary BLE GATT protocol that replaces the WiFi-based protocol of older SP-1/SP-2/SP-3 models. The protocol was reverse-engineered collaboratively via jpwsutton/instax_api#21, with working implementations in javl/InstaxBLE (Python) and this project (Rust).

docs.title: Step 1: Capture BLE Traffic
docs.text:
Android (preferred for packet capture):

  1. Enable Bluetooth HCI snoop log in Developer Options
  2. Open the official Instax app and perform the action you want to capture (print, LED control, etc.)
  3. Disable the snoop log
  4. Pull the log file: 
    adb pull /data/misc/bluetooth/logs/btsnoop_hci.log

macOS (PacketLogger):

Apple's PacketLogger (from Additional Tools for Xcode) can capture BLE traffic directly.

docs.title: Step 2: Analyze in Wireshark
docs.text:
1. Open the .log file in Wireshark
  2. Filter with btspp (for RFCOMM/SPP traffic) or btatt (for BLE GATT)
  3. Look for writes to the Write Characteristic (70954783-...) and notifications from the Notify Characteristic (70954784-...)

docs.title: Step 3: Identify Packet Structure
docs.text:
All Instax Link packets follow this format:

[Header:2B] [Length:2B] [Opcode:2B] [Payload:variable] [Checksum:1B]
  • Client→Printer header: 0x41 0x62 (ASCII "Ab")
  • Printer→Client header: 0x61 0x42 (ASCII "aB")
  • Length: Big-endian u16, total packet size
  • Checksum: (255 - (sum_of_all_preceding_bytes & 255)) & 255
  • Validation: sum(entire_packet_including_checksum) & 255 == 255

docs.title: Step 4: Decode Opcodes
docs.text:
The opcode's first byte is the command group, second byte is the command within group:

Group Purpose Examples 0x00 Device info & capabilities Version info, device queries 0x01 Power & connection control Shutdown, reset, sleep, BLE connect 0x02 Support function queries Battery, film, print count 0x10 Image transfer Download start/data/end, print 0x20 Firmware update FW download, upgrade, backup 0x30 Hardware settings Accelerometer, LEDs, printer head 0x80 Camera settings Live view, post-view upload

docs.title: Step 5: Decode Response Format
docs.text:
Responses include a return code byte after the opcode: - 0x00 = success - Non-zero = error/rejection

For multiplexed queries (opcode 0x0002), the response also includes the InfoType byte so you can match responses to requests.

docs.title: Step 6: Android App Decompilation
docs.text:
The official Instax app can be decompiled with jadx or apktool to discover: - Event type enumerations (all 64+ command/event types) - Payload field definitions - Image encoding parameters - Protocol state machines

Key findings from app decompilation:

SUPPORT_FUNCTION_AND_VERSION_INFO(0, 0)
DEVICE_INFO_SERVICE(0, 1)
SUPPORT_FUNCTION_INFO(0, 2)
IDENTIFY_INFORMATION(0, 16)
SHUT_DOWN(1, 0)
RESET(1, 1)
AUTO_SLEEP_SETTINGS(1, 2)
BLE_CONNECT(1, 3)
PRINT_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD_START(16, 0)
PRINT_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD_DATA(16, 1)
PRINT_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD_END(16, 2)
PRINT_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD_CANCEL(16, 3)
PRINT_IMAGE(16, 128)           // 0x1080
REJECT_FILM_COVER(16, 129)     // 0x1081
FW_DOWNLOAD_START(32, 0)       // 0x2000
FW_DOWNLOAD_DATA(32, 1)
FW_DOWNLOAD_END(32, 2)
FW_UPGRADE_EXIT(32, 3)
FW_PROGRAM_INFO(32, 16)
FW_DATA_BACKUP(32, 17)
FW_UPDATE_REQUEST(32, 18)
XYZ_AXIS_INFO(48, 0)           // 0x3000
LED_PATTERN_SETTINGS(48, 1)    // 0x3001
AXIS_ACTION_SETTINGS(48, 2)
POWER_ONOFF_LED_SETTING(48, 3)
AR_LED_VIBRATION_SETTING(48, 4)
ADDITIONAL_PRINTER_INFO(48, 16) // 0x3010
PRINTER_HEAD_LIGHT_CORRECT_INFO(48, 17)
PRINTER_HEAD_LIGHT_CORRECT_SETTINGS(48, 18)

docs.title: Transport Variants
docs.text:
The same packet protocol works over three transport layers:

Transport Platform Notes BLE GATT iOS, macOS, Linux Primary. Uses custom service UUID 70954782-.... MTU=182, packets fragmented into sub-packets. RFCOMM/SPP Android Classic Bluetooth serial. Same packet format, no MTU fragmentation needed (MTU ~990). USB CDC ACM Any (via USB cable) Printer appears as /dev/ttyACM0. Vendor 04cb, Product 5019. Same packet format.

docs.title: BLE Device Discovery
docs.text:
The printer advertises two BLE names: - INSTAX-{serial}(IOS) — connect to this one (BLE GATT) - INSTAX-{serial}(ANDROID) — RFCOMM/SPP endpoint

Manufacturer data key: 0x04d8, value: 01 00.

docs.title: Device Info Queries (Opcode 0x0001)
docs.text:
The DEVICE_INFO_SERVICE command uses a sub-index byte in the payload to select which field to query:

Sub-index Field Example Response 0x00 Manufacturer FUJIFILM (ASCII, length-prefixed) 0x01 Model SP-4 (internal model name for Mini Link) 0x02 Serial Number 10458647 (ASCII) 0x03 Unknown version 0000 0x04 Hardware version 0102 0x05 Firmware version 1.00

Response format: [return_code:1B] [sub_index:1B] [string_length:1B] [ASCII data...]

Internal model names: - Mini Link = SP-4 - Mini Link 2 = likely SP-5 (unconfirmed) - Square Link = unknown - Wide Link = unknown

docs.title: LED Animation Protocol
docs.text:
The LED system supports multi-frame animations (not just static colors):

Payload: [when:1B] [frame_count:1B] [speed:1B] [repeat:1B] [B,G,R:3B per frame...]
Field Values when 0=immediate, 1=on print start, 2=on print complete, 3=pattern switch frame_count Number of color frames in animation speed Frame duration (higher = slower) repeat 0=play once, 1-254=repeat N times, 255=loop forever Colors BGR format (blue, green, red — not RGB) per frame

Hardware-verified (Instax Square Link, March 2026): - BGR byte ordering confirmed — sending [B=0, G=0, R=255] produces red light, [B=255, G=0, R=0] produces blue light. - repeat=0xFF required for static colors — repeat=0 causes the color to flash once and revert to white. - speed=1 works for static colors (speed=0 caused the color to not display correctly). - For a simple static red: [when=0, count=1, speed=1, repeat=255, B=0, G=0, R=255]

docs.title: Accelerometer Data (Opcode 0x3000)
docs.text:
Returns orientation data as a packed struct:

Format: <hhhB (little-endian)
  x: i16 — X axis acceleration
  y: i16 — Y axis acceleration
  z: i16 — Z axis acceleration
  orientation: u8 — derived orientation value

The official Nintendo app continuously logs accelerometer values (discovered via adb logcat "InstaxApplication:D *:S"), suggesting this was used for motion-based features.

docs.title: Image Encoding
docs.text: Key observations from the community: - Images are always JPEG (not raw pixels) - Variable block counts per image (depends on JPEG file size, not pixel count) - This explains why 69 blocks x 900 bytes = 62,100 bytes, not 600x800x3 = 1,440,000 bytes - Maximum JPEG size is model-specific in InstantLink: Mini 105 KB, Mini Link 3 55 KB, Square 105 KB, Wide 225 KB - Last chunk is zero-padded to full chunk size - Quality should be optimized via binary search to stay under the size limit

docs.title: Confirmed on hardware (Instax Square Link):
docs.text:
• BGR LED byte ordering (not RGB)
  • LED repeat=255 required for persistent static colors
  • LED speed=1 works for static; speed=0 does not display correctly
  • Print flow: DOWNLOAD_START → DATA chunks (ACK per chunk) → DOWNLOAD_END → PRINT_IMAGE
  • Accelerometer opcode exists but not yet tested on hardware

docs.title: Not yet reverse-engineered:
docs.text:
1. Firmware update flow — Opcodes 0x2000-0x2012 exist but payload formats are unknown
  2. Camera settings (0x80xx) — For models with camera features
  3. REJECT_FILM_COVER (0x1081) — Purpose unclear, possibly for cartridge door detection
  4. AXIS_ACTION_SETTINGS (0x3002) — May configure motion-triggered actions
  5. POWER_ONOFF_LED_SETTING (0x3003) — Startup/shutdown LED behavior
  6. AR_LED_VIBRATION_SETTING (0x3004) — AR-related haptic/LED feedback
  7. PRINTER_HEAD_LIGHT_CORRECT (0x3011/0x3012) — Print head calibration
  8. IDENTIFY_INFORMATION (0x0010) — Unknown identification data
  9. BLE_CONNECT (0x0103) — BLE-specific connection reservation command

docs.title: Adding support for new models:
docs.text:
1. Capture BLE traffic with the official app
  2. Query Image Support Info — response dimensions identify Mini, Square, and Wide
  3. For Mini Link 3, require exact ASCII-trimmed DIS FI033 alongside 600x800 dimensions. Exact FI017 requires 800x800 Square dimensions. Reject conflicts and ambiguous FI033 strings; other unknown hints fall back to dimensions.
  4. Test with known chunk sizes (900B for mini/wide, 1808B for square)
  5. If a new model uses different chunk sizes, the DOWNLOAD_START response may contain the requested block size
  6. Verify JPEG quality limits — they may differ by model

The native BLE startup path can resend Image Support Info once after a one-second ACK wait, within the original ten-second deadline. This is a serialized read-only retry; it does not replay failed image or print commands. A failed capability query retires the link.

docs.title: Community References
docs.text:
• jpwsutton/instax_api — Original WiFi protocol RE (SP-1/2/3)
  • jpwsutton/instax_api#21 — BLE protocol RE thread (this document's primary source)
  • javl/InstaxBLE — Python BLE implementation (Mini, Square, Wide)
  • linssenste/instax-link-web — Web Bluetooth implementation

docs.title: From Releases
docs.text:
Prebuilt artifacts are published on the Releases page for each tagged version:

  • InstantLink-vX.Y.Z-aarch64-apple-darwin.dmg for the macOS app
  • InstantLink-CLI-vX.Y.Z.zip for the standalone CLI
  • InstantLink-FFI-vX.Y.Z.zip for FFI consumers

The app release targets macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon. Download the .dmg, mount it, and drag InstantLink.app into /Applications.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Rust stable with edition 2024
  • macOS 15+ for the SwiftUI app and BLE via CoreBluetooth
  • Linux is supported for CLI development and BLE via BlueZ

docs.title: Build the Workspace
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/wu-hongjun/InstantLink.git
cd InstantLink
cargo build --workspace --release

The CLI binary will be at target/release/instantlink.

docs.title: Install the CLI
docs.text:
cargo install --path crates/instantlink-cli

Or copy the release binary manually:

cp target/release/instantlink /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: Build the macOS App
docs.text:
The app bundle embeds the CLI binary and the FFI dylib. Runtime printer/device operations use the bundled FFI dylib; the bundled CLI is kept only for lightweight metadata such as version reporting.

bash scripts/build-app.sh 0.1.5

scripts/build-app.sh requires a semver version argument. It builds the Rust workspace, compiles the SwiftUI launcher, bundles localizations and fonts, codesigns the app, and creates a .dmg when create-dmg is installed (brew install create-dmg).

The resulting bundle is written to target/release/InstantLink.app.

docs.title: Build the FFI Header
docs.text:
The checked-in header at crates/instantlink-ffi/include/instantlink.h is only refreshed when INSTANTLINK_UPDATE_HEADER is set:

INSTANTLINK_UPDATE_HEADER=1 cargo build --release -p instantlink-ffi

Without that environment variable, cbindgen writes the generated header into Cargo's OUT_DIR. Use bash scripts/check-ffi-header.sh --release before release work to regenerate the header and fail if it differs from the checked-in ABI.

Bluetooth Permissions

InstantLink.app includes NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription. When running the CLI directly outside the app bundle, macOS will prompt for Bluetooth permission on first use.

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
instantlink --version
instantlink scan

docs.title: 1. Scan for Printers
docs.text:
Turn on your Instax Link printer and scan:

instantlink scan

Expected output:

Found 1 printer(s):
  INSTAX-12345678

docs.title: 2. Check Printer Status
docs.text:
instantlink status

Connected:  yes
Printer:    INSTAX-12345678
Model:      Instax Mini Link
Battery:    85%
Film:       8 remaining
Prints:     42

docs.title: 3. Print an Image
docs.text:
instantlink print photo.jpg

The image is automatically resized to your printer model. Use --fit to control the result:

# Crop to fill (default) — may cut edges
instantlink print photo.jpg --fit crop

# Contain within bounds — adds white bars
instantlink print photo.jpg --fit contain

# Stretch to exact dimensions
instantlink print photo.jpg --fit stretch

docs.title: Color Mode
docs.text:
# Rich mode (default) — vivid colors
instantlink print photo.jpg --color-mode rich

# Natural mode — classic film look
instantlink print photo.jpg --color-mode natural

docs.title: JPEG Quality
docs.text:
instantlink print photo.jpg --quality 90

If the encoded JPEG exceeds the connected model's size limit, InstantLink automatically lowers quality until it fits. Current caps are Mini 105KB, Mini Link 3 55KB, Square 105KB, and Wide 225KB.

docs.title: 4. LED Control
docs.text:
# Set LED to a color
instantlink led set "#FF6600" --pattern breathe

# Turn LED off
instantlink led off

docs.title: 5. JSON Output
docs.text:
--json is currently supported on scan, info, and status:

instantlink status --json

{
  "connected": true,
  "name": "INSTAX-12345678",
  "model": "Instax Mini Link",
  "battery": 85,
  "is_charging": false,
  "film_remaining": 8,
  "print_count": 42
}

docs.title: Multiple Printers
docs.text:
Target a specific printer by name:

instantlink print photo.jpg --device "INSTAX-12345678"

docs.title: Plan 001: Full-Stack Scaffold
docs.text:
Status: Completed

Historical implementation plan from the initial scaffold. Current source-of-truth behavior lives in the reference and development docs, which reflect later additions such as Rust 2024, Mini Link 3 support, the expanded FFI surface, and the macOS overlay editor.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Scaffold the entire InstantLink project from scratch: workspace, all crates, stub modules, full implementations, and macOS app. Verify compilation, clippy, formatting, and tests.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: InstantLink is a Rust CLI and native macOS app for printing to Fujifilm Instax Link printers via BLE. The architecture mirrors StatusLight, adapted from USB HID to BLE and from sync to async.

docs.title: Phase 1: Scaffold (Completed)
docs.text:
Created workspace root, all Cargo.toml files, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, and directory structure.

Files created:

  • Cargo.toml — Workspace with 3 crates, workspace dependencies, release profile
  • CLAUDE.md — Dev instructions, protocol reference, model specs
  • .gitignore — Rust, macOS, IDE, references patterns

docs.title: Phase 2: Protocol + Commands (Completed)
docs.text:
Implemented the BLE packet protocol and all command opcodes.

protocol.rs:

  • Packet header [0x41 0x62], big-endian length, checksum
  • build_packet() and parse_packet() with full validation
  • fragment() for MTU-sized sub-packets (182 bytes)
  • PacketAssembler for reassembling fragmented notifications
  • 14 unit tests

commands.rs:

  • 14 opcode constants (device info, battery, image transfer, LED, etc.)
  • Command enum (12 variants) with encode() to protocol packets
  • Response enum (10 variants) with decode() from parsed packets
  • 14 unit tests including encode-decode roundtrips

docs.title: Phase 3: Image Processing (Completed)
docs.text:
image.rs:

  • FitMode enum: Crop, Contain (white bars), Stretch
  • load_image() from file path, load_image_from_bytes() from raw data
  • resize_image() with model-aware dimensions using Lanczos3 filter
  • encode_jpeg() with automatic quality reduction to fit the target printer's size limit
  • chunk_image_data() using model-specific chunk sizes
  • prepare_image() pipeline: load → resize → encode → chunk
  • 10 unit tests

docs.title: Phase 4: Models + Transport + Device (Completed)
docs.text:
models.rs:

  • PrinterModel enum with model specs (dimensions, chunk size, name, image-size limits)

transport.rs:

  • Transport trait (async: send, receive, disconnect)
  • BLE service/characteristic UUIDs
  • get_adapter(), scan() using btleplug with service UUID filter
  • BleTransport with notification channel and PacketAssembler

device.rs:

  • PrinterDevice trait (async: status, battery, film, print, LED)
  • BlePrinterDevice with model auto-detection via IMAGE_SUPPORT_INFO
  • ACK-based print flow: DOWNLOAD_START → DATA chunks → DOWNLOAD_END → PRINT_IMAGE
  • Progress callback support

docs.title: Phase 5: High-Level API + CLI (Completed)
docs.text:
printer.rs:

  • scan(), connect(), connect_any(), print_file(), get_status()

CLI (main.rs + output.rs):

  • Commands: scan, info, print, led set/off, status
  • Global --device flag and JSON output where supported by the CLI
  • Progress bars via indicatif
  • JSON output for all commands

docs.title: Phase 6: FFI + macOS App (Completed)
docs.text:
FFI (lib.rs):

  • Global tokio runtime via OnceLock
  • Mutex-protected device handle
  • Functions: init, connect, disconnect, battery, film_remaining, print, set_led, led_off, is_connected
  • catch_unwind on all FFI boundaries
  • cbindgen auto-generates instantlink.h

macOS App:

  • InstantLinkCLI.swift — Initial Process wrapper with 15s watchdog, scan/info/print/LED/status; removed in March 2026 once the macOS runtime became FFI-only
  • InstantLinkApp.swift — SwiftUI with menu bar extra, full window, drag-and-drop print zone
  • build-app.sh — Builds CLI + copies into app bundle

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Check Result cargo build --workspace Pass cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings Pass (0 warnings) cargo fmt --all Pass cargo test --workspace Passed at scaffold completion; current totals have since grown

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text:
1. Async-first: btleplug requires tokio, so core is fully async
  2. No daemon: One-shot printing doesn't need a persistent service
  3. Process wrapper over FFI: the initial plan followed the StatusLight process-wrapper pattern; the shipped macOS app now uses the FFI dylib directly for printer control
  4. Model auto-detection: Query IMAGE_SUPPORT_INFO after connect, match dimensions
  5. ACK-per-chunk: Wait for printer ACK after each data chunk (reliable transfer)

docs.title: Plan 002: CI/CD Setup
docs.text: Status: Completed

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Set up GitHub Actions for continuous integration, documentation deployment, and tagged releases.

docs.title: CI (ci.yml)
docs.text:
Runs on every push to main and on pull requests.

Steps:

  1. Format check (cargo fmt --all --check)
  2. Clippy lint (cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings)
  3. Unit tests (cargo test --workspace)
  4. Build (cargo build --workspace)

Runner: macos-latest — required because btleplug depends on CoreBluetooth on macOS. Unlike StatusLight which uses ubuntu-latest (hidapi has Linux support), InstantLink needs macOS for BLE compilation.

docs.title: Docs (docs.yml)
docs.text:
Deploys MkDocs Material documentation to GitHub Pages.

Triggers:

  • Push to main when docs/** or mkdocs.yml changes
  • Manual dispatch via workflow_dispatch

Steps:

  1. Checkout with full history
  2. Install Python + mkdocs-material
  3. Deploy to gh-pages branch

Setup required: Enable GitHub Pages in repo settings, set source to gh-pages branch.

docs.title: Release (release.yml)
docs.text:
Creates GitHub Releases with pre-built binaries when a version tag is pushed.

Trigger: Push tags matching v* (e.g., v0.1.0)

Artifacts:

  • InstantLink-CLI-vX.Y.Z.zip — CLI binary
  • InstantLink-FFI-vX.Y.Z.zip — Static/dynamic library + C header

Usage:

git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text:
1. macOS runner for CI: btleplug requires CoreBluetooth, so we can't use ubuntu-latest
  2. No Linux CI: The primary target is macOS; Linux BLE (BlueZ) support is secondary
  3. Separate CLI and FFI packages: Different consumers need different artifacts
