The LCD reported Setup needed / Next action Bridge Wi-Fi off. USB SSH was available, NetworkManager and the Bridge were active, and the Wi-Fi radio was enabled. However, no wlan0 interface existed. Kernel boot logs recorded a corrupted SDIO RAM image, failed NVRAM download and an MMC inhibit timeout before the Bridge's runtime power tiers began. vcgencmd get_throttled returned 0x0; this provides no evidence of a downclock or undervoltage cause.

Reloading brcmfmac restored wlan0. Activating the existing hotspot with the root Wi-Fi helper restored 192.168.8.1/24, using the saved SSID/PIN. The Bridge did not restart. The old runtime applied Wi-Fi mode once at startup and never retried a failed activation; the hotspot profile intentionally has autoconnect disabled to keep FTP modes deterministic.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
• The existing root Wi-Fi helper enables the radio, then checks for wlan0. On a Raspberry Pi with no interface, it reloads the fixed brcmfmac module and waits up to ten seconds. Healthy interfaces are never reloaded. Existing constrained sudo permissions suffice.
  • The shared controller schedules one detached recovery task for configured Hotspot mode. Startup/healthy grace is 30 seconds; failed attempts back off for 30, 60, 120 and then 300 seconds. The task checks actual radio intent, serializes with explicit mode operations, checks persisted App network intent after its radio probe, and rechecks readiness after the helper returns. Missing expected IP never becomes ready just because the helper exits successfully.
  • Active photo processing, printing, queued images and recent FTP traffic defer attempts. Stop and mode changes cancel recovery. Wired, Auto and Peer modes do not cause retries; an explicitly disabled radio stays disabled during background recovery.
  • Physical and virtual LCD status share Bridge Wi-Fi unavailable wording, translated in English and Chinese. A missing address is not evidence that the radio was turned off. Setup readiness remains honest until the expected address returns.
  • Cancellation terminates the root helper's active command and bounds Python output draining and reaping, so an inherited output pipe cannot freeze a mode switch or shutdown.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Clean implementation commit cad66aa passed the normal pre-commit gate: 1,282 Bridge tests, Ruff and strict mypy (65 source files). Touched-file Ruff formatting, shell syntax, whitespace and strict MkDocs also passed. An independent review confirmed the persisted-intent and cancellation fixes. No App/iOS schema or API contract changed.

Shell recovery tests exercise healthy-interface preservation, recovery with/without a loaded driver, refusal on other hardware, a bounded failed recovery and real child termination. Controller tests cover grace/backoff, asynchronous scheduling, state guards, explicit mode changes and shutdown. Renderer tests preserve setup-needed behavior and translated copy. Hardware deployment and automatic fault recovery await restoration of USB access; cad66aa is not yet deployed. The manual recovery above succeeded on Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / Debian 13.2 / kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, with Waveshare ST7789 LCD HAT and X306 2300 mAh battery. Saved Instax Square was connected (film 6, battery 95%). No film was consumed. Camera reconnection and a new 16-hour discharge test are not established here.

docs.title: 065 — Simplify the one-photo print flow
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-11. Scope: Bridge print screens and copy; locked Wi-Fi recovery validation.

docs.title: User request
docs.text: Deploy the pending Wi-Fi recovery fix and verify it while locked with the Printer connected. Reduce the number of screens and verbose text shown when printing one photo.

docs.title: Screen audit and implementation
docs.text:
The old path displayed receipt, a preparation placeholder, a timer-free Preview frame, review, Starting/Checking/Finding Printer, transport stages, standalone completion and Home. Some states lasted only until the next coroutine completed, producing flashes without a useful decision.

Path New visible flow Timed review One Review card: Preparing → photo plus countdown → one Printing layout → Home with Printed notice Manual review Same Review card; editing stops the countdown and KEY1 confirms Immediate printing One Printing layout → Home with Printed notice Cancel Return to cached Home; cancel preparation safely No film Keep reload guidance and allow navigation; normal polling detects reloaded film Failure Preserve the error and Check action; never resend automatically Slow/stalled job Keep Still printing / Print stalled and restart feedback Sync Spool and Sync Home retain their existing behavior; no print screens
  • Receipt records photo identity and activity without a separate screen or timer.
  • Preparation stays inside the fixed photo card. The first ready frame includes its actual countdown; no timer-free preview flash precedes it. Editing retains manual confirmation.
  • Printing keeps a fixed headline and one short stage: Connecting, Preparing, Sending or Finishing. One progress bar/percentage and the filename provide useful feedback. Remove duplicated progress, packet/KB details, Printer model, repeated key hints and generic warnings.
  • Completion uses Home's existing card with Printed feedback, including a successful last-sheet print. Its two-second expiry cannot replace Settings/Post opened by the user. No-film guidance likewise has no forced expiry that flashes a new Printer check.
  • English and Chinese use the same concise wording. Print admission, transport serialization, no-film checks, hard timeout, active-job boosts, lock and same-button unlock remain intact.

docs.title: Rendered evidence
docs.text: Synthetic local render using a neutral test image, not a physical LCD photograph. Connecting, Sending and Finishing above are progress updates within one layout.

docs.title: Validation and device status
docs.text:
Clean runtime cbffa65 is deployed. The normal pre-commit gates passed: 1,307 Bridge tests, Ruff and strict mypy (65 source files). Touched-file formatting, shell syntax, whitespace and strict MkDocs passed. Independent review found no remaining actionable defects. No App/iOS contract changed. The first full run found an old test expecting Print complete; its assertion was updated for the requested Printed copy and the entire suite passed.

Controller/app/preview/renderer tests cover initial frames, countdown timing, navigation during completion/no-film, concise stages, translated copy and last-sheet success. A locked-recovery regression covers a dark display, idle CPU tier and preserved Printer state.

docs.title: Device discoveries
docs.text:
USB initially did not enumerate; reconnecting restored en8/SSH. During deployment the camera logged into FTP without uploading a photo. Its past login exposed an overly conservative guard that deferred a missing hotspot for five minutes. Recovery now defers recent activity only on other transports; active photo preparation/printing/queues remain guarded. A failed hotspot cannot carry an ongoing Wi-Fi upload.

The first actual missing-interface trial could not unload brcmfmac: its brcmfmac_wcc vendor extension retained a module reference. The helper now removes that fixed Wi-Fi dependency first, only when wlan0 is absent. The next background retry repaired the existing fault without restarting the Bridge or Bluetooth. The Printer stopped advertising during the extended earlier trial; after the user turned it back on, the Bridge automatically reconnected. The accepted final trial below establishes continuity during recovery, not indefinite Printer uptime.

docs.title: Accepted hardware smoke
docs.text:
Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / Waveshare ST7789 240×240 LCD HAT / X306 2300 mAh; Debian 13, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17. Printer: Instax Square INSTAX-52006924, film 4. Camera profile remains Sony a7C II; no new photo upload was exercised.

A temporary observation wrapper ran the real Bridge application, injected its normal KEY2 abstract action after Printer readiness and recorded controller state. Physical GPIO input, framebuffer/backlight, CPU helper, NetworkManager and Rust FFI BLE were real. It used no test doubles. Faults were injected over USB SSH, leaving the runtime's own recovery responsible for restoring Wi-Fi.

Fault Restore time Samples Outcome Saved hotspot profile deactivated 32.90 s 60 Expected IP and FTP readiness restored SDIO function 1 unbound, wlan0 absent with driver loaded 31.99 s 59 Driver and hotspot restored automatically

Each trial observed another 31 seconds after restoration. Every sampled CPU frequency was 600 MHz with powersave; GPIO24 remained low and the controller stayed locked. BlueZ reported Connected at every sample, and fresh Printer status continued advancing at its 10-second cadence. The final driver trial additionally monitored selected-device D-Bus property changes and saw no connection-loss event. The Bridge PID was unchanged during both accepted trials; film stayed at 4. USB SSH remained usable. The temporary wrapper/drop-in and probe files were removed and the normal service restored afterward.

Recorded observations include the controller, CPU, backlight, interface and BlueZ measurements. The profile trial used controller 46f155f; the final driver trial included helper cbffa65. An initial SDIO function-2 test did not remove wlan0 and was rejected by the fault assertion; the accepted trial used function 1.

Normal service was restored at 21:43 EDT with Bridge, manager, Bluetooth and NetworkManager active, NRestarts=0, Printer connected (film 4/battery 65%), throttling 0x0 and hotspot FTP greeting/NOOP passing. Debian 13.2 and BlueZ 5.82 were rechecked.

No film was consumed. Physical switch actuation, colour output on film, a new camera upload and a 16-hour full-charge discharge remain outside this smoke's acceptance.

docs.title: 066 — Default to one-second print review
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-11. Scope: default review delay, shared Bridge/App management settings and deployment.

The user requested a shorter default instead of a five-second pause. New and missing configuration now use Review 1s. Bridge and App offer Confirm each, Print immediately, Review 1s and Review 5s. Explicit existing manual/immediate/five-second choices remain supported. The connected Bridge's previous five-second delay was changed to one second for this request.

The Python config/parser, orchestration fallback, example config, LCD label/options, manager validation and App model/draft/options/localizations must agree on the new value. Legacy positive non-option delays map to the new default; invalid booleans remain invalid. Manager validation accepts only 0/1/5/off. The countdown still begins after the prepared photo is visible, and edits require manual confirmation. No print transport, image pipeline, CPU tier or sync contract changes.

docs.title: Validation and deployment
docs.text:
Clean runtime 4574aa9 was deployed. 1,324 Bridge tests and 156 App tests passed, with Ruff, touched-file formatting, strict mypy (65 source files), whitespace and strict MkDocs. The new App label is present in all 12 locales; the global localization checker retains its pre-existing discrepancies. The initial full Bridge run found three old dispatch assertions expecting five seconds; these were updated to one second and the whole suite passed. The App portion of the pre-commit gate passed before that correction and was reused for the commit.

The live config was updated under ib, changing only the workflow delay from 5 to 1. Bridge and manager were restarted and are active with Bridge NRestarts=0. An on-Pi controller smoke loaded this saved config and supplied a synthetic prepared photo with NullDisplay/NullInput: the first review title was Print in 1s, workflow label Review 1s, and acceptance occurred 1.002 seconds after the photo frame. No Printer sender was used and no film was consumed. Hotspot remains at 192.168.8.1/24; throttling is 0x0.

Hardware/OS: Pi Zero 2 W / Waveshare ST7789 / X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17. This verifies the saved setting and controller timing; it is not a new physical-print benchmark. The App source/options were updated and tested; no App release was installed on this Mac.

docs.title: 067 — Bridge startup, Settings and resource audit
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-11. Scope: Bridge runtime, shared physical/virtual LCD and manager listeners.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Start UI and FTP independently of BlueZ. Gate Printer work on Bluetooth readiness, defer keepalive/FFI loading and optional Sync construction until core readiness, and track startup tasks through cancellation/failure. Health probing and metadata reads run off the UI loop.
  • Keep user navigation open during startup and status updates; exiting Settings uses current cached home. Help opened during startup resolves current readiness when dismissed.
  • Print Settings presents Post, Image fit, Confirmation and Printer, with Image quality and Printer options under Advanced. Ordinary helper paragraphs move to KEY3 Help. Read-only rows show their complete values in Help; long credentials wrap at all text sizes. About says Bridge version. Post still contains independent Looks and Correction; KEY3 opens Post.
  • Probe both interface addresses in one subprocess per health/discovery refresh. Bonjour address probing runs off the event loop and reuses a snapshot during late registration.
  • Cancel/timeout image preparation cleans up its isolated process group, including external HEIF decoders and descendants whose worker parent already exited. No image rules change.
  • Retry a missing manager address while serving the working listener; remove failed sites before retry. Preserve exact address binds, USB authentication and shutdown responsiveness.

Awake/preparing/printing CPU remains at the supported 1000 MHz maximum. Locked idle remains 600 MHz. Radios, recovery cadence, review default (1 second), APIs and native artifacts stay unchanged. Existing Printer idle auto-off cannot be prevented by status keepalive; the Bridge reconnects when it is powered on again. No film is used by this audit.

docs.title: Baseline and validation
docs.text:
Controlled reboot of deployed 4574aa9: kernel 2.635 s + userspace 14.313 s = 16.948 s systemd startup. Core ready 16.146 s, FTP 13.964 s, hotspot receive-ready 18.625 s, manager USB 19.131 s. The Printer was powered on later, so its baseline first status is excluded from boot comparisons. These are kernel-monotonic reboot timings, excluding firmware and power-button latency.

Local validation and post-deploy measurements are recorded below. The Settings contact sheet is at ../assets/bridge-audit-067/settings.png. This audit does not establish a 16-hour battery runtime; X306 has no host current or fuel gauge. A controlled discharge remains required. Physical button actuation, a new Sony upload and film colour/throughput remain separate hardware acceptance checks.

docs.title: Local validation
docs.text: 1,369 Bridge tests passed, including startup sequencing/failure/cancellation, late Help readiness, Settings navigation, read-only Help/credential wrapping, address refresh responsiveness, EXIF responsiveness and real process-group descendant cleanup. Ruff, touched-file formatting, strict mypy (65 source files), shell syntax, whitespace and strict MkDocs passed. Normal pre-commit gates passed for both runtime commits. No App/iOS/API/schema/FFI changes require cross-surface updates in this audit. Before/after Settings frames were visually inspected.

docs.title: Hardware observations
docs.text:
Clean runtime 50d2ec6 was deployed, followed by 8eb962d to cap missing manager listener retry at 10 seconds after a live trial exposed unnecessary latency with the initial 30-second cap. Source deployment preserved native artifacts and dependencies. Hardware/OS are Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / Waveshare ST7789 / X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17, saved Instax Square INSTAX-52006924 and Sony a7C II camera profile. No new camera upload or film print was performed.

First post-change reboot: UI frame 14.536 s, core readiness 14.551 s, FTP 14.204 s, Bluetooth agent 14.617 s, hotspot receive-ready 18.889 s and manager USB 19.435 s. Splash finished 9.864 s, before the first app frame. Systemd total was 17.178 s; this is not a material whole-system improvement over 16.948 s. Core readiness improved 1.594 s. Hotspot activation and Python startup remain practical constraints; the 7-second target is not met. Timings measure each subsystem separately and do not equate agent/core readiness with a connected Printer.

A live hotspot-loss trial restarted only the manager with the hotspot address absent. USB responded after its normal startup; the Bridge restored hotspot readiness about 33 s from fault injection. The manager rebound automatically without another restart, but its initial 30-second retry cap delayed HTTP availability to 54.00 s. This led to the 10-second cap. Bridge PID and post-restart manager PID were unchanged throughout recovery; screen-off idle was 600 MHz with GPIO24 low.

Comparable 35-second dark-idle samples (Printer absent, one offline scan, 600 MHz): Bridge process CPU 9.31% → 9.46% of one core, manager 0%, RSS 69,320 → 68,448 KiB. Board busy 7.30% → 3.40% varies with other activity and is not attributed to this change. There is no measured Bridge idle CPU reduction or battery-duration gain. Deterministic improvements are fewer network subprocesses, responsive UI and decoder cleanup. See the sanitized measurements at ../assets/bridge-audit-067/measurements.json.

Second reboot at final runtime 8eb962d: UI 14.324 s, core readiness 14.340 s, FTP 13.995 s, Bluetooth agent 14.403 s, hotspot receive-ready 18.685 s, manager USB 19.229 s, splash complete 9.808 s. Systemd total 16.924 s (2.614 s kernel + 14.310 s userspace). The two post-change core-readiness trials improved 1.59–1.81 seconds against the same hardware baseline. FTP, hotspot and total startup remain effectively unchanged. Neither post-change boot had a powered-on advertising Printer, so a boot-to-Printer measurement cannot be claimed; a fresh power-on was requested after its documented idle shutdown.

Final late-address trial with the 10-second cap: both manager endpoints returned HTTP 200 42.91 s after fault injection. Bridge PID and manager PID remained unchanged after the intentional manager restart; final CPU was 600 MHz and backlight GPIO24 low. Hotspot FTP 220 greeting and NOOP/200 passed. Bridge and manager were active with NRestarts=0, vcgencmd get_throttled was 0x0, and deployment metadata reported clean 8eb962d. Temporary probes lived in /tmp; no service wrapper, drop-in or configuration change remained. Printer connection continuity was not part of these final trials because it was not advertising.

docs.title: 068 — Bridge concurrency audit
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-11. Scope: Bridge startup, UI, photo jobs, sync outbox and Python FFI ownership.

The Pi Zero 2 W has four CPU cores. The runtime uses asyncio for I/O scheduling, executor threads for blocking filesystem/system/FFI work, a killable image process, and the native Rust runtime. Independent work must preserve response ordering, bounded memory, configuration consistency and cleanup ownership. No public API/schema or image rules change.

docs.title: Stages and dependencies
docs.text:
Stage Independent work that overlaps Required ordering Boot CPU helper, FTP import/bind, Bluetooth agent First UI/input and core READY wait for maximum CPU; Printer waits for agent; optional Sync starts after core readiness. Settings Refresh Network health and saved-Printer lookup Apply only to the still-open page; repeated actions share one worker. Network health UI input, BLE work, FTP/sync transfers Startup/poll/Settings/recovery share one probe; changed config or Wi-Fi activation invalidates and rechecks results. About Version/identity and metrics collection off the UI loop Metrics wait for CPU baseline; one cached collector; no off-page or post-stop repaint. QR identity loads independently and never encodes a placeholder. Preview Printer model detection and enabled EXIF datestamp read Decode/resize follows model; adjustment order is preserved; one large image worker. Immediate print Existing configured-model preparation alongside BLE connect Detected model validates prepared image; transport commands/status/keepalive stay serialized. Sync ingest New file copy/hash alongside reads/acks of existing photos Additions retain arrival order; publish/evict/index commit under metadata lock. Pending photos are not exposed. Shutdown Cancel all UI tasks together within one fixed six-second budget Join owned sender/image/filesystem work before freeing resources or CPU boost; repeated cancellation cannot interrupt FFI grace or decoder cleanup.

The single photo consumer preserves film order. FTP reception, HTTP streaming, GPIO/virtual input, watchdog, network recovery and BLE monitoring already run independently of that consumer. Two large HEIF/RAW pipelines are not admitted together on the 512 MiB board; their pixel buffers can exhaust memory. Transforms that consume preceding output remain ordered. No unbounded worker pool or speculative extra image was introduced. Tiny configuration/preset reads were reviewed; no measured stall justified changing their persistence/rollback ordering in this pass.

docs.title: Ownership corrections
docs.text:
• Stop reaches pending review/preparation/send instead of waiting for a whole photo job. Sender cleanup finishes before releasing its CPU boost or shared backend.
  • FTP bind and outbox-add threads are shielded and joined: cancelling an asyncio waiter cannot stop their socket/filesystem transactions. Captured FTP listeners stop even if startup is cancelled; hashing failures remove unpublished spool files.
  • Image-worker close interrupts active internal preparation instead of waiting on the same lock for the entire job. New/queued work is rejected after close; process-group cleanup survives concurrent close and repeated caller cancellation.
  • FFI cancellation retains the Printer lock until its blocking call completes or the original five-second restart deadline expires. Repeated cancellation cannot reset that deadline or let a second command enter early. A slow-print notice keeps waiting for the original job.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Tests use mutual-start handshakes and held I/O/cleanup gates to prove overlap and ownership, rather than asserting task creation alone. They cover shared network waiters, stale config and activation, navigation during Refresh/About, model/EXIF overlap, sync reads/acks during hashing, fixed shutdown deadlines, decoder descendants and repeated cancellation. Final local checks and hardware observations follow after deployment. No new film print, camera transfer or controlled battery discharge is implied by concurrency smoke tests.

Final local validation: 1,406 Bridge tests, Ruff, strict mypy (65 source files), touched-file formatting, whitespace and strict MkDocs passed. Three independent agents reviewed separate boundaries and the integrated cancellation/startup paths. No App/iOS or FFI ABI changes; sync API response/endpoint review confirmed the existing contract is unchanged.

docs.title: Deployment and on-device checks
docs.text:
Clean runtime 473a62c deployed with its normal pre-commit gate passing. Hardware/OS: Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / Waveshare ST7789 / X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17. Native artifacts/dependencies and saved configuration were preserved. The saved Printer is Instax Square INSTAX-52006924; Sony a7C II remains the camera profile.

Software smoke ran under ib with production methods and injected gates, without GPIO input, a camera upload or a Printer send. Settings Refresh overlapped two injected 250 ms waits, completing in 271.9 ms. Existing sync depth/get/ack completed in 3.1 ms while a new checksum was held. Repeated cancellation retained the FFI lock and kept the next operation queued until the first worker exited. Real Linux image-worker/Pillow preparation produced an 800×800, 4,037-byte synthetic JPEG; closed workers rejected new work. These are controlled concurrency checks, not a physical print-speed or battery benchmark.

First reboot: core ready 14.429 s, UI 14.406 s, FTP listener 14.076 s, Bluetooth agent 14.462 s, hotspot receive-ready 18.797 s, manager 19.344 s. Systemd total 17.152 s. Results remain within plan 067's prior range: this pass adds no measurable boot-speed improvement. Performance governor was applied at 13.464 s, before the first UI frame; normal idle later returned to powersave/600 MHz and GPIO24 low. Both services were active with NRestarts=0; throttling 0x0; hotspot FTP 220 greeting and NOOP/200 passed.

Sanitized measurements and About loading/ready frames accompany this record. The About values are illustrative rendered states, not physical LCD photographs.

The user powered the Printer on for a second reboot. Core ready 14.224 s, UI 14.205 s, FTP 13.870 s, Bluetooth agent 14.262 s; first valid Printer status 17.321 s, hotspot receive-ready 18.620 s, manager 19.252 s, total systemd 16.991 s. Both receive and Printer status were therefore available by 18.620 s after kernel start. BlueZ reported Connected=yes; subsequent status reads retained film 4 / battery 65%. This confirms fresh power-on boot reconnection at the latest runtime; no physical print was sent. The preceding baseline had no advertising Printer and cannot establish a before/after connection speedup. Approximate 4.5-minute Printer idle auto-off remains an external limitation.

Final live hotspot-loss test used normal automatic dark idle (no observation wrapper or injected key). After deactivating the saved hotspot, its IP recovered in 29.75 s. Across 38 samples including 10 seconds after recovery, CPU stayed 600 MHz, GPIO24 stayed low and BlueZ stayed connected. Bridge PID was unchanged; status reads continued with film 4 / battery 65%. These are sampled connection observations, not a claim that every subsecond radio event was monitored. The temporary probes were removed; no config, service wrapper or drop-in remained.

docs.title: 069 — Bridge HIF flow benchmark and ownership fixes
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-12. Scope: Bridge camera reception, HIF preparation and review. No public schema, sync API, native FFI or image-rule changes.

docs.title: Method and baseline
docs.text:
Measurements use the connected Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / Waveshare ST7789 / X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5 and BlueZ 5.82. Saved Printer: Instax Square INSTAX-52006924. Camera profile: Sony a7C II. Runtime baseline: 473a62c. All timed image runs use stock maximum performance, 1000 MHz, with no concurrent benchmark. Each probe restores the previous CPU governor; no source photo is altered.

The largest available camera HIF is 11,255,808 bytes, primary 7008×4672. The existing thumbnailer supplies normalized 1600×1069 RGB, then Square preparation produces 800×800. Saved settings are Auto fit, quality 100, Vivid (saturation 1.5), zero Correction, no date or watermark, and one-second review. Square's 105,000-byte limit selects JPEG quality 76, 102,303 bytes. Exact JPEG and decoded-pixel hashes are recorded in the measurements.

Baseline stage Time External HEIF decode and PNG write 4.793 s HIF opener including PNG read/RGB 5.115 s Fit/crop 0.194 s Colour adjustment 0.088 s JPEG size search, eight attempts 0.327 s Fresh child preparation, three trials 5.892 / 5.785 / 5.798 s

The opener consumes about 89% of the instrumented 5.725-second preparation. Per-process peak RSS was 44,928 KiB for the Python probe and 38,996 KiB for its decoder child; these are independent peaks, not a simultaneous whole-board memory total.

An isolated production FTP receiver uses hotspot address 192.168.8.1:2121 and temporary incoming storage, with the real controller, image worker and review countdown. The client runs on the same Pi, so traffic is locally routed and does not measure Sony Wi-Fi airtime. Square identity/status are seeded; an observer captures the prepared JPEG at the sender boundary. No BLE send or film ejection occurs. The actual Printer is off/not advertising and cannot be remotely powered on. This bounds what can be validated without user action.

Three baseline trials reached that boundary in 7.069 / 7.033 / 7.006 s: FTP upload 0.117–0.141 s, HIF/preview 5.858–5.945 s, review/lookup 1.005 s. Each photo prepares once; the already prepared JPEG is reused at the sender boundary. Native Rust JPEG preparation still occurs later; this probe does not measure it or establish physical print speed.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• The parent image worker owns one temporary, lossless RGB BMP for the current HIF/model. Normalization precedes creative Looks, edit/fit and independent Correction, so reusing the source preserves output exactly. A bounded writer overlaps transformations and joins before JPEG encoding. Lazy Pillow sources load before any shared access.
  • Identity includes canonical path, device, inode, size, mtime and ctime, plus Printer model and working bounds. Replacement, a new photo/model, corruption or decoding failure causes a fresh decode. Cancellation/close removes the cache; idle expiry is five minutes. Maximum working RGB is 1600×1600 (about 7.68 MB plus BMP header); the benchmark cache is 5,131,254 bytes. Large image jobs remain serialized on the 512 MiB board.
  • Successful preparation emits one structured image.prepared event with cache-hit state, source/transform/JPEG/total durations, byte count and selected quality. These are stage boundaries, not a CPU profiler; external decode remains inside the source stage.
  • Queued/current originals are pinned against incoming age/budget pruning. Pins are released for success, failure, cancellation, overflow and shutdown. The 100-job queue is retained; its pinned originals can temporarily exceed the soft incoming storage budget.
  • STOR reserves its canonical destination before opening it. Concurrent or queued/current destinations return 450 instead of allowing an already-open writer to change accepted bytes. Root and /incoming paths share this protection. Interrupted transfers release reservations. Shutdown rejects new uploads with 451 before awaiting teardown, drains queued ownership and retains abandoned files. A late/closed-loop handoff also releases its pin.
  • Datestamps read nested ExifIFD DateTimeOriginal as well as the top-level value. All seven real HIF headers on this Pi store the date in the nested field. Metadata reads avoid pixel decoding; no extra image decode is introduced for the date.

docs.title: A/B and independent review
docs.text:
Interleaved uncached/cached/cached/uncached runs use the same real HIF, settings and fresh killable child for each edit. Uncached edits take 5.75–5.80 s; cached edits take 0.666–0.676 s, about 88% less time. First-photo preparation remains 5.78–5.93 s. All corresponding JPEG bytes, decoded RGB hashes, dimensions and selected qualities match. This improves repeated review edits; it does not speed up first-photo HEIF decoding.

Independent adversarial review reproduced a lazy HEIF decoder race, overlapping FTP writers, late handoff/shutdown ownership leaks and exceptions before job cleanup. All were repaired. Real-socket tests cover overlapping uploads, separate root destinations and interrupted retry; unit/integration tests cover review retention, queue overflow, cleanup, metadata, cache source replacement, model/fit/orientation, corruption, expiry and cancellation. The final review found no remaining P1/P2 issue. A minor timing-boundary caveat was also corrected by eagerly materializing normalized pixels before recording the source stage.

docs.title: Remaining limits
docs.text: First-photo HIF decoding is still the dominant CPU cost. Lowering source resolution or forcing a different thumbnail selection could change print quality, so neither was adopted without quality evidence. JPEG size search is comparatively small and retains its exact output rules. Sony Wi-Fi transfer, native BLE send and mechanical ejection require an awake Printer/camera; their physical duration remains unmeasured in this pass. No claim of improved battery runtime, whole-flow physical print speed or film colour validation follows from the software timings.

docs.title: Final deployment and validation
docs.text:
Clean runtime 738a088 deployed with native artifacts, dependencies and saved configuration preserved. 1,448 Bridge tests, Ruff, touched-file formatting, strict mypy (65 source files), whitespace, strict MkDocs and normal pre-commit passed. Independent final review confirmed the lazy-source timing correction and found no new correctness or material performance risk.

All seven saved HIFs passed on the deployed runtime. First preparation 3.103–5.802 s; cached edits 0.649–0.703 s; uncached corresponding edits 3.146–5.875 s. Every edit matched exact JPEG, decoded RGB, dimensions and quality. All 621 clock samples across the 21 preparations read 1000 MHz; final benchmark temperature 48.850°C, throttling 0x0. Cache cleanup on worker close passed. Date metadata was present in all seven files: first opener registration and header read 247.6 ms, subsequent reads 16.9–28.7 ms. An earlier dataset trial had an idle CPU transition and was excluded from performance results; its parity still passed.

Deployed FTP/controller replay: 7.106 / 7.038 / 7.035 s to sender boundary, HIF/preview 5.977 / 5.897 / 5.902 s, review/lookup 1.004 / 1.005 / 1.005 s, one preparation per photo. All output hashes matched the baseline and all 211 clock samples read 1000 MHz. These fresh-photo times remain within variation of the baseline; no improvement is asserted.

Additional real-socket checks under ib on the Pi verified root and incoming overlapping STOR rejection, queued byte preservation, separate root destinations, interrupted retry, shutdown 451 and cleared pins/reservations. Production services remained active with NRestarts=0 and unchanged post-deploy PIDs. Hotspot and USB addresses, authenticated FTP 220/NOOP 200 passed. Final dark idle was restored to powersave/600 MHz, GPIO24 low, throttling 0x0; no working cache or benchmark listener remained. Printer scans continued to report no advertising device.

Sanitized measurements include complete trials, settings, hashes, versions and final service state. Photos and credentials are excluded. BLE/film, real Sony transfer and battery runtime remain outside the measured boundary.

docs.title: 070 — Bridge print cycle and SD cache audit
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-12. Three independent agents audited receive/queue, review/UI, and image/native Printer boundaries. Root verified the live deployment and benchmarked SD versus tmpfs cache. No public config, sync API, native FFI ABI, protocol timings or App/iOS changes.

docs.title: Cycle coverage and ordering
docs.text:
State Ownership and required behavior Audit result Boot / setup CPU, UI and FTP can start alongside Bluetooth and optional Sync setup. A dequeued item now waits for its chosen destination inside its shutdown-observed job. Unpaired / offline / no film FTP rejects an unusable Print destination before accepting STOR; Sync is independent. Existing checks retained; no automatic resend after uncertain printing. Receive / queued Reserve upload pathname before open; pin completed source before handoff; preserve FIFO. Prior overlapping-upload and retention repairs retained. Shutdown closes admission synchronously. Sync Accepted source remains owned until shared outbox setup completes. Repair early dequeue loss; visible Sync unavailable if setup failed, original retained. Constructor handoff is joined on cancellation. Model / metadata Exact Printer model governs dimensions; enabled date metadata may overlap detection. Cached model is a preparation hint, never a replacement for detection or explicit configuration. Immediate Skip review; prepare independently of BLE connect when a model hint is available. Auto-model now benefits from the same overlap as explicitly configured models. Mismatch discards speculative output. Initial review Decode once; show photo before starting the full 1/5-second review interval. Existing visible-countdown and cancel behavior retained. Edits / tools First interaction requires manual confirmation; coalesce edits to latest state. Unchanged edits now skip worker/encode; bounds and unsupported directions still stop the timer. Accept during update Freeze accepted edit and retain its preparation/cache ownership. Repair SELECT cancelling the cached worker and triggering an unnecessary new HIF decode. BACK/shutdown still cancel safely. Superseded review Newer state/session owns the screen. Confirmation loop rechecks ownership before repaint, preventing late Preview over Printing/error/new session. Lock / wake Shared physical/virtual state persists; active work retains maximum CPU while dark. Existing lock, unlock, no-film and cancellation regressions pass; no new GPIO action is implied. Prepare / native handoff Verify actual model and pass matching prepared bytes. Python handoff reuses the latest edited bytes; core still performs native JPEG preparation. Download start / chunks / end Printer command lock and ordered ACKs preserve transaction integrity. Kept serialized; ACKs lack chunk identifiers suitable for multiple in-flight chunks. LED / execute Existing handoff LED and model pre-execute delay precede PrintImage. Unchanged pending physical validation; optional LED timeout/overlap remains a follow-up opportunity. Success / failure / busy Drain scheduled progress before terminal screen; never blindly resend. Existing Error/no-film/stalled and navigation-preserving Printed notice retained. Sync-only errors no longer restart Printer polling. Shutdown Close admission, release queued ownership, join active workers and close resources in order. Repeated outer cancellation now joins one shielded teardown; delayed Sync construction cannot escape cleanup.

The visible default remains Review → Printing → Home, with a brief Printed notice. Manual, immediate, one-second and five-second confirmation modes remain supported. The single image consumer and large-image worker preserve film order and bounded memory; unrelated FTP, input, network and status work continue independently.

docs.title: SD-card experiment
docs.text:
The live Pi mounts /tmp as tmpfs, with a 232 MiB limit; /var/lib/InstantLinkBridge is on /dev/root, about 57 GiB total with 48 GiB free at measurement. The current normalized source cache is therefore already memory-backed. Linux tmpfs documentation.

Controlled interleaved trials use the same real 11.26 MB Sony HIF, Square model, saved Vivid settings and stock 1000 MHz. Only the parent's temporary cache directory changes. The same 5,131,254-byte lossless BMP is written under /tmp or a temporary SD directory. Four edits per trial, tmpfs / SD / SD / tmpfs, have exact matching JPEG and decoded RGB hashes.

Edit-cache location Samples Mean Range tmpfs 8 0.665 s 0.659–0.670 s SD, file pages still cached 4 0.667 s 0.659–0.670 s SD, file-page eviction requested 4 0.876 s 0.864–0.894 s

For the SD eviction trials, the isolated BMP was fsynced, then POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED requested eviction for that file only. This is advisory; no whole-system cache was dropped. Durable flush cost was 0.245 / 0.259 s, outside edit timing. Clock samples for every retained run read 1000 MHz; no throttling. Probes removed their files and restored dark idle to 600 MHz. Complete sanitized trials.

Decision: keep the active-photo cache in tmpfs. Moving it to SD does not increase hit rate in today's one-photo review flow and makes reads slower when pages are evicted. A bounded persistent SD cache could skip HIF decoding for a previous photo revisited after expiry, another photo or restart. That requires a real revisit/reprint workflow and versioned invalidation; it does not accelerate the first decode of a new camera photo. A normalized-source cache must identify exact source content, decoder/normalization version, model and working bounds. A final JPEG cache must additionally identify all edits, fit, quality, Looks, Correction and overlays. No persistent SD cache, swap change or boot configuration change was introduced.

docs.title: Quality guard
docs.text: The installed heif-thumbnailer v1.19.8 selects an embedded thumbnail when present and only downsizes. The previous HEIF path ignored the model's minimum source edge and could silently enlarge a tiny thumbnail for printing. It now closes an undersized result and retries once with -p at the same bounded working size. Adequate thumbnails keep the same command and pixels. An intrinsically small primary remains printable; fallback failure uses the existing friendly decode error. The decoder timeout and killable process group cover the retry. A regression cancels a real blocked primary-decoder subprocess, clears the working cache and verifies the next job can proceed.

docs.title: Remaining native/hardware opportunities
docs.text:
• The Rust core still reloads, resizes and re-encodes the already prepared JPEG. A future validated prepared-JPEG core/FFI entry point could reduce CPU work and JPEG generation loss. It needs exact detected-model, RGB/JPEG integrity, dimensions and byte-budget guards. Mini Link 3 must still receive exactly one vertical flip; Mini/Square/Wide passthrough and Link 3 must not be conflated. Native elapsed time and physical output are not measured this pass.
  • The optional handoff LED uses the generic ten-second response timeout. Bounding its wait or overlapping it with the mandatory pre-execute delay may save latency, but its relationship to Printer firmware must be verified. Protocol chunk delays remain: the reference 102,303-byte Square image has 57 chunks, 8.55 seconds of configured packet sleeps plus one-second pre-execute delay before other transport/ACK overhead. These are code-derived, not a measured physical total.
  • Core returns at successful PrintStatus. Code does not separately observe mechanical ejection. Two queued physical photos should establish whether success already implies readiness for the next DownloadStart. No mechanical/busy regression is asserted without that evidence; automatic retry after uncertain send would risk duplicate film consumption.
  • Fresh FTP address probes and per-photo paired-device lookup are small remaining candidates; measure their actual contribution before adding stale network/identity caches.

The saved Printer remains off/not advertising, so no BLE send, ejection, new Sony Wi-Fi upload or battery discharge is claimed. Hardware/OS: Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / Waveshare ST7789 / X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17; Sony a7C II profile, Instax Square INSTAX-52006924.

docs.title: Final validation and deployment
docs.text:
Firmware code a7f5fc1 committed, pushed and cleanly deployed; subsequent documentation-only firmware deployment includes identical runtime code. 1,471 Bridge tests, normal pre-commit, Ruff, touched-file formatting, strict mypy (65 source files), whitespace and strict MkDocs passed. Independent cross-review found no actionable P1/P2 finding. Test groups reported by agents overlap and are not added together as an inflated total. Existing sync API and App/iOS contract unchanged.

On-Pi state smoke exercised real HIF review and an actual active image child. SELECT during the zoom 1.25 update remained pending until its result, then completed in 0.739 s; two preparations used one source decode and handed the edited 103,366-byte, quality-80 JPEG over unchanged. The controller used abstract input, NullDisplay and seeded Square status; no physical Printer send or GPIO action occurred. A synthetic real HEIF with an embedded 160×120 thumbnail retried primary 1600×1200, with exact primary RGB parity.

Deployed seven-file dataset retained exact baseline JPEG/decoded RGB, dimensions and quality for initial and edited output. First preparation 3.116–5.813 s, cached edits 0.638–0.693 s; every retained clock sample across 21 jobs read 1000 MHz. All dates present, worker cache cleanup passed; final benchmark 47.236°C, throttling 0x0. No first-photo speedup is claimed.

Verified health: clean deployment, Bridge/manager active, NRestarts=0, hotspot/USB present, authenticated FTP 220/NOOP 200, GPIO24 low, powersave/600 MHz, throttling 0x0, no working-cache directories. Config/dependencies and native FFI SHA are unchanged. Temporary benchmark scripts/directories and synthetic fixture were removed. Physical Printer remained not advertising, so native send/LED/ejection and two-photo mechanical readiness were not benchmarked. No boot/swap settings changed.

docs.title: 071 — Prepared JPEG native handoff
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-12. Three agents implemented native validation/FFI, Bridge preparation/handoff, and independent adversarial tests. Root benchmarked real HIF-derived payloads on the Pi.

docs.title: Implementation and compatibility
docs.text:
The Bridge now hands its final JPEG to three additive prepared-JPEG FFI exports. Core owns validation and the existing serialized Printer transaction; the App's file-based ABI remains unchanged. No public management/sync API, settings, protocol delays or App/iOS code changes.

  • Require exact detected model, including Mini versus Mini Link 3 despite identical dimensions. Model configuration is a preparation hint; mismatch discards speculative preparation.
  • Require the model's exact dimensions and byte limit, 8-bit three-component baseline JPEG, complete entropy scan, neutral recognized EXIF orientation and no trailing data.
  • Apply Mini Link 3's vertical transport flip before the final Python JPEG encode. Reverse it only for the LCD preview. Mini/Square/Wide preserve their prior JPEG and pixels. The lossless working cache remains before the transport flip and is reused by edits.
  • Feature-detect the optional native export off the UI loop. Older native builds prepare an unflipped JPEG and retain the legacy file path; stale Link 3 output is rebuilt from its source.
  • Keep the in-memory ctypes buffer and callback alive through the synchronous native operation, including repeated outer cancellation. Release global FFI device ownership before callbacks; retain the per-Printer operation lock through the transaction. No fallback/resend after errors.
  • Validate before every Printer write and transmit the exact supplied JPEG bytes. A bounded decode checks integrity but does not resize, correct colour or encode again.

See the FFI contract for model IDs, return codes and buffer/callback rules.

docs.title: Adversarial review and repairs
docs.text:
Independent tests reproduced a half-truncated entropy scan with EOI restored being accepted by both attempted Rust decoders, which recovered missing pixels even in strict mode. The final validator uses an owned per-call libjpeg-turbo handle with STOPONWARNING enabled and checks header parameters before bounded allocation. Quarter/half/three-quarter truncations with EOI restored now fail. TurboJPEG is statically bundled through turbojpeg-sys; CMake/compiler and x86 NASM prerequisites are documented and installed in CI. No new Pi runtime package is needed. Upstream TurboJPEG API.

Independent tests cover exact model/flip, byte limit/dimensions, grayscale, CMYK, PNG, progressive/trailing JPEG, EXIF orientation, corrupt entropy and no Printer writes on rejection. Bridge tests cover upright previews, exact prepared bytes/flag/model, old-library compatibility, no resend on native failure and buffer/lock lifetime under repeated cancellation. Final review has no remaining actionable P1/P2 issue. All nine independent native tests also ran on arm64 Pi.

The full Bridge suite exposed an existing FTP test timing race: queue handoff can precede the callback's ownership-release finally. A same-connection NOOP after 226 orders terminal assertions without weakening overlap/rejection/byte checks. The test fixture now closes its event loop on its serving thread. This tests-only fix passed 300 stress cases with zero BadFD teardown noise and an independent second review. Production FTP code is unchanged.

docs.title: On-Pi benchmark
docs.text:
Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0, stock 1000 MHz (every sampled frequency checked), Debian 13.2, Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17. ST7789 LCD and X306 2300 mAh battery; Sony a7C II profile, saved Instax Square INSTAX-52006924.

The real 11,255,808-byte HIF has primary dimensions 7008×4672. Saved Auto fit, Vivid saturation 1.5 and neutral Correction were retained. Requested quality 100 is reduced by each model's existing size budget to Mini 80 / Link 3 42 / Square 76 / Wide 85. Both native paths were built in the same arm64 release. Five interleaved measurements per model compare legacy native decode/resize/encode/chunk with strict validation/chunking of the final Python JPEG. Times below are medians; they exclude Python preparation, BLE, ACKs and mechanical ejection.

Model Legacy native preparation Prepared validation/chunk Time reduction JPEG bytes Chunks mini 738.49 ms 13.47 ms 98.18% 104,154 → 102,631 116 → 115 mini_link3 612.31 ms 10.78 ms 98.24% 54,224 → 54,498 61 → 61 square 943.30 ms 15.56 ms 98.35% 104,628 → 102,303 58 → 57 wide 1609.59 ms 28.87 ms 98.21% 223,131 → 217,375 248 → 242

All prepared output JPEG hashes match their Python inputs exactly. Square preserves the prior 102,303-byte reference JPEG and RGB hashes. This removes a lossy generation; the new pixels need not equal the old native re-encoded pixels. Link 3 flips once before encoding, so its JPEG can differ slightly from flip-after-decoding an earlier lossy generation; asymmetric-image orientation tests check semantics, not equality with the old lossy result.

The Square native preparation saves about 0.928 seconds. Its one fewer packet, and Wide's six fewer packets, also reduce configured packet sleeps by 0.15/0.90 seconds respectively; those are code-derived opportunities, not measured physical print totals. First HIF preparation still takes 3.86–6.24 seconds across models, with decode remaining the main first-photo cost. No new SD cache is introduced; the active lossless source remains in tmpfs.

Full benchmark, byte/RGB hashes, pixel differences, clock samples and settings. No throttling (0x0); benchmark restores powersave at completion and removes temporary JPEGs/cache.

docs.title: Validation and deployment
docs.text:
• Rust workspace: 205 passing tests (25 CLI, 134 core, 9 independent integration, 36 FFI, one doc test), build, formatting, Clippy with warnings denied and committed-header drift check.
  • Bridge: 1,497 tests, Ruff, touched-file formatting and strict mypy (65 source files).
  • App harness: 156 tests; existing file-based ABI reviewed for compatibility.
  • Nine independent native tests passed on the Pi (2.10 seconds).

Clean code commit 6ca7035 was pushed and deployed with newly built arm64 CLI/FFI artifacts. Native provenance records that source commit, dirty=false, locked release build and artifact hashes. Installed FFI SHA-256: 8d5ee8081dc297f9c588038410941433d3f72a5eebe9b8c5f688dad476e5f75d. All three exports are present. The validator has no new dynamic JPEG dependency on the Pi.

Installed production worker/ctypes smoke passed for all four models using an asymmetric synthetic image: correct dimensions/budget, exact in-memory bytes/model/flip, upright decoded LCD render and Link 3-only transport flip. The actual C export rejects null/zero/invalid declarations with -5 and valid calls with -1 in its separate no-device process. Connect/model lookup were observed at the Python boundary; no actual BLE connection, connected transaction, progress dispatch or physical LCD was tested by that smoke. The separate nine native arm64 integration tests cover strict JPEG validation and transaction rejection. No film was consumed.

Post-deploy health: Bridge/manager active, NRestarts=0, hotspot 192.168.8.1 and USB 192.168.7.1, FTP greeting 220 / NOOP 200, dark powersave 600 MHz, GPIO24 low, throttling 0x0 and zero working cache directories. Python/Pillow/pillow-heif/pyftpdlib versions are unchanged. Temporary candidate libraries, benchmark binaries, source overlays and probes are removed after verification. Subsequent documentation-only deployment carries identical verified runtime code and artifacts. The saved Printer is not advertising, so physical BLE/film speed and colour remain unmeasured.

docs.title: 072 — Live HIF-to-Printer benchmark
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-12. The user powered on the saved Instax Square Printer. The unmodified installed Bridge 7249d4e automatically reconnected, reporting film 4 and battery 65%. Native artifacts remain the clean 6ca7035 build; FFI SHA-256 8d5ee8081dc297f9c588038410941433d3f72a5eebe9b8c5f688dad476e5f75d. No production code, settings, protocol delay, service restart or native artifact change this pass.

docs.title: Method and boundaries
docs.text:
One saved Sony a7C II HIF (DSC02697.HIF, 11,255,808 bytes, primary 7008×4672) was uploaded once with a unique filename to the production FTP listener at the hotspot address. This was a same-Pi local-route replay: it exercises real FTP admission, queue, physical/virtual UI flow, image worker, one-second review, native prepared-JPEG export, BlueZ and physical Square Printer. It does not measure camera Wi-Fi airtime. Existing Auto fit / Vivid saturation 1.5 / neutral Correction / requested quality 100 settings were retained. The existing byte budget chooses 76. No retries or additional sheets were used.

A temporary btmon observer captured host/controller traffic without changing the runtime or Printer transaction. An offline parser checked every reconstructed Instax packet checksum, 57 ordered data indexes, matching successful ACKs and zero padding after declared JPEG size. It reassembled the actual outgoing JPEG. Monitor data had zero reported drops. Journald and btsnoop timestamps were correlated with the FTP client's clock; benchmark boundaries use journal observation times, with native phases measured directly from HCI traffic.

Hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / ST7789 LCD / X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2, Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17; Instax Square INSTAX-52006924. All 128 retained CPU samples during the boosted job were 1000 MHz; throttling remained 0x0. This is one measured print, not a latency distribution.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Stage Time Boundary Local FTP upload 0.153 s Client STOR start through 226 Dequeue through JPEG ready 6.618 s Includes CPU wake / worker setup; pipeline itself 5.850 s Image source opening 5.222 s Worker stage log; dominated by HIF decoding Transform / JPEG encode 0.297 / 0.331 s Worker stage logs JPEG ready through native job start 2.060 s Includes visible 1-second review, UI and Printer lookup Job start through DownloadStart 0.025 s Wrapper/model checks and strict native JPEG validation DownloadStart through DownloadEnd ACK 21.811 s Actual successful 57-chunk BLE transfer LED acknowledgement 0.026 s Optional handoff LED answered promptly LED send through PrintImage send 1.030 s Includes LED ACK and required 1-second pre-execute wait PrintImage send through PrintStatus ACK 0.031 s Command accepted; not mechanical ejection Native job start through Bridge completion 23.151 s Includes transfer and terminal callback/UI drain FTP STOR start through Bridge completion 32.005 s 31.852 s after upload completion

Film changed 4 → 3, and subsequent live status polls confirmed film 3. The first film-3 poll was about ten seconds after the Bridge's completion log. The Bridge/native success event means successful PrintStatus; there is no mechanical-ejection sensor or measured film-development interval. Do not label 32.005 seconds as time until developed film is ready.

No comparable full-print run of the old firmware on this exact workload was made, so this does not establish an end-to-end before/after speedup. Plan 071 separately measured the removed native re-encode (Square median 943.30 → 15.56 ms under the same release).

docs.title: Quality and orientation
docs.text:
The JPEG recovered from actual Bluetooth writes is exactly the prior Python reference:

  • 800×800, 102,303 bytes, selected quality 76, Square transport flip false.
  • JPEG SHA-256 1354cc449d9903ef44a15c09f9e75e35484af2f596df89034a3255ebed337ec8.
  • Decoded RGB SHA-256 a7b9a07e96030e453f17d2c72f5bd99d7a01f06f1e47055f197e982bb7d262f9.

The recovered image was decoded and shown to the user for comparison. After development, the user confirmed the physical film was upright, unmirrored, and free of unusual colour or detail problems. This is direct visual confirmation for this Square photo and saved settings; no instrumented colour measurement, film photograph, other model print, or all-scene quality claim. Personal image pixels and the raw Bluetooth capture are retained locally, not committed to Git.

docs.title: Next optimization: BLE transfer
docs.text:
The transfer dominates this run. Exact HCI attribution:

  • 10.089 s accumulated span between first and last outgoing fragment of each data chunk. This is transport fragment dispatch time, not isolated CPU cost or a pure RF measurement.
  • 2.785 s waiting from each chunk's final outgoing fragment through its Printer ACK; mean 48.85 ms, range 45.40–61.79 ms.
  • 8.707 s between ACK and next chunk send across 56 gaps, mean 155.48 ms; plus 0.158 s after the last data ACK before DownloadEnd. The configured minimum is 150 ms per chunk, 8.550 s total; actual scheduling adds small overhead.
  • DownloadStart/DownloadEnd ACKs and small dispatch gaps account for the remainder.

A read-only BlueZ query after printing reported the write characteristic MTU 247, flags write-without-response and write, and WriteAcquired false. Current core fragments are fixed at 182 bytes. A full Square packet is 1,819 bytes, requiring 10 current writes; an ATT value budget of 244 bytes would require 8. The negotiated MTU is exposed by the BlueZ 5.82 GATT API. The installed btleplug 0.11.8 public Peripheral API has no MTU getter.

First candidate: measure a transport path that respects negotiated MTU and preserves per-model fallback, byte identity, ACK ordering, timeout/cancellation and reconnect behavior. Potentially fewer writes address the largest non-sleep span. A larger negotiated ATT MTU does not prove the Printer's application firmware accepts larger Instax fragments; that requires controlled validation before changing production. A Linux acquired-write path is another option, but must own/close its descriptor and re-acquire after reconnect, per the same upstream API. No acquired write or larger-fragment send was attempted in this audit.

Second candidate: benchmark a smaller post-ACK delay independently, keeping one command in flight and testing multiple photos/models and recovery. This could reduce the measured 8.9-second wait budget; one success at 150 ms gives no evidence that a shorter delay is reliable. No delay was changed. HIF source opening remains the next CPU bottleneck at 5.22 seconds. Cached edits already bypass that decode. Optional LED handling is not a meaningful target on this run because its ACK arrived in 26 ms. Review/render/Printer lookup contributes another 2.06 seconds, including the deliberately retained one-second review.

docs.title: Final state and evidence
docs.text:
Bridge/manager remained active, PIDs 13129/13127, NRestarts=0; FTP stayed listening, dark idle returned to powersave 600 MHz / GPIO24 low, no throttling. Printer status stayed fresh at film 3 through 08:28:13 EDT. At 08:28:23 it became unavailable and then stopped advertising; the cause was not observed, and this audit does not establish indefinite Printer uptime. The Bridge kept its normal saved-Printer reconnect/search behavior. No service was restarted.

The temporary monitor/process, root-owned trace/probes and duplicate benchmark upload were removed from the Pi after completion. The original HIF is retained. Production source/artifacts are unchanged. Sanitized timing, transactions, hashes and verification.

docs.title: Scope and decision
docs.text:
Implement negotiated fragments in authoritative Rust core, preserve prepared JPEG bytes and model orientation, and verify Printer reconnects. Three subagents implemented, wrote independent fault and packet tests, and performed adversarial review. No public FFI ABI, Python configuration, sync contract, App UI, image processing, protocol pacing or SD cache change.

Linux reads the exact connected BlueZ write characteristic MTU once per connection with a bounded one-second query. Production uses min(MTU - 3, 236); absent or ambiguous metadata and other platforms retain 182 bytes. Known small MTUs clamp either policy. Diagnostic comparison permits 244. All packet/ACK operations remain serialized; uncertain delivery is never replayed. Actual large-write failures downgrade that device on a fresh connection and require link reset. A small status failure requires reset without a false size downgrade. The process cache is bounded at 128.

docs.title: Physical paired print
docs.text:
Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W / ST7789 240×240 / X306 2300 mAh; Debian 13.2, Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82, Bridge 0.1.17. Instax Square INSTAX-52006924. User-selected DSC02825.jpeg, saved Vivid saturation 1.5 / neutral Correction, Auto fit. Real production FTP/UI/native printing; two sheets, no replay. Same-Pi hotspot-address FTP excludes camera Wi-Fi airtime. Completion means Bridge/Printer command completion, not timed mechanical ejection or film development.

Metric Stable 182 Candidate 244 FTP start → Bridge completion 27.934 s 28.375 s Native handoff → completion 23.224 s 24.089 s Download start → End ACK 21.837 s 22.724 s Data GATT writes 570 456 Data HCI ACL packets 3,990 4,275

Both transferred the exact same 102,846-byte / 800×800 / quality 87 prepared JPEG, SHA-256 867ca28e128bd60149a33d719646ab649c12d4d45d62e0b104e4ec1dda32f878, identical decoded RGB. All 57 indexes, ACKs, checksums and zero padding matched. Square flip false. User confirmed the second film was upright, unmirrored and had the same colour/detail as the first. Film 3→2→1. Other models have unit coverage, not new physical film verification.

244 reduced GATT writes but was slower. The Pi controller exposes 27-byte LE buffers and no Data Length Extension feature; related length commands return Unknown HCI Command. The full 1819-byte Square packet takes 70 HCI packets at 182, 75 at 244, and 70 at 236. Hence 236 is the production ceiling. HCI captures do not measure radio retransmissions, battery energy or general runtime.

docs.title: Same-connection no-film crossover
docs.text:
Two rounds each of 182, 244 and 236, same prepared JPEG / connection / 1000 MHz. Each download ends with an exact Cancel ACK; no PrintImage command. Six Start/End/Cancel pairs, 342 ordered Data ACKs, identical JPEG hashes; film remains 1 and history remains 67.

Payload Mean download/cancel Data GATT writes 182 21.896 s 570 244 22.784 s 456 236 21.778 s 456

236 saves 20% of GATT writes and only 0.117 s (~0.54%) in these two samples. This is a small transport improvement, not a measured large full-print speedup. All 1,388 clock samples were 1000 MHz. The remaining ~8.9 s of post-ACK pacing and controller/write scheduling dominate. Shortening model-specific pacing needs separate reliability evidence and is outside this change. SD cache does not address this transport bottleneck.

The original crossover completed counters but exited with a teardown Timeout before its JSON was emitted. HCI capture independently verifies completed measurements; retained JSON explicitly records that nonzero exit. No HCI Disconnect was recorded before the teardown timeout/recovery. The original capture did not identify which D-Bus stage expired. The fix attempts bounded physical disconnect first and verifies authoritative disconnected state; it closes the old transport and marks reset before any await. Cancellation preserves reset, and forced reset skips a potentially stuck preliminary state query. The diagnostic now prints completed rows and separate benchmark/cleanup errors before returning nonzero on either failure.

docs.title: Validation and deployment
docs.text:
Independent tests cover MTU bounds/identity ambiguity, bytes and padding for every model, lock serialization, partial-write/no-ACK/cancellation poisoning, bounded D-Bus resources and recovery cache, no replay, teardown RPC failure/timeout/cancellation, and retained diagnostic results. Rust workspace 245 tests, build/fmt/Clippy, App 156 tests and strict docs passed. All 44 independent transport/diagnostic tests also passed on the Pi arm64. Adversarial final review found no remaining P1/P2 issue. Final hardware teardown and clean artifact deployment are recorded in the Bridge context and sanitized assets after verification.

Evidence: docs/assets/bridge-audit-073/physical-{baseline,candidate}.json, download-crossover.json, controller.json. Personal pixels and raw Bluetooth captures are not committed. Sources: BlueZ characteristic API, Bluetooth Link Layer.

docs.title: Follow-up from live teardown validation
docs.text:
The first status-only check still timed out. Filtered D-Bus capture proved Disconnect was received by BlueZ, but no reply or HCI disconnect occurred before the two-second application budget. BlueZ 5.82 deliberately schedules radio teardown with a two-second GLib seconds timer, which can run after our deadline. Linux now allows five seconds for physical disconnect and eight seconds around the FFI teardown; state queries/notification cleanup remain two seconds, other platforms retain prior budgets. All waits stay bounded and cancellation retains reset. BlueZ device implementation.

Status-only evidence also exposed an existing history decoder error: observed Square data is 00000043 00000012; reading its first two bytes incorrectly returned zero. The narrow correction recognizes the observed eight-byte body and reads its leading big-endian 32-bit counter with checked conversion to the existing public u16. Exact two-byte legacy replies remain supported; malformed/overflow replies fail explicitly. Diagnostic Python fallback uses the same rule. Trailing history bytes remain uninterpreted; no public ABI change or broader protocol claim.

Final clean code a24b8b7 and rebuilt arm64 CLI/FFI deployed. Installed FFI selected MTU 247 / payload 236, returned film 1 / history 67, completed two disconnects with return code 0 and authoritative closed state (1.987 / 2.133 s). The normal Bridge automatically reconnected with fresh status. HCI confirms two Disconnect Complete events and zero download/print commands. Rust 251 tests, Bridge 1,524 tests/lint/mypy (65 files), touched-file formatting, header drift and 51 independent Pi cases passed; App 156 and strict docs passed. Full Python formatting flags 16 untouched baseline files. Sanitized installed validation/health and clean artifact manifest accompany the measurements.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Optimize the Square Printer's post-ACK 150 ms chunk delay using no-film evidence on the Pi. Three subagents own implementation, independent tests and adversarial review; root controls hardware benchmarks and deployment. Work starts from clean 096c7ca, native a24b8b7.

Image bytes, model geometry/orientation, chunk sizes, 236-byte production fragments, ACK ordering, and pre-execute waits remain unchanged. Other models and platforms retain their existing pacing. The final chunk keeps its model settling delay before DownloadEnd. SD caching does not change these Bluetooth waits.

docs.title: Safety audit
docs.text:
Current Data ACK matching checks only the opcode, although the observed Square reply echoes a 32-bit chunk index. The correction enforces an exact reported index and rejects malformed indexed replies for Square only, where the echoed index is verified. Other models keep their response-tail compatibility until hardware evidence supports a stricter interpretation. Exact one-byte legacy status replies remain compatible. They cannot authorize faster pacing; the baseline is retained after a legacy reply. Stale/future ACKs share the transaction's original deadline, without sending the chunk again.

Any accelerated transfer failure must require a fresh connection and conservative pacing for future jobs. No uncertain image is replayed. A failure before acceleration starts must not falsely disable faster pacing. Transfer cancellation and failures around End/execute need explicit review.

docs.title: Benchmark design
docs.text:
Real hardware: Pi Zero 2 W, ST7789, X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2 / Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5 / BlueZ 5.82 / Bridge 0.1.17, Instax Square INSTAX-52006924. Use the previous DSC02825.jpeg at saved Auto fit / Vivid saturation 1.5 / neutral Correction. Prepared Square JPEG is 102,846 bytes / 800×800 / quality 87; SHA-256 867ca28e128bd60149a33d719646ab649c12d4d45d62e0b104e4ec1dda32f878.

One connection, fixed 236-byte fragments, two reversed-order rounds of intermediate delays 150 / 100 / 75 / 50 / 25 / 0 ms. Only a matching indexed ACK authorizes the next shorter wait. Final settling remains 150 ms. DownloadStart → 57 Data ACKs → DownloadEnd → DownloadCancel, with exact ACK checks and no PrintImage, LED, reset or shutdown command. CPU is sampled at 1000 MHz; normal power/service behavior is restored after each trial. Compare before/after film and history, reconstruct the outgoing JPEG from HCI and verify checksums, padding and indexes.

Follow with fresh-connection comparisons of the selected policy and baseline, then exercise the installed production transfer loop without executing a print. Final reconnect and dark 600 MHz health checks must pass. No-film evidence proves outbound byte identity and protocol acceptance; it does not independently measure developed-film appearance, mechanical execution, other models, battery energy or real camera Wi-Fi airtime.

docs.title: Validation gate
docs.text: Mock/paused-time tests cover every model's baseline, held/stale/indexed/legacy ACKs, operation serialization, exact prepared bytes/flip/padding, final settling and pre-execute waits, failure and cancellation, bounded fallback, no replay and no-film diagnostic command restrictions. Run affected Rust gates, header drift if needed, App logic checks and strict docs. Record the selected timing, sample size, independent review, clean native provenance and installed hardware state before declaring completion. Personal pixels and raw Bluetooth captures stay out of Git.

docs.title: Initial offline implementation status
docs.text:
During initial offline preparation, production preferred delay remained 150 ms pending hardware measurements. The new no-film helper shares the production transfer loop, hardcodes print option 0, checks Cancel ACK and never calls LED or PrintImage. The diagnostic wrapper also rejects actuator packets.

A full-transfer guard covers Start/Data/End/handoff/execute and cancellation during chunk waits. Interrupted transfers require reset; after an accelerated wait, uncertain errors restore baseline pacing for future jobs in a bounded 128-device cache. Fragment and pacing fallback are separate. Known NoFilm/CoverOpen/LowBattery errors require reset without falsely penalizing pacing; busy, unknown rejection and transport uncertainty remain conservative. The first selected shorter wait is marked before await, and the final settling delay is excluded.

Three subagents completed implementation, independent tests and review. No unresolved P1/P2 issue in this passive 150 ms state. 278 Rust workspace tests, build, fmt, Clippy, committed FFI header drift and strict docs passed. All 52 targeted mock tests also passed on real Pi arm64, including five Linux-specific transport cases. Hardware benchmark, shorter-delay selection and final firmware deployment remain pending because the Printer is unavailable/not advertising. The Pi remains reachable and its existing services are active. No film consumed in this task.

docs.title: Hardware selection
docs.text:
After Printer discovery resumed, all 12 sweep transfers completed successfully. Two reversed-order samples per intermediate delay, fixed 236-byte fragments and final 150 ms settle:

Intermediate gap Mean download/end/cancel 150 ms 23.403 s 100 ms 19.296 s 75 ms 17.376 s 50 ms 15.704 s 25 ms 14.947 s 0 ms 13.139 s

The first 150 ms sample was 25.281 s versus 21.524 s on its repeat; it is not a representative warm baseline. A fresh connection with 25/150 then reversed 150/25 gave 22.266 s at 150 ms and 15.349 s at 25 ms: 6.918 s / 31.1% less transfer time. Four complete samples; this excludes camera upload, processing/review, pre-execute and mechanical printing.

Select 25 ms to retain intermediate settling margin even though zero delay was accepted. Only Square/Linux/236-byte/indexed-ACK connections use it; fallback and unverified contexts keep 150 ms. Final settle 150 ms and pre-execute 1000 ms remain unchanged. No film used. All 16 transfers reconstructed the identical JPEG/RGB hashes, ordered indices, zero padding and checksums. There were 912 indexed Data ACKs, exact End/Cancel ACKs and zero actuator commands. Film stayed 1 and history stayed 67; both trials disconnected successfully. All clock samples were 1000 MHz with no throttling. This establishes protocol acceptance on this Square/Pi, not internal stored pixels, developed-film quality, mechanical timing, other models or battery runtime.

Independent adversarial review decoded the sweep separately and confirmed the evidence. The selected constant still passes model/platform/fragment/legacy/failure gating tests. Shared production-loop and installed-firmware checks follow before completion.

docs.title: Shared production transfer check
docs.text:
Selected 25 ms compiled code exercised the actual send_image_data loop via the strict no-film helper. Two successful runs took 14.875 / 14.850 s; each reported exactly 56×25 ms waits and one final 150 ms wait, 236-byte payload, 57 indexed ACKs, identical JPEG/RGB/padding/checksums, checked End/Cancel and no actuator commands. Film 1/history 67 unchanged; clean disconnect, 1000 MHz, no throttling. This validates the shared transfer path while avoiding PrintImage.

An earlier production-probe attempt failed before model detection/Data with Not connected. HCI shows connection establishment followed by reason 0x3e; no host Disconnect or image packets. Normal Bridge recovered automatically. The harness now explicitly closes/verifies the prior link before a fresh probe; this is controlled handoff, not proof that an old disconnect timer caused the event. The failed setup is retained separately and excluded from timing means.

docs.title: Clean firmware deployment
docs.text:
Selected source f574445968e963ae35231d64d5f784ac1f5a5b28 was committed, pushed and deployed using the standard arm64 artifact build and Bridge deploy script. The manifest records a clean worktree and locked release build; the installed FFI SHA-256 matches b601ec6a8b14138617ebbae5e5c74b892bb461ee2d2747dbfc6ed181f253bacb.

Selected code passed Rust 278 workspace tests, all 52 targeted arm64 tests on the real Pi, format/Clippy/header checks and strict docs. The normal source-commit hook also passed Bridge 1,524 tests, lint and mypy. Three subagents implemented, tested and independently reviewed.

Initial installed health: both services active, NRestarts 0, correct USB/hotspot addresses, FTP 220 / NOOP 200, no throttle or working caches. After the normal 60-second idle timeout, the screen was off (GPIO24 low) and CPU was 600 MHz / powersave, with FTP/Wi-Fi still ready. The Printer had stopped advertising during the build, so these initial health records explicitly show it disconnected and do not establish post-deployment Printer reconnect.

The first installed probe stopped before discovery/image commands because its temporary harness required a cached BlueZ device. An absent cache now permits fresh discovery; a connected cache still prevents starting a fresh probe. No production-source change or film consumption resulted. At this stage, the post-deploy shared-core probe and installed FFI reconnect checks awaited the next Printer power-on.

docs.title: Final installed validation after Printer power-on
docs.text:
The shared-core no-film probe rebuilt from clean f574445 passed two post-deploy transfers: 14.950 / 15.104 s, 236-byte payload and exactly 56×25 ms plus final150 ms waits each. An independent decoder verified 114 exact indexed ACKs, unchanged canonical JPEG/RGB hashes, ordered requests/replies, padding/checksums and two successful End/Cancel pairs. Zero actuator commands, film1/history67 unchanged, all sampled CPU clocks1000MHz and throttle0x0.

The actual installed FFI separately passed two status/disconnect/fresh-reconnect cycles: Square, MTU247/payload236/conservativefalse, film1/history67, return code0 and authoritative closed state in 2.769 / 2.206 s. Independent HCI decoding confirmed two physical Disconnect Complete events and only support-info commands, with no Download/PrintImage/LED/reset/shutdown. The shared-core probe exercises the installed source's transfer loop; it does not call the FFI print API. No new physical-film appearance or mechanical print timing was measured.

The normal Bridge automatically reconnected after probe restoration. Final idle state: 600 MHz / powersave, screen off/GPIO24 low, Printer connected, fresh film1/battery35 status following the powersave transition. Both services active with unchanged PIDs/NRestarts0, Wi-Fi/USB addresses correct, FTP220/NOOP200, throttle0x0 and zero working caches. Runtime docs commit61925ba and native sourcef574445 are both clean; installed FFI hash matches the official manifest. The final independent adversarial review found no unresolved issue.

Sanitized evidence is in docs/assets/bridge-audit-074/. Temporary test binaries, duplicate photo uploads and raw captures are removed after review; the user's original DSC02825.jpeg is retained. The Bridge remains running normally with the selected 25 ms policy.

docs.title: Extended idle observation
docs.text:
After completing the connected screen-off check, normal status polling continued every ten seconds through 14:47:03. The first unavailable status was 14:47:13, approximately 299 seconds after reconnect and over three minutes after the 600 MHz transition. Services and Bluetooth daemon PIDs remained unchanged; documentation-only deployment did not restart them. Latest health still verifies powersave600MHz, screen off, Wi-Fi/FTP ready, NRestarts0, no throttle or working caches, with the Printer offline.

This timing is consistent with the Square's documented five-minute idle auto-off (Fujifilm manual); the official FAQ documents its automatic power-off toggle. The prior physical power-light state was not recorded, so its actual power-off is not asserted. Independent review found no reason to invalidate completed transfer/reconnect checks: selected pacing affects image DATA transfers, while idle support-info handling is unchanged.
