Bond-cache reset occurred after the Printer disappeared. No pacing rollback or Printer power-setting change was made. Do not infer indefinite idle availability from these checks.

docs.title: Automatic recovery after the extended offline period
docs.text:
The user powered the Printer on again. Without restarting/unlocking the Bridge or issuing a manual Printer connection, the existing 30-second recovery scan matched it at 15:33:47.030; connection completed 15:33:50.237, fresh film1/battery35 status 15:33:50.764 and again 15:33:56.582. Time from physical power-on was not measured.

Read-only health confirms the same Bridge/manager PIDs13234/12101, NRestarts0, CPU600MHz powersave, screen off/GPIO24 low, Printer connected, FTP220/NOOP200, correct USB/hotspot, throttle0x0 and no working caches. Runtime ab76bb4 is clean; native FFI hash remains the validated f574445 artifact. No film or additional test photo was used. This closes the normal power-on reconnect check after the extended idle/offline observation.

docs.title: Bridge runtime correctness and idle audit
Scope and evidence
docs.text:
The user prioritizes system correctness and efficiency over battery-runtime benchmarking. The Pi is disconnected for other work. Audit the saved runtime journals, status/recovery records and source locally; do not claim access to the complete current Pi journal or deploy without a reachable device. Source baseline: clean 20a6eb0, native f574445.

Saved evidence covers boot, normal connected/offline polling, Wi-Fi recovery, FTP/printing, and the recent extended idle/power-on cycle. Several captures are filtered or overlap, and older captures precede subsequent fixes. Distinguish observed events from source-derived findings. Personal photo data and raw journals remain outside Git.

docs.title: Findings and implementation
docs.text:
1. A failing blocking FFI worker can replace its caller's cancellation during the cleanup grace period. A completed worker raising TimeoutError can also be mistaken for a stuck worker. Preserve cancellation after consuming the completed worker's error, retain serialization until actual completion and keep the existing deadline for genuinely stuck workers. The print sender watchdog has the same TimeoutError ambiguity: inspect completed results before reporting a slow or stuck print, preserving a sender's own timeout as a failure.
  2. Obsolete Printer polls can apply failure/recovery side effects despite their generation being superseded. Bond-reset cancellation is swallowed, and cancelled poll tasks are dropped from shutdown ownership. Reject stale results before side effects, propagate cancellation and retain retired task references until cleanup.
  3. Unchanged status is logged at INFO on every poll; ordinary Printer absence produces repeated warnings and scan progress. Keep state changes/recovery and genuine errors visible, move unchanged observations/expected repeated absence to DEBUG, preserving scan frequency, status I/O, freshness and Printer recovery policy. Keep first/value-change/recovery status records and a five-minute healthy heartbeat at INFO so quiescent operation remains observable. First expected absence is INFO; recurring not-found scans are DEBUG. Late-stage connection failures remain visible with their stage.
  4. The render maintenance timer wakes every 0.35 seconds even with the screen off. About collection can also continue while its page is hidden by the lock. Use a slower dark maintenance cadence bounded by freshness deadlines, reschedule on display transitions, and avoid starting hidden About collectors. Awake interaction and networking remain operational.

docs.title: Validation and limits
docs.text:
Reproduce the cancellation, stale-result and hidden-collector cases before fixing them. Use controlled worker/events, cancelled recovery tasks and fake clocks to verify ordering, cleanup ownership, genuine error visibility, TTL expiry and prompt wake. Run touched-file formatting, Ruff, strict mypy, the complete Bridge suite and strict docs. Audit affected shutdown/printing/network paths for regressions.

No native ABI, image bytes, Bluetooth pacing, config/schema, sync API, App or iOS change is planned. Do not infer energy savings or hardware performance from timer/log reductions. Hardware smoke and the complete live journal audit remain unavailable while disconnected.

docs.title: Audit coverage and results
docs.text:
Reviewed available boot journals, runtime status/recovery captures, FTP/print traces and the prior hardware audits alongside current startup, printing, FFI serialization, UI polling, shutdown ownership, power scheduling, image-worker/cache, FTP spool and manager-listener code. The saved log inventory summarizes event counts and ranges without committing raw journals. It contains overlapping and filtered sources; aggregate counts are not a complete uptime or error-rate measurement. Several older warnings describe behavior fixed in earlier plans.

The startup branches already overlap independent CPU helper, FTP, UI and Bluetooth work. Network callers share bounded probes and recovery backoff. Image preparation stays off the event loop with source/cache ownership retained through cancellation. FTP upload ownership and manager listener retry/cleanup remain intact. The main queue's bounded wait also checks FTP listener failure; it was not lengthened at the expense of shutdown/failure detection. Existing bond reset and silent-link recovery policy was retained because it has verified hardware purpose; this audit fixes obsolete/cancelled callers, not Printer protocol policy.

An offline replay of the 25 saved unchanged healthy status records produced 1 INFO / 24 DEBUG records while still making 25 fetches and preserving readiness. This is a mocked I/O replay, not a hardware or energy benchmark. Dark maintenance's nominal maximum interval changes from 0.35 to 5 seconds; expiry deadlines and user wake still take precedence.

Eighteen new regression cases cover worker failures during cancellation (including its own TimeoutError), sender timeouts before/after the slow notice, stale failure generations before and during fetch, bond-reset cancellation, retired cleanup ownership, TTL expiry while dark, prompt wake, hidden About reads, unchanged/changed status, sparse heartbeat and genuine error visibility/stage tracking. Focused checks passed; the complete Bridge suite passed 1,542 tests. Ruff, strict mypy (65 source files), touched formatting and strict docs are the final gates. Validation host: macOS / Python3.13.9, mock I/O; no Pi or Printer accessed in this audit.

The candidate is committed/pushed for review. It is not deployed while the Pi is disconnected. Installed native f574445 and its firmware runtime are unchanged. On a future connection, verify real lock/wake, Print/Sync transitions, cancellation/reconnect and a full runtime journal before claiming hardware efficiency or complete live-log acceptance.

docs.title: Subsequent live acceptance
docs.text: The Pi was reconnected later on 2026-10-12. Plan076 records deployment of these changes, review of all retained application/service journals plus the current kernel journal, and real-runtime lock/unlock, FTP print and recovery checks. The offline counts above remain unchanged historical evidence. Additional native discovery, startup bond and network readiness fixes are recorded in plan076 rather than attributed to this offline audit.

docs.title: Bridge live runtime acceptance
docs.text: Deploy plan075, review complete available service/kernel journals, and validate installed lock/unlock, printing and automatic recovery on Pi Zero2W / ST7789 / X306 / Instax Square.

docs.title: Live finding: inactive BlueZ records
docs.text:
The fresh boot retains the saved Printer's name, UUIDs and bond, but Connected=false and no RSSI property. Native discovery accepts the cached name immediately and attempts connection: 30-second reply timeout followed by In Progress. Cancelling a genuinely long call during deployment hit the old runtime's five-second cleanup deadline. Plan075's completed-error correction does not claim to fix a still-running native connection attempt.

On Linux, exclude a candidate with neither RSSI nor a confirmed connected link. Keep already connected devices usable without advertisements. Bound connected-state queries by one shared 250ms budget per collection, rather than paying a new timeout for every cached Printer. Other platforms and image/packet/pacing behavior stay unchanged. RSSI is scan evidence, not a guarantee of current liveness; stale RSSI after prior discovery remains a limitation.

docs.title: Hardware validation
docs.text:
Use a temporary root/ib-only Unix socket observer around the installed runtime. Send abstract button events through the same action queue as GPIO; use the actual LCD/framebuffer, CPU helper, FTP, networking, FFI and saved settings. Record this automation boundary: it does not test the electrical switch contacts. Restore the normal service afterward and remove the observer.

Check same-button unlock including different GPIO identities sharing Select, blank-frame regression, ten-second abandonment and CPU return to600MHz. Upload DSC02825.jpeg once through production FTP for one authorized physical print; no uncertain retry. Check film/history and captured JPEG bytes, expected orientation, ACKs, CPU boost and terminal UI state. Recover a controlled disconnected link automatically while locked and retain service/FTP/network health. Separate deployment/test restarts from spontaneous failures and historical faults.

docs.title: Live finding: startup bond recovery
docs.text:
Repeated service-discovery failures after deployment exposed a missed online→offline edge: BlueZ retains the Printer bond across Bridge restarts, while an Instax power-off can clear its key. Check the existing reset_bond_if_disconnected guard once when a status polling generation starts, after backend readiness and before its first fetch. Connected identities are preserved; selection is retained. Superseded generations do not fetch after the check, and cancellation propagates through owned cleanup. Three regression cases fail before the fix. This startup action is logged at INFO with its actual reason.

The user-selected validation photo changed to DSC02832.jpeg because the earlier source was no longer present. Preserve the original and saved processing settings.

The same live attempt showed reactive bond removal racing a later status connect: bluetoothctl remove timed out while the poll entered discovery again. Polls now await active rebond recovery before their startup guard or another fetch, using shielded ownership because recovery may replace the polling generation. A regression test verifies the wait and that cancelling a poll does not cancel the recovery task.

docs.title: Live finding: down interface with retained IPv4
docs.text: A locked wlan0-down fault left 192.168.8.1 assigned, and the address-only health snapshot continued reporting receive-ready indefinitely. Recovery did not run; Printer stayed connected. Restore wlan0 explicitly after this failed probe. The shared bounded address snapshot now excludes interfaces whose explicit Linux flags omit UP. This also avoids Bonjour advertising an administratively down endpoint. Do not require LOWER_UP/carrier or operstate=UP: dormant AP/USB interfaces must remain available. Five cases cover down and admin-up/dormant/unknown state; the two down cases fail before the fix. No additional poll, subprocess, public field or sync wire-contract change is needed.

docs.title: Hardware results and remaining cost
docs.text:
• GPIO-equivalent queue events on the actual ST7789 framebuffer passed prompt/nonblank frame, button-identity reset, three same-button unlock and 10-second abandonment. Timeout/lock returned to 600MHz; awake prompt/unlock ran at 1000MHz. No electrical contacts actuated.
  • One production FTP print of DSC02832.jpeg passed, film1→0, history67→68 on later fresh connection. Initial post-print history remained67 while the Printer finished its own work. Exactly one PrintImage, 58 ordered indexed ACKs and exact 104,552-byte/800×800/quality88 JPEG and RGB reference hashes, Square flip=false. Captured image reviewed upright; developed film not inspected. 19.779s FTP-start→Bridge completion; processing1.844s, download15.238s, native handoff→completion16.340s. Same-Pi FTP excludes camera airtime and mechanical/development time. All65 sampled job clocks were1000MHz, throttle0x0; locked600MHz resumed afterward.
  • Forced authoritative BlueZ disconnect recovered automatically in44.340s with unchanged Bridge PID3981, fresh status and physical Connected=true. Screen stayed locked600MHz. Genuine warnings caused by the injected lost link are recorded, not suppressed.
  • The retained-IP wlan0 fault failed before the network fix; the interface was manually restored. With the fix, a second outage recovered via the normal hotspot helper in32.706s, restoring AP/readiness while locked600MHz. This repeat had the Printer offline; connected Printer retention during the new recovery still requires a powered Printer. No camera association/airtime measurement.
  • A30s dark/offline sample used3.1 process CPU seconds (10.33% of one core at600MHz). Native GPIO polling was the largest identified thread (6.9% lifetime CPU); a separate1s strace showed ppoll on8GPIO-line FDs with mostly500µs timeouts. Python GPIO held threads and Rust workers were low. No dependency/alert timer changed: that needs electrical input latency, bounce and held-button validation. This is not an energy measurement or before/after claim.

Local gates: Bridge1551, Rust282 including doctest, App156; Ruff/strict mypy65 files, touched format, Rust build/fmt/Clippy/header drift, strict docs and normal hooks passed. Pi runtime has no pytest installed; no test dependency was added. Native clean dedfdb2 SHA and runtime clean8bbbd88 provenance are saved in docs/assets/bridge-audit-076/. Printing used811d51f; subsequent8bbbd88 changes only network snapshot filtering and retain identical print/native code. No additional physical print is needed; the Printer now has no film.

docs.title: Goal and boundaries
docs.text:
Reduce the lgpio input alert thread's idle CPU cost while preserving button responsiveness, physical button identities, 50 ms stable debounce, held-press behavior and lock/unlock rules. The previous live audit measured 3.1 process CPU seconds in 30 seconds at 600 MHz; a native GPIO thread was the largest observed cost. Its alert loop uses a hard-coded 500 µs ppoll. There is no supported alert-period configuration; lgpio MIN_DELAY controls transmit timing.

Use a GPIO character-device v2 group request with kernel debounce and asyncio fd readiness. Keep the legacy gpiozero/lgpio path as a safe fallback. Do not modify installed dependencies or the LCD backlight in this change. Any lgpio backlight transmit activity remains a separate cost. Keep source, hardware verification and performance claims distinct.

docs.title: Implementation and validation
docs.text:
• Independently verify GPIO v2 ABI, flags, event semantics and chip identity against primary documentation and the actual Pi headers. Preserve all eight BCM mappings and queue IDs.
  • Own and close request descriptors on every setup/read failure; remove readers before closing. Bound batch draining, detect lost/out-of-order records, and avoid ambiguous synthetic presses.
  • Run kernel GPIO-mockup tests for edge/debounce/burst/held timing and lock/unlock integration. Use only a newly created simulated chip and its debugfs values; never drive physical inputs. Remove only test-owned resources. Electrical switch contacts are outside this automation.
  • Measure paired actual-runtime dark CPU samples at 600 MHz with matched background activity, including per-thread and child CPU and whole-system counters. Exclude tracing overhead from timing samples; do not infer energy/battery runtime from CPU counters.
  • Run an independent adversarial review, local affected tests, Ruff/strict mypy/full Bridge gates and strict docs. Deploy the clean validated source, verify the actual input backend, lock/unlock and normal runtime health, then remove temporary observers and test resources.

docs.title: Candidate results, 2026-10-12
docs.text:
• Default input owns one GPIO v2 request for all eight lines, using both edges, pull-ups, kernel debounce and bounded asyncio readiness reads. Held startup levels are suppressed until release. Overflow resynchronizes and discards uncertain buffered presses. Setup, read failure and shutdown release owned descriptors before fallback/reopen.
  • An actual legacy close/reopen failure exposed a retained native pin callback. Public callback detachment before Button.close fixes persistent registration; no private dependency patch or installed-package change is needed. Independent review has no blocking findings; an already executing legacy callback is an inherited teardown limit.
  • Three 30-second actual-runtime samples per condition, dark/600 MHz/Printer offline: baseline mean 10.012%, candidate 1.710%, forced legacy repeat 10.900% of one core. Child CPU is separate; whole-system counters are recorded. This measures process CPU, not energy, battery runtime or performance with the Printer connected.
  • Paired kernel mockup input tests passed 21 assertions/28 actions for each backend. Candidate stimulus-to-queue p95 56.38 ms, legacy 52.47 ms: about 3.91 ms extra including 50 ms debounce and kernel scheduling. Candidate stable-event-to-queue p95 0.583 ms. Short bounce/35 ms presses ignored; stable75 ms, held, triple and eight-line burst accepted. A simulated pull-up resets startup level, so physical held-at-claim is covered by unit policy tests rather than claimed from mockup hardware.
  • Kernel edges into the production UI queue passed 11 cases with the real LCD/CPU: nonblank wake, key/joystick identity reset, triple unlock, held press, rapid75 ms presses, 10-second abandonment returning dark/600 MHz, and detached mock callbacks remaining inactive. Physical switch contacts were not actuated. Printer offline/film0; no film consumed.
  • Bridge 1571 tests, Ruff, strict mypy 66 files and touched format passed; independent reviewer separately passed 68 focused tests and descriptor checks. Sanitized evidence: docs/assets/bridge-audit-077/. Raw journals and temporary tooling remain outside Git.
  • One CPU setup sample was rejected during unlock warmup; one UI assertion needed to await the asynchronous wake. A recreated root-only mock device needed test-owned permissions. Harness corrections are recorded; these are not accepted timings or production failures.

docs.title: Bridge idle network and recovery lookups
Goal and evidence
docs.text:
Audit the remaining dark idle CPU after kernel GPIO input. Current normal runtime uses 600 MHz with Printer offline, camera hotspot control session idle and services stable. Three 30-second baseline samples measured 1.365%, 2.265% and 1.132% of one core. A shared executor worker accounts for the largest process share and runs both network probes and FFI; its CPU cannot be attributed exclusively to network queries. Network health launches ip every five seconds locked and every second awake; sync address maintenance also requests snapshots. Trace time is not a CPU measurement.

Current logs show no new exception, GPIO fallback, rendering error or reconnect fault. The two earlier rejected FTP health probes are controlled plan077 events. Printer absence is deduplicated. An authenticated hotspot control session has no upload in the capture.

docs.title: Boundaries and implementation
docs.text:

Retain bounded ip fallback for unsupported systems or protocol/socket failure. No address cache, dependency change, new setting or App/iOS/FFI contract change.

Preserve existing UI network cadence, coalescing, stale-generation rejection, hotspot recovery, source policies, FTP reception, CPU tiers, wake/lock and Printer reconnect. Native Bluetooth scan/keepalive timing is outside this change. Per-interface lookup compatibility must remain explicit; its current assigned-address behavior differs from UP-filtered batches.

docs.text:

docs.title: Additional log/profile finding
docs.text:
The initial full-runtime candidate samples were higher than the older baseline despite zero network subprocesses. A same-process forced ip repeat and a native repeat separate the network change from startup/ambient BLE variation. Do not attribute all shared executor CPU to network probes or claim total CPU savings from query latency alone.

A subsequent syscall diagnostic identified bluetoothctl devices and info launched by silent-link recovery for an offline Printer. The existing 30-second recovery cooldown can make these read-only checks recur even when they correctly find no connected link. Each observed child used roughly 0.08–0.09 CPU seconds. No-op recovery is not a new runtime fault.

Replace only that discovery with a fresh bounded BlueZ ObjectManager D-Bus snapshot. Preserve Address and Alias identity matching, platform suffix normalization, authoritative Connected booleans and default-controller semantics. Fast path requires one verified adapter; ambiguous or unavailable/malformed data uses the existing CLI fallback. No negative cache, no cooldown change and no change to disconnect/remove/trust mutations, native scanning or keepalive.

Validate shared-bus cancellation isolation, malformed/timeout fallback, connected-only identity matching, empty/offline no-op and no pseudo addresses passed to CLI. Benchmark both changes with no tracing during CPU intervals, and identify remaining native Bluetooth CPU separately.

  • BlueZ5.82 CLI device enumeration
  • BlueZ Device1 contract

docs.text:
• Fresh snapshots matched ip in ten physical-interface comparisons. Seven isolated namespace cases passed multiple prefixes, scope filtering, aliases, point-to-point local/peer, retained addresses on down interfaces, deletion and forty concurrent reads. Physical interfaces were read only; owned namespace/dummy removed.

  • Read-only BlueZ parity passed five comparisons.100fresh D-Bus lookups median 22.851ms, versus10CLI lookups median 616.758ms. FDcount 8→8. Diagnostic process owned one separate bus without registering/exporting an agent or mutating devices; production uses its existing registered agent connection.
  • Independent review caught a blocking-constructor risk in the first BlueZ draft. That draft was not deployed; shared-agent lookup resolves it. No remaining blocking findings. Network non-atomicity and existing fallback timeouts are explicit boundaries.
  • Local Bridge 1647 tests, focused 221, Ruff and strict mypy 67 files passed. Eleven kernel-to-production-UI cases passed with both changes, real LCD/CPU and no film. Physical button contacts, developed-film output and live Printer reconnect are not tested here; Printer is offline and native print/transport code is unchanged.

docs.title: Full-runtime candidate measurements
docs.text:
All sets contain three30-second dark/600MHz/offline samples; syscall tracing is separate. Original baseline process+children 2.242% of one core. Network-only first candidate 3.219% is retained rather than hidden; shared worker/startup/Bluetooth CLI activity prevents attributing that comparison to network. Final combined/forced legacy/combined repeat on one PID12639: 1.576% /1.998% /1.754% including children. Six native samples pooled mean 1.665%, approximately 16.7% less than the three legacy samples. Native sets have zero child CPU and no lookup CLI calls; first native90s captured18network/3Bluetooth reads. Legacy90s has18ip/2devices/2info, no mutations. docs.text:

One additional ERROR is retained: temporary observer writer.drain after a test client reset (associated missing-argument invocation). This harness was removed; it is not a production source fault. No new production faults, service failures or automatic restarts identified. Historical actual faults remain recorded. This is service-journal review, not kernel review. All owned observer/source/scripts/socket/drop-in/mockup/namespace resources are removed.

docs.title: Goal and baseline
docs.text:
Reduce repeated Linux discovery work while preserving automatic Printer reconnect, unfiltered scanning, model detection, scan cleanup and existing candidate checks. All hardware checks in this work use no film.

The installed Bridge, dark at 600 MHz with the Printer offline, measured 1.499%, 2.631% and 1.499% of one core in three 30-second intervals, with zero child CPU. A separate 36-second D-Bus diagnostic found 12 native ObjectManager queries and 225 native Device1 GetAll queries. Cached unrelated devices are queried on each 400 ms discovery poll. One additional ObjectManager query belonged to Python recovery. Tracing is excluded from accepted CPU intervals.

docs.title: Implementation boundaries
docs.text:
Keep btleplug's selected-adapter peripheral handles. Read a second fresh bulk BlueZ snapshot and skip only records with valid metadata that identifies no Instax name or service. Possible Printers still use the existing fresh properties, Android exclusion and Linux RSSI/connected evidence checks. Missing, malformed or removed records use the original per-device path; unavailable bulk data uses the complete original path. Snapshots are never cached across polls.

Reuse an owned D-Bus connection with a 500 ms overall acquisition/open/query budget. Cancellation drops the caller's resource; a mutex waiter cannot invalidate another caller. A stalled blocking connection open holds its semaphore permit until completion. The reader never starts or stops discovery.

No dependency, FFI, settings, image, fragment, pacing, CPU-tier or UI change. The extra snapshot is not atomic with BlueZ property updates: a name/service arriving after the prefilter is observed by the next poll. One-shot scan results retain a boundary at their final collection time.

Source review found unchanged cached-session/command-lock/timeout/retry policies, with no prefilter-specific concern. INFO logs do not establish a radio cause or an exact delay breakdown. docs.title: Recovery defect found by hardware testing
docs.text:
The 180-second Bluetooth daemon restart check did not pass. The later shutdown journal showed bluetooth.agent_unregister_failed, ending in BlueZ Does Not Exist. The process still held _registered=True even though the restarted daemon had lost its pairing agent. This is a concrete lifecycle defect, separate from the unproven radio cause of individual status failures. The full service log capture contains 2592 records; the temporary candidate process has 225 INFO, 25 WARNING and one ERROR. The error is a production agent lifecycle error, not an observer writer failure.

Extend this work with event-driven owner tracking on the existing Python agent bus. An awaited match rule and handler precede the initial owner query. Registration uses fresh proxies addressed to the current unique owner, owned bounded retry tasks and checks after awaits. Owner loss clears readiness immediately. Shutdown removes its handler/tasks, unregisters the current partial/full registration, and closes its bus; BlueZ's expected missing-agent reply is handled narrowly. No idle polling or process launches are added. Test daemon absence/return, repeated signals, partial registration, owner/stop races and snapshot reply freshness, then rerun the real restart gate.

The native optimization itself is clean a8b637c, pushed and installed. Native FFI SHA-256 fdd47eaddb35f630534b5f250c8810515c5c14ac0ad5a68fa46a83f46f185973; CLI 3744699d034ab1870e563bbca2c3aad88aff43f0485097ae6bf929595d051cee. Both baseline and candidate ELF comments identify Rust 1.97.1 and the same compiler and linker versions. Installed normal PID16829 / manager16827 are active, NRestarts0, dark600MHz, FTP220/200 and no current application WARNING/ERROR; Printer offline at that capture. A fresh installed Printer check and agent-recovery deployment remain.

docs.title: Bridge stale-link detection and reconnect retries
Evidence and goal
docs.text:
Plan079 exposed slow cached-link recovery: a forced disconnect exceeded a 65-second test deadline before eventual recovery. Status and background keepalive share a command lock, failed commands wait up to ten seconds, and a second failure can fall back to the ordinary offline search period. The pairing-agent registration defect identified there is already repaired.

Reduce wasted waits after a dead link, preserve transient-error tolerance and bounded scan/bond recovery, and use no film in hardware benchmarks.

docs.title: Implementation boundaries
docs.text:
• Probe authoritative transport connectivity only while an expected response has been missing for a second. Bound each query; inconclusive errors retain the original response deadline. Idle and normally acknowledged commands add no probes.
  • Confirmed disconnect closes the old transport and quickly fails queued work. Available acknowledgements take priority. Never replay image or execute commands.
  • Keep the FFI connectivity getter cheap and callback-safe; report terminal disconnected state without a blocking hardware query or a new export.
  • Cached Bridge sessions marked disconnected are discarded. Unknown status failures retain existing tolerance. Permit two short status-recovery retries after an online-to-failed transition, then return to ordinary offline cadence.
  • Wait for both bond reset and silent-link recovery before a new status fetch; retain cancellation, generation guards and live-connection protection.

No image, fragment, pacing, settings, CPU tier or sync-contract change.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Independent core and Bridge implementation, plus adversarial review.
  • Mocked timing, ACK/disconnect races, inconclusive queries, cancellation, queued work, keepalive ownership, bounded retry and recovery/fetch concurrency tests.
  • No-film baseline/candidate native status latency and full-runtime reconnect, with all failed attempts retained and radio absence distinguished from timing.
  • Affected local gates, actual ARM64 unit execution, clean source/native manifests, deployment, final log/health checks and removal of owned test resources.

docs.title: Source acceptance
docs.text:
Independent review found and resolved a recovery/fetch overlap: both rebond and silent-link cleanup are now awaited before a fresh connection. Final frozen review passed, including ACK precedence, bounded/inconclusive queries, cancellation, callback-safe getters, scoped keepalive ownership and bounded retry budget. Sixteen independently selected cases passed.

Host locked workspace tests: 291 unit/integration plus one doctest; App 156; Bridge 1689. Pi ARM core 190 and FFI 39 passed. docs.title: Live acceptance after Printer power-on
docs.text:
The normal installed runtime automatically reconnected and reported Square film 0 / battery 20% at 08:18:20 EDT on 2026-10-13. No manual Reconnect action was used.

  • Two external Device1 disconnects recovered automatically, observed by 19.867 s and 11.610 s on the installed firmware. Every sampled state stayed locked at 600 MHz, with camera receive readiness preserved and fresh film 0 status after recovery. Harness times include state reply and a final BlueZ query; status timestamps were 19.780 / 11.561 s.
  • Historical source 4c9e28b was archived and rebuilt with the same toolchain/flags. Its FFI SHA256 exactly matches the previously installed baseline (fdd47e…5973). Full-runtime baseline missed its 100 s deadline, then recovered in the same PID at 104.242 s. All timed rows and the subsequent state are retained. Different poll phases and target visibility prevent a universal speedup claim; the target matched on a later attempt, with cause unproven.
  • Baseline reused the dead cache twice, then started fresh connection attempts at 39.235, 69.237 and 99.240 s. Installed fresh attempts started at 9.849 and 9.390 s; the first run needed one prompt retry after a five-second miss. This verifies the cache/retry changes.
  • Direct native tests: the first status won the disconnect race on both builds (~89 ms). The next failed status took 2.793 ms baseline / 6.035 ms installed; baseline still returned connectivity 1, while installed returned 0. These show correct retirement, not reduced write latency or a hardware measurement of the one-second missing-ACK probe. Successful direct status reads all showed film 0 / history 68. Keepalive was disabled only in these test processes.
  • Initial baseline direct setup missed a scan; retried setup missed another then connected. All failures are retained. No radio cause or baseline connection defect is inferred.
  • Independent evidence review passed after correcting stale pending conclusions and timing labels. No additional source correctness issue; no image/print commands or film used.
  • Normal service restored: Bridge PID 23036 / manager 20393, active / NRestarts 0, 600 MHz, GPIO24 low, temperature 42.932°C, throttle 0x0, hotspot/USB/FTP healthy, Printer connected with fresh Square status. Reviewed 3697 current-boot service records; normal PID has 39 records and no warnings/errors at capture. Controlled baseline warnings and earlier harness/historical faults remain in the full journal; raw logs are private.
  • Observer/drop-in/socket, baseline source/library and test scripts removed; configuration and saved photos unchanged. Current native artifacts/clean manifest restored after the historical rebuild; installed hashes remain the reviewed d8cee35 binaries.

The next latency candidate is the 9.4–9.8 s wait for the next status poll after a drop. A disconnect event on the existing shared BlueZ bus could prompt the next check sooner, without increasing idle polling. Successful fresh connect/status attempts took 2.17–3.83 s in these runs; these are entire attempt durations, not BLE-only timings.

docs.title: Final normal-service power-return check
docs.text:
After the clean 08:33 capture, the Printer stopped advertising at 08:37:01 EDT. The cause was not observed. Two one-time status-loss warnings were logged; the same Bridge PID 23036 retired the link, removed the disconnected bond and resumed search. Hotspot/USB/FTP and 600 MHz operation remained healthy. A later camera FTP control session is separate from this benchmark; no upload/airtime claim.

The user turned the Printer on again. Automatic discovery matched it at 08:43:08.842, and fresh Square film 0 / battery 20% status returned at 08:43:12.386 EDT, with no manual Reconnect action or service restart. Power-on time was not measured. Final health confirms the same PID / NRestarts 0, connected, 600 MHz, reviewed native hash and clean runtime source 79b53e9. The two earlier warnings remain in the final snapshot; there is no additional fault on power-return. No film used.

docs.title: Goal and evidence
docs.text: Plan 080 measured 9.4–9.8 seconds waiting for the next status poll after a link drop. Use disconnect events on the existing agent-owned BlueZ bus to prompt that check, keeping periodic status as a fallback and preserving bounded reconnect retries. No film is used in validation.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Authenticate unique BlueZ sender, selected device identity, owner and lifecycle. Handle connection loss/removal/daemon changes conservatively; unrelated or malformed messages cannot initiate recovery.
  • Callbacks only coalesce a wake request. Status fetching remains serialized with printing and recovery; callbacks do not disconnect, delete bonds or replay commands.
  • Retain events arriving during a fetch. Retired generations/selection changes and shutdown disarm subscriptions. Own cleanup signals cannot create a retry loop.
  • Keep ten-second status checks as fallback, normal offline cadence, two prompt retries, print pause/cancellation, screen behavior and 600/1000 MHz tiers.
  • Reuse subscriptions while online. No per-poll snapshot, new idle queries, extra polling, Rust/FFI change, public configuration field or sync-contract change.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Independent producer/consumer implementation and adversarial review; authenticated signal/lifecycle, lost-wake, print-pause, cancellation, retry and fallback tests. Baseline/candidate/installed real status-only disconnect/reconnect timing; retain misses and separate target visibility from software latency. CPU samples, actual LCD/input/power checks, full running-log review, clean deployment and removal of owned test resources.

Hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Rev1.0 / ST7789 LCD / X306, Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924. Debian 13.2, Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82.

docs.title: Source acceptance
docs.text:
Independent producer and consumer work plus adversarial review resolved three issues:

  • Stale disconnected iOS/Android aliases could invalidate a healthy connection. Resolve one live path; ambiguous identity retains periodic fallback.
  • A failed watch setup could repeat snapshot IPC/warnings on every successful poll. Attempt once per connected episode; a real transition/generation permits another attempt.
  • Detected model metadata could differ from the captured selection and reject its callback. Match address and name, allowing model updates while rejecting either selection change.

Final independent review passed 36 targeted cases, including independent regressions. Agent suite 48 and controller/runtime suite 288 passed; strict mypy 67 sources, Ruff, touched formatting and whitespace checks passed. Native/FFI, image processing, protocol, configuration and sync contracts are unchanged. Full final path-scoped gates run at commit.

docs.title: Early hardware observations
docs.text: The first baseline harness accidentally started protected wake from automatic screen-off. It recovered in 15.536 s but failed the locked at 600 MHz condition; excluded and retained. The aligned baseline passed at 12.401 s, first new fetch 9.885 s after disconnect request. Early candidate runs woke from the actual BlueZ signal in about 260 ms, with full recovery observed by 19.558 s and 13.963 s after failed scans/target matching. Target visibility varies: these demonstrate wait removal, not a universal full-flow speedup. All accepted rows stayed locked at 600 MHz/camera-ready. No film used. Final installed acceptance follows below.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Reduce measured discovery/setup overhead while preserving automatic reconnect, model detection, notification readiness, selected identity and command serialization. Real-device validation uses status requests and external disconnects only; no film or image/print commands.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
• Subagents audit native setup, Bridge bond gating and dependency lifecycle independently.
  • Reuse the agent bus for a fresh bounded connected-identity check with conservative CLI fallback.
  • Overlap read-only MTU discovery with the existing notification-settling floor; retain fallback.
  • Correct the observed bluez-async message-stream cleanup panic without suppressing other failures.
  • Retain active-scan/ambiguity/Android/liveness and retry behavior. Avoid optimistic cached advertising assumptions or additional idle polling.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
Record baseline/candidate/installed setup stage timings and full recovery, misses and variable radio availability separately. Compare negotiated MTU/payload, low-frequency locked state, status freshness, camera/network readiness, subprocess/query overhead and current running logs. Use focused cancellation/race/fallback tests, full path-scoped gates, independent adversarial review and normal deployment. Remove owned temporary fixtures and restore normal service.

Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W Rev1.0 / ST7789 / X306, Debian13.2, Linux6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python3.13.5, BlueZ5.82; Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924.

docs.title: Log audit correction
docs.text: Plan081's final normal-process WARNING/ERROR counts were accurate for those severity strings, but missed a native Tokio panic printed directly to stderr during service discovery at09:41:09 EDT. Printer connection and status subsequently succeeded. The full-log scan here includes panicked, D-Bus cleanup failures and thread messages so a zero structured-error count is not misreported as complete fault absence. This task investigates and fixes that cleanup race.

docs.title: Implemented and reviewed
docs.text:
Clean source 82f60971f7465fa46492cda455edff38de2695b4 is installed under /opt/InstantLinkBridge. Final FFI SHA256 d23d3b817108b0243ab474af2970f1fd7748431c317af64b38bc4c5eb94f3d38, CLI b3fcffc0c0d1a351e2cdafbdddee065393434cb1c01f56e6fa1239874e9502dc.

  • After an authenticated disconnect, serialized recovery closes the old session and runs the existing live-link guarded bond cleanup before its first fresh discovery. A live matching identity prevents removal. The first failed-fetch path does not duplicate cleanup; generation checks, print pauses, two prompt retries and periodic/offline fallback remain.
  • The connected-identity gate uses the agent's bounded fresh snapshot, requiring one known adapter and valid device state. Unknown/malformed/unavailable data uses CLI. A successful inventory does not probe an absent old physical address; failed/unknown CLI state cannot authorize removal. Cancellation kills and reaps owned CLI children despite repeated cancel.
  • Replacement polls join earlier cleanup and distinguish child cancellation from their own cancellation. Printing joins all three mutating recovery owners, with a six-second limit that aborts printing while retaining unfinished owners; resuming still waits before fetch.
  • MTU metadata lookup overlaps the unchanged 200 ms notification settle floor, with a fresh post-settle retry for missing/default MTU and the original 1.2 s combined budget. A known small MTU remains safe if refresh fails. Print bytes, orientation, pacing and ABI unchanged.
  • Localized bluez-async 0.8.2 patch retains receiver/match ownership, handles in-flight local dispatch, and removes one captured daemon match without panic. Cleanup is bounded best effort on daemon failure/prolonged dispatch/runtime absence. Licenses/provenance retained; Linux workspace scope and equivalent upstream style fixes keep normal host/Linux gates.

Independent adversarial review found and fixed unscoped negative snapshots, orphaned CLI children, overlapping recovery, print handoff and post-cancel reconnect termination. It also checked actual repeated host subprocess cancellation. Final independent affected suite: 337 passed. No source blocker remains.

An early prototype was absent for its 100 s initial readiness wait. Candidate 1 has a complete passed JSON but its stdout capture encountered ENOSPC; candidate 2 could not save JSON and is excluded. Gates: normal hooks 1763 Bridge tests, 27 existing GPIO/deprecation warnings; host Rust 298 tests +1 doctest, App156, targeted337, strict mypy67, Ruff/touched format, Rustfmt, host/Linux production strict Clippy, header drift and strict docs. docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Remove the duplicate Printer status read after a named progress connect. Keep status freshly read during each caller request, automatic reconnect and cancellation ownership. No retained status cache or time-to-live policy. Hardware checks use status/disconnect only, no film.

docs.title: Design and validation
docs.text:
Subagents implement core/FFI and Bridge integration; independent adversarial review checks initial failures, unchanged connected polling, status identity, callback/pointer safety, replacement/cancellation and older-library compatibility. An additive connect-and-status FFI returns the successful initial read directly. Existing API meanings remain unchanged.

Compare baseline/candidate/installed status command count and setup/status-tail times, keeping failed attempts, scan/radio variance, locked600MHz/camera-ready state and full running-log review. Validate all path-scoped gates, deploy clean native/Python artifacts, restore normal service and remove owned fixtures. Pi unit binaries use SD-backed /var/tmp.

docs.title: Source acceptance, 2026-10-13
docs.text:
Clean source ffe637e implements the additive seven-argument C entry point with four signed i32 status outputs. A fresh request consumes the connection's initial read once; established polls and the existing print connection path retain their hardware reads. Older libraries retain their established fallback; a new-API failure does not retry another connect entry point. No cache or TTL is introduced. Non-connect operations retain the existing caller serialization contract. Null inputs preserve outputs/current session, and failed initial reads retire the provisional connection without publishing status.

Independent adversarial review fixed two lifecycle issues: ordinary disconnect retains admission through physical teardown, and caught panic cannot poison the unit admission guard permanently. Callback disconnect invalidates provisional generation; reentrant connect fails promptly rather than deadlocking. A further freshness fix moves successful scan cleanup before the initial status read, with no awaited adapter cleanup after successful sampling. A gated regression changes replies during cleanup and verifies the new values, using one status sequence.

Normal hooks passed 1773 Bridge tests, 27 existing warnings; 308 Rust tests +1 doctest, App156, Ruff/strict mypy67, formatting, production Clippy, header generation/drift and strictdocs. Independent suites: Bridge55, FFI23, corePrinter23 and cleanup regression1. Pi ARM connect tests23 plus teardown/panic checks2 passed with no Printer. Source review/hashes are retained under docs/assets/bridge-audit-083/. Final Linux FFI SHA256 88974b10dd285f4eb3b31a08fc8af68756d3612e5cdf8910a1c719b74e265e82; CLI e720bef273ebfca85b96743d85b9c77bb99dd8fcce13fc91e9d3ba52b15f7d79.

docs.text:
After Printer power-on, baseline/candidate/installed tests completed on the hardware above. No image or print commands, and no film used. Each status sequence is battery, film/charging and history. The returned fields are from the same successful physical connection; later polls read hardware again. Candidate and installed captures include successful subsequent periodic requests after reconnect. The roughly 0.51 s removed from the measured reconnect tail is supported by packet counts. Startup tails remain about223ms, including first-watch registration; do not interpret these results as eliminating all post-connect work. Baseline and candidate each had a startup model-response timeout and recovered automatically; those failed attempts remain in the evidence. The first harness launch preceded socket readiness and failed without touching the Printer; it was rerun after service startup. Installed observer log had zero warning/error/panic messages. Evidence: docs/assets/bridge-audit-083/live-benchmark.json and installed-ui-smoke.json. Raw journals remain private under host /tmp. Audit observer/drop-in/socket and candidate source/library/archive were removed; normal service restored before final health verification. Remaining setup costs include variable advertisement/GATT availability, the BLE handshake, model-query timeout recovery and initial watch registration. Further optimization should measure these boundaries without weakening status freshness or reconnect ownership.

Final normal service at 18:15:40 EDT: PID31925/manager31549 active, NRestarts0, Printer connected,600MHz powersave/GPIO24low,45.084°C, throttle0x0, GPIOv2, hotspot/USB and FTP220/200 healthy. docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Reduce the startup delay when the Printer does not answer the first ImageSupportInfo query. Preserve automatic reconnect, model-specific preparation/orientation, authoritative dimensions, command serialization and failed/cancelled session retirement. Hardware validation uses status requests and external disconnects only; no film.

docs.title: Approach and acceptance
docs.text:
Subagents implement and audit a single retry of this read-only capability request after a short first response window, within the original ten-second response budget. One command lock and delivery guard span both writes; terminal failure still retires the uncertain session. No actuating command is replayed. Model detection retains queried dimensions and validates known DIS identity conflicts. Ambiguous Link 3 hints fail safely instead of changing orientation.

Independent adversarial review covers late/duplicate replies, partial packets, no response, write failure, cancellation/disconnect, unrelated commands and model/hint conflicts. Compare baseline, candidate and installed warm startup, request counts, subsequent periodic freshness, automatic reconnect at 600 MHz and logs. Preserve failed attempts and radio variance. Run relevant local/ARM gates, deploy clean artifacts and restore normal service/remove owned fixtures.

Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W Rev1.0, ST7789 LCD, X306 battery; Debian13.2/Linux6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python3.13.5/BlueZ5.82. Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924. No physical film-quality claim.

docs.title: Source acceptance
docs.text:
Clean source b2b6c8c implements Transport::query_image_support. The production BLE transaction sends the eight-byte capability query, waits up to one second for its reply, and resends once only after a response timeout. Both writes and receives share the original ten-second total deadline, command lock and delivery guard. Healthy queries still send once. Write failures, confirmed disconnects and cancellation do not trigger replay. Terminal failure retires the uncertain session. Custom transports retain their existing transaction behavior.

Independent review found and fixed partial-frame retention when the outer first-response timer cancels receive before its inner cleanup. The assembler is reset before each model-query write, while queued complete notifications remain available. A real-channel regression combines an incomplete first reply, complete retry reply, duplicate model reply and fresh battery status. Late duplicate capability replies cannot satisfy status selectors.

Dimensions remain authoritative. ASCII-trimmed exact FI033 requires 600×800 and selects Mini Link 3; exact FI017 requires 800×800 Square. Conflicts and ambiguous formerly recognized Link 3 strings fail safely instead of changing orientation. Other unknown/missing hints use dimensions. DIS reads require the canonical service; normalization remains ASCII-only throughout. Model specifications, JPEG preparation, image bytes, transfer pacing and C ABI are unchanged.

Normal hooks passed 322 Rust tests plus 1 doctest, 1773 Bridge tests (27 existing warnings), Rust formatting, strict production workspace Clippy, Ruff and strict mypy (67 modules). Header drift and strict MkDocs passed. Independent core suite (196 tests) passed. Pi ARM tests: 8 model-query and 47 device tests. The first formatting gate caught a final concurrent formatting change; corrected and rerun through normal hooks. Source hashes and manifests are in source-validation.json.

docs.title: Hardware benchmark and deployment
docs.text:
Status-only checks completed on the hardware above, with no image/print commands or film. Warm startup timing below is first status attempt to first successful completion, not a cold boot measurement. Each successful request used three fresh status commands. Subsequent periodic requests also used three hardware reads, with advancing completion timestamps.

Run Initial status completion Model-query behavior Baseline1 3.673s Healthy, one query Baseline2 32.271s First query timed out; later connection recovered Candidate1 3.734s Healthy, one query Candidate2 3.703s Healthy, one query Candidate3 3.866s Healthy, one query Installed 4.326s Healthy, one query

The missed-first-reply case did not recur in the three candidate warm starts or installed startup. These observations do not measure live retry speedup or prove all startup timeouts are eliminated. Deterministic paused-time tests drop the first reply and return a model reply 140ms after resend: completion at 1.140s, exactly two queries and no third write. Silent links still reach the original ten-second deadline and retire safely. No DIS-only model shortcut is used. Baseline1 collection began after status was already ready; its original 14.669s collection latency is retained, but the table derives 3.673s from actual attempt timestamps.

Candidate and installed external-disconnect recovery took 11.828s and12.486s. Each included a scan miss followed by automatic recovery. All 33 observations in each run remained locked, not unlocking, at 600 MHz and camera-ready. Radio/discovery variation prevents a universal total reconnect speedup claim. Exact FI017/Square and MTU 247/payload 236 were retained. Installed same-button triple unlock, nonblank LCD at 1000 MHz, relock at 600 MHz and status pause/resume passed through production abstract input actions and the physical LCD; button contacts were not actuated. Physical film quality was not retested; model preparation byte/orientation tests passed.

Clean Python/native b2b6c8c deployed. FFI SHA256 9e31f99896ece2b687652bfdd0e80318a349cdb387c4e8c2d44ef35fa0d34031; CLI 1068fcb591c94e5a2b8bb888361230ade931b8da5b529528500c58edba4ce38e. Candidate and installed observer logs had zero matched warning/error/panic messages, including successful reconnect after scan misses. Baseline2 timeout remains recorded. Observer/drop-in/ socket, candidate library and owned ARM test binary removed; normal service restored.

Evidence under docs/assets/bridge-audit-084/: source validation, live benchmark, independent adversarial review, installed UI smoke, final health, cleanup and running-log review. Raw journals remain private. Remaining costs include advertisement/GATT availability, BLE handshake and initial watch registration. A future occurrence where both model replies are lost should retain its packet/connection trace before changing the retry or teardown policy.

Final normal service verified at 18:54:58 EDT: PID34446/manager34001 active, NRestarts0, Printer connected, 600 MHz powersave/GPIO24low,43.470°C/throttle0x0, GPIOv2, hotspot/USB/FTP220/200 healthy. Clean deployment/native manifests and loaded library hashes match b2b6c8c. Final normal log has zero matched warnings/errors/panics. Whole current-boot Bridge/manager service review covered 9294 records and retained 134 historical matched issue messages, including two earlier native panic episodes. Task084 baseline2 warnings are retained; candidate, installed observer and restored normal processes have no matched issues. No kernel-log claim. Independent source, hardware and final-health/log review passed. All owned fixtures, including the final health script, are removed. See final-health.json, cleanup.json, running-log-review.json and adversarial-review.json.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Reduce work needed to arm the initial Bluetooth disconnect watch while preserving automatic reconnect, fresh status and ownership during pause, printing, selection changes and shutdown. Hardware benchmarks use status requests and external disconnects only, with no film.

docs.title: Approach and acceptance
docs.text:
Reuse a complete Device1 identity snapshot maintained by authenticated BlueZ signals, scoped to the current bus, owner, generation and lifecycle. Fast arming requires an unambiguous live Printer identity; incomplete, invalidated or ambiguous state retains the bounded fresh-snapshot fallback. Signals received during snapshot resolution must win over older replies. Keep owned cleanup, bounded state and the periodic status fallback. Controller completion must still own its registration token and selected Printer identity before retaining the watch.

Subagents implement the agent and controller boundaries, with independent adversarial review of race, malformed-input, sender/identity, lifecycle and cancellation cases. Measure actual watch duration and snapshot calls separately from UI rendering and status completion. Compare baseline/candidate/installed startup and locked reconnect, preserve failures/radio variation, run path-scoped gates, deploy clean source and restore normal service/remove owned fixtures.

Hardware: Pi Zero2W Rev1.0/ST7789/X306; Debian13.2/Linux6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8/Python3.13.5/BlueZ5.82; Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924. No image/print commands or physical film-quality retest.

docs.title: Source acceptance
docs.text:
Clean 57e7db9 implements the bounded identity cache and registration ownership checks. Existing fresh GetManagedObjects calls seed Name/Alias/Connected identity fields. Authenticated signals maintain them, scoped to the agent lifecycle, bus and BlueZ owner. Fast arming requires one unique matching connected identity and a live shared bus. Missing, ambiguous, malformed, invalidated or disconnected-bus state retains the fresh bounded snapshot fallback. The cache is capped at 512 rows and adds no startup query/task or per-poll work. The bond-removal gate continues to read fresh state. Signal revisions prevent older replies restoring removed or changed identities. Stop and owner transitions clear reusable state.

Controller completion checks its registration token, current generation and selected address/ name before retaining the unsubscribe callback. A delayed obsolete result cannot replace a new watch. Source and independent tests cover snapshot/removal/readdition races, stale/spoofed senders, malformed/invalidation input, bus/owner/lifecycle changes, ambiguity, cancellation, stop, pause, print handoff, selection and newer same-generation ownership.

Normal hooks passed 1807 Bridge tests, 27 existing warnings, Ruff, strict mypy (67 modules) and touched formatting. Strict MkDocs passed. Producer agent/pairing (122 tests) and controller (270 tests) passed; independent affected suite (392 tests) plus 3 additional adversarial cases passed. No C ABI, native, config or sync schema changes. Native source b2b6c8c remains installed, FFI SHA256 9e31f99896ece2b687652bfdd0e80318a349cdb387c4e8c2d44ef35fa0d34031.

docs.title: Hardware acceptance
docs.text:
Watch registration is timed directly, with same-task snapshot spans attributed within each call. These are small samples on the hardware above, not estimates of whole boot or energy.

Registration Duration Extra snapshot reads Baseline startup1 10.984ms 1 Baseline startup2 13.524ms 1 Candidate startup 0.495ms 0 Installed startup 0.484ms 0 Baseline reconnect 31.172ms 1 Candidate reconnect 0.792ms 0 Installed reconnect, cache inconclusive 26.486ms 1 Installed pause/resume 0.541ms 0 Installed audit-only forced fallback 10.061ms 1

The initial fast path removes one snapshot and about 10–13ms from the measured registration. Natural installed reconnect used the safe fallback; zero-request registration is conditional. The audit-only fallback invalidated identity state, armed a temporary second watch, then unsubscribed immediately, leaving the production watch intact. Startup had one existing bond snapshot versus baseline two total reads. Later status requests still sent fresh selectors 1/2/3. All captured wire commands were status/model queries; no image/print commands or film used.

External-disconnect recovery took 11.824s baseline, 7.179s candidate and 12.588s installed. Baseline/installed each had a failed first scan before automatic recovery. All 32/15/35 accepted observations respectively remained locked, not unlocking, 600 MHz and camera-ready. Radio and scan variation prevent attributing full recovery differences to this millisecond optimization. Correct physical FA:AB:BC:C7:95:64 watch, fresh periodic polls, same-button triple unlock/nonblank LCD at 1000 MHz, relock at 600 MHz and status pause/resume passed. Abstract input used production controller/physical LCD; button contacts were not actuated. Physical print quality not retested; native image/printing code and artifacts are unchanged.

docs.title: Correction of prior timing attribution
docs.text:
The earlier plans/context attributed the roughly 223ms Connected→status-fetch-return tail to watch registration. The watch starts after fetch returns, so that attribution was incorrect. Candidate direct render instrumentation measured the NoFilm LCD render at 219.344ms inside that fetch. Historical measurements remain valid, but that tail measures rendering/status publication rather than watch setup. Visible LCD rendering is the larger remaining local cost.

The existing Plan084 model-query retry was incidentally exercised on hardware: candidate sent one capability query, received no reply during its first window, and resent 1.002s later. A matching reply arrived 186ms after resend (1.189s after first write), then fresh status completed on the same connection. Identical writes prevent assigning that reply to a particular request; this validates the live retry path without claiming the resend caused the response.

Clean Python 57e7db9 deployed; native unchanged. All observed task 085 service processes had zero matched warning/error/panic messages, including safe scan-miss recovery. Final normal service at 19:33:33 EDT: PID36582/manager36128 active/NRestarts0, Printer connected, 600 MHz powersave, 41.856°C/throttle0x0/GPIO24low/GPIOv2/hotspot/USB/FTP220/200 healthy; source/native hashes match clean manifests and the loaded production library. FTP probe uses the Pi's own hotspot address, not a wireless upload. Full current-boot Bridge/manager review covered 10681 records, retaining 134 historical matched messages including two earlier native panic episodes. No kernel-log claim. Observer/drop-in/socket/candidate archive/source and final health script removed.

Independent source, hardware and final health/log adversarial review passed. Evidence under docs/assets/bridge-audit-085/; raw journals remain private. Next measured local cost is visible LCD rendering (~220ms per changed frame); advertisement/GATT availability and BLE handshake also remain variable setup costs. Periodic status and safe fallback stay enabled.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Reduce display work while preserving exact pixels, button responsiveness, lock/unlock, backlight ordering and the shared physical/virtual LCD state machine. Hardware benchmarks use display/status operations only; no film.

docs.title: Approach and acceptance
docs.text:
Subagents optimize framebuffer RGB565 packing with existing Pillow operations and audit controller/render lifecycle. Keep synchronous frame ordering, existing deduplication and pixel restore before backlight activation. Independent review checks byte order, channel quantization, input modes/sizes, every UI state, image immutability, and failure paths.

Profile actual Pi frames by layout drawing, RGB565 packing, kernel framebuffer writes and backlight control, including main-thread CPU and event-loop stalls. Compare baseline, candidate and installed equivalent frames at 1000 MHz. Validate Linux GPIO mockup input through production code, same-button triple unlock, mixed-button reset, debounce, 10s abandonment, dark 600 MHz and awake 1000 MHz, framebuffer equality against the original scalar oracle, fresh status and reconnect. Preserve actual panel-scanout/contact/energy measurement limitations. Run all path-scoped gates, deploy clean source and restore normal service/remove owned fixtures.

Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / ST7789 / X306, Debian 13.2 / Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8 / Python 3.13.5 / BlueZ 5.82. Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924. No image/print commands or physical film-quality retest.

docs.title: Implementation and independent review
docs.text:
Clean source cac3318 replaces the Python per-pixel RGB565 loop with existing Pillow native band lookup/add/interleave operations. Channel fields are disjoint; addition cannot overflow. The two-byte LA container preserves low-byte/high-byte ordering without alpha interpretation. No new dependency or asynchronous frame queue. Existing redraw suppression, dark blanking, pixel restore before backlight, controller ordering and shared virtual renderer remain intact.

Independent review checked all 16,777,216 RGB colours, 17 Pillow modes, six zero/odd layouts and 40 light/dark UI snapshots: 64 byte-equivalence checks passed. All 456 independently run affected tests passed. Normal source gates: 1825 Bridge tests, 27 existing warnings, Ruff, strict mypy (67 modules), formatting and strict MkDocs passed. No native/C ABI/schema changes.

docs.title: Pi rendering benchmark
docs.text:
Eighteen equivalent frames per variant, six UI states repeated three times, actual /dev/fb1 at 1000 MHz. Synthetic Printing snapshots exercise display only; no Printer image commands.

Median milliseconds Baseline Candidate Installed Total render 267.376 45.810 41.830 Layout/text drawing 30.930 33.718 31.022 RGB565 packing 234.782 10.132 9.350 Kernel framebuffer write 0.342 0.376 0.365 Backlight operation 0.917 1.018 0.900 Rendering thread CPU 266.528 43.397 41.154

All 18 frame hashes match across all three variants. Installed total time fell 84.4% and rendering thread CPU fell 84.6%; these measure changed frames, not whole-device idle CPU, energy or battery runtime. Timing ends when the kernel framebuffer write returns, not panel scanout. Fonts/QR are already cached; layout/text drawing (~31 ms) is the next rendering cost.

Maximum heartbeat lag was 272.445/179.448/48.735 ms baseline/candidate/installed. Concurrent services were active, including BLE setup during candidate frames. These observations include other event-loop work and do not establish an isolated LCD or universal button-latency bound.

docs.title: Input, lock and reconnect validation
docs.text:
Baseline, candidate and installed each passed 11 checks using an owned Linux GPIO mockup controller through production input code, actual framebuffer/backlight and CPU tiers. Covered key 2 lock, rejected bounce/sub-50ms press, accepted 75ms wake, held key counted once, same-action/different-button reset, same joystick triple unlock, rapid key 1 triple unlock, 10s no-new-press abandonment to black/600 MHz and detached mock inactivity with physical GPIOv2 input still registered. Wake/home pixels matched the original scalar packing oracle; dark timeout checks intentionally require black pixels. Awake tier was 1000 MHz.

Queue-to-task-completion sample medians were 218.158/34.340/34.024 ms baseline/candidate/ installed. Initial state/action counts differ (18/15/15); these are descriptive observations, not controlled physical contact latency. Wake includes CPU transition work and can take longer. Physical contacts were not actuated; panel scanout was not measured.

Candidate/installed startup status was ready in 3.492/3.815s and subsequent periodic status remained fresh. Automatic recovery after external BlueZ Device1.Disconnect took 12.135/6.466s, with all 31/15 observations locked at 600 MHz and camera-ready, followed by new fresh status and a connected Printer. Advertisement/setup variation remains; no reconnect speedup is attributed to the LCD change. No image commands or film were used.

Native b2b6c8c unchanged; FFI SHA256 9e31f99896ece2b687652bfdd0e80318a349cdb387c4e8c2d44ef35fa0d34031 and CLI 1068fcb591c94e5a2b8bb888361230ade931b8da5b529528500c58edba4ce38e. Full current-boot Bridge/manager journal review: 11667 records, 136 matched issue messages. 135 were historical, including two earlier native panic episodes and a PID480 CRITICAL status-worker-stuck restart. The prior plan085 filter omitted CRITICAL; this audit includes it. No accompanying grace timeout or display/input fault. Full candidate/installed/normal process logs (249/231/36 records) have no matched warnings, errors, render/input failures or panics. This scope does not claim all kernel logs or historical faults are clean.

Evidence: audit assets. Exact framebuffer equivalence, input reliability, CPU tiers, fresh status, automatic reconnect and normal-service health pass; no film used. Remaining LCD work is layout/text drawing, subject to preserving exact output and avoiding delayed frames after lock. No extra optimization is claimed for BLE setup.

docs.title: Bridge LCD text and layout drawing
Goal and acceptance
docs.text:
Reduce text/layout CPU time while preserving exact display pixels, font fallback, clipping, language/font/theme changes, current animation clocks, button responsiveness and reliable same-button triple unlock with 10s abandonment. Physical and virtual LCDs keep one synchronous renderer and state machine. No image/print commands or film during hardware validation.

Subagents profile and implement bounded text reuse, audit renderer/controller lifecycle, and independently compare original/candidate output across UI modes, themes, font sizes, English/Chinese strings, clock phases, transitions and difficult clipping. Include cold/warm work, bounded cache memory and concurrent virtual/physical rendering in acceptance.

Pi benchmark: actual framebuffer draw/pack/write/backlight spans at 1000 MHz, equivalent baseline/candidate/installed frames, main-thread CPU and event-loop observations. Kernel GPIO mockup tests exercise production button queues, actual LCD and 600/1000 MHz tiers. Physical contacts and panel scanout are not measured. Fresh status and automatic reconnect remain required when the Printer is available. Deploy clean reviewed source, restore normal service, remove owned fixtures and review running logs including CRITICAL messages.

Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / ST7789 / X306, Debian 13.2, Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82. Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924.

docs.title: Implementation and source review
docs.text:
Clean source 06bbe86 adds bounded LRU caches for text bounding boxes (512 entries), grayscale masks (256 entries) and variation capability (32 entries). Mask pixels cap at 256 × 240 × 48 bytes, below 3 MiB; font, text and cache metadata overhead are additional. Keys retain actual resolved font and underlying font core, text and anchor. Direct text calls keep their original font choice; CJK fallback resolves before caching where it did previously.

Each frame still resolves current layout, theme, clipping, coordinates and animation clock. Private grayscale masks use Pillow's bitmap route, preserving antialiasing rounding on coloured backgrounds. Output images remain independent. Variable fonts, multiline/long text, oversized masks, fractional coordinates and unsupported image/font modes use original drawing. No new dependency, asynchronous frame queue, controller/GPIO/framebuffer/Bluetooth/config/C ABI change.

Subagents implemented and audited. Frozen renderer SHA256 df10cadf41ea34c9b3baabcd5edcb08b75764804fda851151a4f6c60ebed7775 independently passed 1303 pixel/behavior/cache checks against the original e895b44 renderer, plus 80 concurrent frames and 454 existing affected tests. Producer 220 tests and runtime audit 136 tests pass. Normal gates: 1926 Bridge tests, 27 existing warnings, Ruff, touched-file formatting, strict mypy (67 modules) and strict MkDocs pass.

docs.title: Pi rendering benchmark
docs.text:
Eighteen equivalent actual framebuffer renders per variant, six states repeated three times, 1000 MHz with fonts/text warmed. All 18 framebuffer byte hashes identical across variants.

Median milliseconds Baseline Candidate Installed Total render 42.092 18.576 13.994 Layout/text drawing 31.158 3.656 2.663 RGB565 packing 9.502 11.662 9.873 Rendering thread CPU 41.417 15.600 13.728

Installed total rendering fell 66.8%, layout/text 91.5%, and rendering thread CPU 66.9%. These are changed-frame samples, not whole-device idle CPU, energy or battery runtime. Timing ends at kernel write completion, not panel scanout. Normal concurrent services were active; BLE setup overlapped candidate measurements. Heartbeat maxima 48.523/157.346/18.683 ms include unrelated work, so do not attribute all lag or guarantee button latency from these.

The first baseline trial overlapped GPIO/profile operations; a clock assertion rejected its mixed 600/1000 MHz samples. Those results were excluded and replaced by the sequential, fixed-1000-MHz baseline above. No failed trial is included in accepted result files.

A separate fixed-clock draw-only experiment clears added text caches before each of six states, then repeats immediately. Fonts are already loaded, and the frozen original renderer runs as an RGB oracle in the same process. Candidate cold/warm medians 26.045/2.743 ms versus original 29.160/29.034 ms; installed 27.013/2.899 ms versus original 30.263/30.019 ms. All 12 frames per variant match original RGB pixels. This is glyph-cache-cold work, not a font-disk-cold startup benchmark. The main improvement is repeated text reuse.

An additional Pi draw-only matrix checks 240 frames: all 20 modes, light/dark, English/Chinese, three font sizes, using actual installed font files. Every RGB frame matches the frozen original and preview pixels remain unchanged. No framebuffer/Printer operations in this matrix.

docs.title: Input and automatic reconnect
docs.text:
Baseline/candidate/installed each pass all 11 Linux GPIO mockup checks through production input, controller and actual LCD. Covered key 2 lock, bounce/sub-50ms rejection, accepted 75ms wake, held button counted once, mixed-button reset, same-button joystick triple unlock, rapid key 1 triple unlock, 10s no-new-accepted-press timeout, black/600 MHz abandonment and detached mock inactivity with physical GPIOv2 reader still registered. Awake tier is 1000 MHz, and wake/home framebuffer pixels match the frozen original renderer plus scalar RGB565 oracle.

Queue-to-task-completion sample medians 34.454/16.643/16.670 ms have differing initial states and action counts (15/15/18). They are descriptive production-queue observations, excluding physical contact and panel latency. Wake also includes CPU-tier transition work.

Candidate/installed initial status 3.534/3.910s, with subsequent fresh periodic reads. The Printer was initially off in baseline; its first-attempt-to-ready 123.760s includes an availability wait and is not a boot or connection benchmark. Successful status-attempt spans are recorded separately. Baseline/candidate/installed automatic recovery 8.848/12.463/6.650s; all 21/32/15 observations locked at 600 MHz and camera-ready, final BlueZ connected and a new fresh status. BLE advertisement/setup variation remains; no recovery speedup is attributed to the text caches. No image/print commands or film.

docs.text:

Native b2b6c8c unchanged: FFI SHA256 9e31f99896ece2b687652bfdd0e80318a349cdb387c4e8c2d44ef35fa0d34031, CLI 1068fcb591c94e5a2b8bb888361230ade931b8da5b529528500c58edba4ce38e. The expanded filter includes ANSI-stripped Python/Rust WARN/WARNING/ERROR/CRITICAL/FATAL and journald priority 0–3. It adds eight historical systemd startup-failure records to the earlier 136 matches; those records, two old native panic episodes, an old CRITICAL worker-stuck restart and prior task086 shutdown cancellation warning remain explicit. Raw journals retained privately; no kernel-log cleanliness claim.

Evidence: audit assets. Exact display output, button and unlock reliability, CPU tiers, fresh status and automatic reconnect pass with no film used. Framebuffer RGB565 packing (~10 ms per changed frame) is now the largest measured rendering cost. Cache reuse improves changed-frame drawing; no whole-boot or battery-runtime claim.

docs.title: Goal and acceptance
docs.text:
Reduce changed-frame framebuffer packing CPU while preserving exact little-endian RGB565 quantization, pixel order and input conversion. Synchronous frames, pixels-before-backlight, button responsiveness, same-button triple unlock and 10s timeout/600MHz idle remain intact. No image/print commands or film during validation.

Subagents implement/profile, audit runtime/dependency/lifecycle, and independently review all RGB colours, Pillow modes/dimensions/concurrency/memory/fallback. Compare Pi baseline, candidate and installed equivalent actual framebuffer frames at 1000 MHz, and first-frame backend initialization. Existing NumPy supplied by RAW dependencies is optional; its import must not block first framebuffer paints or lock blanking. Retain the exact Pillow path while an owned background preload, scheduled after the first successful paint, prepares the backend and in minimal/no-event-loop runtimes.

Pi alternatives measured separately: Pillow 9.859 ms, byte-output 4.722 ms, word-expression 4.222 ms and word-output 3.160 ms per 240×240 frame, identical bytes (100 rounds). Chosen word-output uses explicit little-endian uint16 output plus local scratch. Fresh NumPy import 531.424 ms wall/858.105 ms CPU and ~15.4 MiB peak RSS increase with filesystem pagecache already warm; production first-paint behavior requires a separate gate.

Validate owned preload completion/failure/close/cancellation, kernel GPIO mockup through production input/controller and real LCD/CPU, fresh status and automatic reconnect. Deploy clean reviewed source, restore normal entrypoint, remove owned fixtures and review full running logs including native severity labels and journald priority errors.

Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W Rev1.0 / ST7789 / X306, Debian13.2/Linux6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python3.13.5/BlueZ5.82/NumPy2.4.6, Instax Link Square INSTAX-52006924. Measurements do not claim contact-to-photon latency, physical scanout or battery lifetime.

docs.title: Implementation and adversarial review
docs.text:
Final clean source 398dde5 uses optional NumPy already pinned through RAW dependencies. Exact uint16 output (<u2) plus one local uint16 scratch array replaces repeated Pillow band operations after loading. RGB export, quantization and little-endian row/pixel order remain exact. Buffers are per-call and the returned bytes immutable; traced 240×240 peak ~519 KiB excludes Pillow native storage. 1000 repeated packs retained ~760 traced bytes. NumPy module memory is additional; standalone fresh-process import increased peak RSS by ~15.4 MiB.

The display constructor creates no preload task. First successful frame write/backlight finishes before one owned asyncio.to_thread import task starts. Frames and black blanking use the ready callable synchronously, initially exact Pillow. Success switches only while open; close cancels the task, and the worker never mutates the display. Missing NumPy keeps a quiet cached fallback; unexpected loader failures warn once without interrupting frames. Failed first writes/backlight do not start loading; no-loop boot splash uses Pillow without NumPy.

Review found and fixed first-paint import contention in the provisional constructor-start variant. Final display SHA256 608d52b29c5b4aad4c116fd0e63111b4f6155dfa81e26ab2fe679513ac17af1a. Packing arithmetic was exhaustively validated for all 16,777,216 RGB colours on the preceding hash and is unchanged by the final post-paint scheduling delta. 71 additional mode/size/frame/ mutation/concurrency checks, independent blocked-worker lifecycle cases and 594 affected tests pass. Producer 63 display tests/runtime audit 122 pass. Normal 1956 Bridge tests, 27 existing warnings, Ruff, touched formatting, strict mypy 67 modules and strict MkDocs pass. No dependency/C ABI/native/config/schema changes.

docs.title: Settled Pi rendering and first paint
docs.text:
Eighteen equivalent actual framebuffer frames per variant at 1000 MHz, six states repeated three times after warming/settling. All 18 framebuffer hashes match across variants.
