Median milliseconds Baseline Candidate Installed Total render 14.121 7.905 7.784 Text/layout draw 2.682 2.813 2.742 RGB565 pack 9.852 3.186 3.311 Kernel write 0.361 0.425 0.402 Backlight 0.943 0.974 0.992 Rendering thread CPU 13.772 7.513 7.479

Installed packing fell 66.4%, total rendering 44.9% and rendering thread CPU 45.7%. This is changed-frame work, not whole-device idle CPU, energy or battery runtime. Timings end at kernel write/backlight return, not panel scanout. Maximum heartbeat lag 18.826/11.382/13.020 ms captures other loop activity too and is not a physical button latency guarantee.

First-frame render 129.009/128.165/149.037 ms baseline/candidate/installed; first hashes identical. Candidate and installed first paint finish before loader start, then NumPy becomes ready about 1.486/1.468s later while frames retain Pillow. Warm service ExecStart-to-first completion 2.729/2.758/2.398s with prebaked bytecode and filesystem pagecache warm; no power-on boot or universal startup-speed claim. Installed first-frame variation is retained explicitly.

Early uncompiled/provisional measurements overlapped startup/import work and were replaced by settled, prebaked comparisons. Raw preliminary results retained privately. First GPIO fixture attempt at Booting was rejected before input and its owned module unloaded; the fixture now waits for startup to finish, and all subsequent cases pass.

docs.title: Input validation
docs.text:
Baseline/candidate/installed each pass 11 owned kernel GPIO mockup cases through production input/controller and actual LCD. Debounce/short rejection, held-once, 75ms accepted/rapid presses, same-button triple unlock, mixed-button reset, nonblank wake, 10s no-new-press timeout to black/600 MHz and awake 1000 MHz preserved. Frame pixels match the frozen renderer plus independent scalar RGB565 oracle. Mock detach leaves physical GPIOv2 input registered.

Queue-to-task-completion medians 16.502/10.299/11.952 ms, with action counts 18/15/18 and varying initial states, are descriptive only. Physical contacts and scanout were not measured. No image/print commands or film.

docs.title: Installed status and reconnect
docs.text:
The Printer was initially unavailable: candidate status wait timed out after 100s without a fresh result. This is retained; no candidate reconnect success claimed. After the user turned it on, installed successful status-attempt duration was 3.443s and subsequent periodic reads were fresh. Availability-inclusive first-to-ready 243.459s includes the powered-off wait and must not be interpreted as a boot/setup benchmark.

Installed automatic recovery from external BlueZ Device1.Disconnect took 11.649s, all 31 observations locked at 600 MHz and camera-ready, final BlueZ connected with new fresh status. No manual Reconnect, image commands or film. Advertisement/setup timing remains variable; no recovery-speed attribution to RGB565 packing.

docs.title: Deployment, normal health and running logs
docs.text:
Clean Python 398dde5 installed with native b2b6c8c unchanged. FFI SHA256 9e31f99896ece2b687652bfdd0e80318a349cdb387c4e8c2d44ef35fa0d34031 and CLI 1068fcb591c94e5a2b8bb888361230ade931b8da5b529528500c58edba4ce38e verified; loaded library mapping and reviewed source hashes match. Candidate and installed independent LCD reviews passed, then installed Printer status/reconnect and final normal health/log/cleanup reviews passed.

Normal service restored at 22:12 EDT. Final health 22:14:50 EDT: Bridge PID43539/manager43015 active, zero restarts, Printer connected, 600 MHz powersave, 44.008°C/throttle0x0, GPIO24 low/GPIOv2, hotspot/USB and FTP220/200 healthy. FTP probe uses the Pi hotspot address locally; no wireless airtime/camera upload measured. All owned observer/drop-in/socket/mockup/ source archives/oracle/scripts/bytecode/health fixtures removed, private raw evidence retained.

Full current-boot Bridge/manager review: 14728 records, 146 matched messages, including 144 historical faults and two baseline shutdown status_cancel_waiting_for_worker warnings at requested restarts while the Printer was unavailable. No accompanying grace-expired, worker-stuck, display or input faults. Earlier native panic/CRITICAL/systemd failure records retained; historical plans unchanged. Provisional/final candidate/installed/normal logs (192/246/515/51 records) contain no matched warnings/errors/render/input/packer failures or panics. Filter includes ANSI-stripped Python/Rust severity labels and journald priority0–3; no kernel-log cleanliness claim.

Evidence: audit assets. No film used. NumPy's measured initialization/RSS tradeoff is explicit; first paint and synchronous ordering are preserved. Remaining local rendering costs are packing (~3.3ms), text/layout (~2.7ms) and backlight (~1ms) per changed frame; further changes should preserve measured startup and pixel equality.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Install the existing optimized build, independently audit every optimization in plans 057–088, fix the findings, review the fixes independently, and deploy the validated result. Each of the 32 plans has its own fresh subagent review of the same clean baseline, c4a2787. The code stayed unchanged until those reviews finished. Review results and exact focused checks are retained in docs/assets/bridge-audit-089/individual-audits.json; overlapping test counts are not additive.

No film, image download or actuator command is needed for hardware acceptance. This work does not measure battery runtime, wireless camera airtime, mechanical print duration or developed-film quality. Existing print-byte, quality and orientation evidence remains bounded to its original Printer models and photos. No Rust source, FFI header, image transformation, Bluetooth fragment size or pacing policy changes are planned.

docs.title: Findings and fixes
docs.text:
Area Audit Correction CPU policy 057, 058 Retry transient governor failures autonomously with capped backoff and coalesced warnings. Invalidate cached state before external writes, including partial or cancelled writes. CPU shutdown Fresh review Join the owned governor restoration through repeated cancellation before propagating cancellation. Saved Looks 060 Persist/load clamped vignette; legacy files default to zero. Round hue's inverse scale to preserve every valid UI value. Error footer 059 Sync errors show KEY3 iPhone, matching the actual action. Lost input 062, 077, fresh review Discard uncertain buffered input, balance queue accounting and relock before a new unlock sequence. Apply to queue overflow, kernel sequence gaps and failed resynchronization/backend fallback. Physical and remote inputs share this behavior. Review duration 066 Start the selected interval after the first timed photo frame finishes rendering. Manual confirmation and immediate printing retain their separate behavior. About details 067 Identify value dialogs by their information key and refresh them after collection. Explanatory Help remains unchanged. Hidden About work 075 Avoid collection behind the locked/unlock overlay; collect once the page is visible. Metadata ownership 068, follow-up Shield/join the EXIF thread before releasing preview or sender ownership, including repeated cancellation. Accepted print parameters 072 Freeze live UI configuration after confirmation, before consuming prepared bytes. Selection, sender options and detected-model fallback use that same accepted configuration. The captured upload destination stays fixed. Sync originals 068 Copy new spool originals to independent inodes. Atomically detach persisted legacy links. Legacy incoming files Upgrade review Detach a shared incoming inode before FTP opens it for writing, including the period before deferred Sync initialization. Preserve append/resume content. Outbox publication Storage failure follow-up Commit a staged index before publishing arrivals or deleting evicted/acknowledged originals. Failed index writes preserve the committed queue; readers remain responsive during publication. FTP overflow 069 Retain source ownership through rejected-photo deletion, including errors and multiple owners. Shutdown admission 070 Close FTP admission when shutdown is observed, before joining active photo cleanup. Resource shutdown 067 Run every ordered cleanup after an individual resource fails, then report the failure. An input-close failure also preserves Printer/provider/display cleanup. Backlight ownership 086 Close the owned GPIO fallback exactly once. Manager responsiveness 067 Collect HTTP information off the event loop; share a bounded stable-info cache and serialize CPU sampling. Firmware operations invalidate cached versions. Config, pairing and metrics remain fresh. Snapshot freshness 078, 081 Retry a superseded snapshot once and refuse uncertain results; protect consumers as well as the cache. Watch authentication/bounds 085 Require the captured authenticated owner for snapshot seeds; abandon an overflowing pending watch and retain polling fallback. Bond removal targets 082, fresh review Validate the exact deletion set, never enlarge it from a later inventory. Check the next CLI target last, immediately before dispatching removal. Removal result Fresh review Count successful removals only. Failed-only batches do not retire the native session. Recovery logging 080 Log the transition from retaining a session to disconnecting it; suppress repeated observations with the same disposition.

The live-link guard is a fresh check immediately before dispatch, not an atomic transaction with BlueZ. A state change after dispatch cannot be prevented by application-side checks. Legacy spool migration fails closed if the filesystem cannot create an independent file: originals and index remain retained, the failure is logged, and Sync requires a successful restart. No claim is made that a disk failure can be repaired without sufficient writable storage.

docs.title: Independent validation
docs.text:
The initial audits include malformed JPEG/C ABI checks, complete RGB565 color-space comparisons, original-renderer pixel comparisons, real local FTP transfers, held-worker cancellation, controlled governor failures, D-Bus reply/signal interleavings and reconnect ownership. Linux-only Rust transport execution is explicitly distinguished from macOS host tests. Each report records its limitations; historical hardware observations are not presented as new measurements.

Fixes have separate fresh reviews for power/presets, Bluetooth, files/manager and interface/input. Review failures are retained along with their resolutions rather than omitted from the record. The final path-scoped gates, clean source revision, device acceptance and normal-service state will be recorded after they finish.

The full Python formatting gate also exposed 13 unchanged baseline files. Their formatting is polished in this round; independent AST comparisons confirm all 13 preserve the baseline code.

docs.title: Initial installed measurements
docs.text:
The clean baseline was installed with the standard deployment script. A normal dark/offline 30.056-second sample at 600 MHz used 0.46 process-thread CPU seconds, about 1.53% of one core. This excludes system/child-process CPU and is not an energy measurement. On the real ST7789, 18 fixed awake frames at 1000 MHz had median render time 7.627 ms, with packing 3.204 ms and thread CPU 7.385 ms. These are controlled frame measurements, not a full-print timing claim.

All available current-boot Bridge/manager service logs and kernel logs were copied privately and classified. At the initial review, 14,796 service records included 144 historical flagged records and no warning/error from the installed baseline process. The 626 kernel records included 177 brcmfmac vendor-IE errors, five early multimedia initialization failures and one earlier HCI connection-timeout warning. These precede this audit's installation and are retained historical driver/firmware findings; this application polish does not claim to repair their kernel causes. Raw journals remain private; only count inventories are committed.

docs.title: Final local gates and installed acceptance
docs.text:
Clean source 6a60165ae7993722a034e9389e0516db1819df85 passed the normal commit hooks: 2,269 Bridge tests, 27 existing warnings, Ruff, all 152 Python files formatted, and strict mypy on 67 source files. Strict MkDocs passed. The first full run exposed an old cancellation test that expected its EXIF reader to outlive its owner; it now requires joined cleanup while proving input remains responsive. Four independent fix reviews have no remaining scoped findings, including the later transactional outbox changes. Their histories remain in polish-reviews.json.

Installed on Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0 / ST7789 240×240 / X306 2300 mAh; Debian 13.2, Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82 and NumPy 2.4.6. All 67 installed Python source hashes match the clean commit. Native source remains b2b6c8c; the existing FFI SHA 9e31f99896ece2b687652bfdd0e80318a349cdb387c4e8c2d44ef35fa0d34031 and CLI SHA 1068fcb591c94e5a2b8bb888361230ade931b8da5b529528500c58edba4ce38e are unchanged.

  • Eleven real kernel GPIO-mockup cases through the production action queue passed bounce, held/mixed controls, 75 ms presses, triple unlock, ten-second abandonment, framebuffer restoration and 600/1000 MHz policy. Physical switch contacts were not actuated. The slowest observed unlock frame write completed 52.2 ms after accepted input. Queue completion can include governor warmup (maximum 400.2 ms); it is not a pure display-latency measurement.
  • A one-shot governor failure recovered autonomously in 0.337 s. Cancellation after the real helper wrote performance restored the locked board to powersave/600 MHz, with no photo work begun. The intentional warning and traceback remain in the test journal.
  • Eighteen awake frames matched every baseline RGB565 byte. Median render 7.627 → 7.703 ms, thread CPU 7.385 → 7.320 ms; this small sample does not establish a rendering speedup.
  • Installed file-ownership tests used synthetic files on the Pi filesystem: separate spool inodes/checksums, failed add/ACK publication retaining the committed index/original, legacy pre-open detachment and reload migration all passed. No production camera upload was made.
  • Eight concurrent real manager hello requests had median 326.1 ms including a shared cold collection; fifteen concurrent time requests had median 5.71 ms, maximum 50.46 ms. No manager delay was injected; these are HTTP responsiveness observations, not CPU/energy measurements.
  • Normal production dark/offline runtime at 600 MHz used 0.37 CPU seconds / 30.029 seconds, about 1.23% of one core, versus 1.53% in the initial 30-second sample. Neither sample used an observer. Short samples and scan phase limit comparison; no battery/energy result is claimed.

Normal Bridge/manager PIDs 45900/45198 are active, NRestarts 0, with powersave/600 MHz, no throttling, FTP 220/200 on the Pi hotspot address and no normal-runtime warning/error or input fallback. Removed the owned observer, runtime drop-in/socket, GPIO mockup and helper scripts. The final complete available service journal has 15,172 records / 148 flagged records: 144 historical, two bounded status-worker cancellation waits during test restarts, and the two intentional governor fault records. The normal restored process has zero flagged records. The kernel journal has 637 records / 193 flagged records: 187 vendor-IE errors (ten additional ones during service reconfiguration), five early multimedia failures and the same historical HCI timeout warning; no new HCI warning. AP/FTP operation remains healthy. Driver causes are recorded maintenance limits, not claimed repaired by these changes.

Initially pending hardware gate (resolved by the follow-up below): INSTAX-52006924 was not advertising during the initial round. Its power-on was requested; no film was consumed and no actual Printer disconnect/reconnect test is claimed. Source/mock safety and freshness tests passed, including both selection backends, current-owner identity changes and failed removal commands. Repeat the installed status-only reconnect check when the Printer is available.

docs.title: 2026-10-14 live status-only follow-up
docs.text:
The normal installed Bridge automatically found INSTAX-52006924 when the user turned it on, while the board was already in powersave at 600 MHz. Printer status reported Square, film 0, battery 80%. The same Pi/OS/native artifacts listed above were used; no image, download, print, LED-test or other actuator command was dispatched, and no film was consumed.

An observer around the installed production controller measured external BlueZ Device1.Disconnect recovery with no manual Reconnect action. Source 6a60165 recovered in 12.373 s, remaining locked at 600 MHz with camera receive readiness true and the same PID. This trace exposed a published-state inconsistency: the successful-status timestamp was invalidated by the event, but live_snapshot.printer_status_fresh remained true until a later dark-screen maintenance tick. The saved pre-fix trace includes this failure rather than presenting the entire test as a correctness pass.

Clean source 4145e771e4c2f46ff4d2fa06c654666b5a3878de fixes the disconnect callback to publish stale status immediately and wake the render converger. The callback performs no Bluetooth or display I/O; cleanup and reconnect remain in the serialized poll. Current watch-token, generation and selected-identity guards still reject stale callbacks. Existing in-flight reply protection prevents a pre-drop ACK from restoring readiness. A fresh independent review was clear with 27 relevant tests; added awake/locked, stale-callback and pending-reply assertions passed the normal hooks: 2,270 Bridge tests, 27 existing warnings, Ruff and mypy on 67 source files. Both changed Python files pass formatting. All 67 installed source hashes match the clean new commit; native FFI/CLI hashes are unchanged.

The final installed reconnect passed in 10.887 s from Disconnect dispatch to sampled fresh status. The disconnect signal arrived at 2.118 s; the serialized reconnect fetch began 0.466 s after that event. All sampled states remained locked at 600 MHz, with camera receive readiness true, the same PID 47347, no retired status task, and stale published status whenever the success timestamp was invalid. Recovery obtained a new successful status and rearmed exactly one disconnect watch. Timing includes BlueZ link teardown, radio discovery and protocol setup; radio availability was not controlled. These two runs do not establish a transport speedup from the freshness fix.

Three presses of the same KEY2 action unlocked to a nonblank physical framebuffer and 1000 MHz; KEY2 relocked at 600 MHz. Status pause/resume removed/rearmed the watch and restored fresh status while locked. These actions used the shared production action queue; physical switch contacts were not actuated. The retained photo/film verification from earlier rounds was not repeated. Sanitized traces and review/source-integrity evidence are in docs/assets/bridge-audit-089/live-*.json.

Final normal services are Bridge/manager 47710/47345, active with NRestarts 0. The Printer is connected, board powersave/600 MHz, GPIO24 low, temperature 42.932°C and throttle 0x0. Hotspot-address FTP returned 220/200; no working cache, input/network fallback, mockup or observer drop-in/socket remains. Owned helper scripts, outputs and bytecode were removed.

The complete available current-boot service journal now contains 15,434 records. All 262 records added since the prior final capture were reviewed, with zero new warning/error/panic records. The expanded severity/priority/panic predicate marks 150 records, all previously present (including two historical unwrap lines omitted by the earlier count of 148). The old normal process, both follow-up observers, and final normal Bridge/manager have zero flags. One transient not-advertising INFO in the first disconnect test recovered on the next bounded retry; the final test recovered on its first scan. The 644 kernel records include 199 flags: six additional brcmfmac vendor-IE errors occurred during the three service reconfigurations; there is no new HCI fault. The known driver/firmware limitations remain, with AP/FTP healthy. No further application defect was identified in this follow-up. Raw logs remain private; live-log-inventory.json records counts and the exact predicate.

docs.title: Bridge Wi-Fi driver errors and hotspot continuity
Goal and scope
docs.text:
Investigate the remaining brcmf_vif_set_mgmt_ie: vndr ie set error : -52 records, remove avoidable hotspot disruption, and preserve camera FTP and automatic Printer reconnect. Baseline source is 3230a5c, with runtime 4145e77 installed. Use no film or image/actuator commands on the Printer. Independent agents cover driver sources, runtime/helper lifecycle, benchmark isolation and adversarial review. Root owns all Pi mutations.

Hardware: Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0, BCM43430/1 Wi-Fi firmware 7.45.96.s1 (June 14, 2023, FWID 01-70bd2af7 es7), Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, NetworkManager 1.52.1, wpa_supplicant 2.10, BlueZ 5.82. Printer: INSTAX-52006924, Link Square. GPIO/LCD and native FFI/CLI remain the previously verified configuration. Kernel BRCM tracing is not enabled.

docs.title: Driver evidence
docs.text:
• The driver maps any negative firmware reply to Linux -EBADE (52); this message cannot identify the specific firmware rejection. Raspberry Pi fwil.c.
  • Initial source inspection found AP teardown resets firmware before clearing cached management IEs. Later scalar entry/return probes narrowed the residual failure to brcmf_cfg80211_stop_ap clearing probe-request IEs (pktflag=0x10, length 0, return -52). Scan calls with that flag returned 0. No pointers, IE payloads or key material were traced. Raspberry Pi cfg80211.c.
  • The accepted upstream correction, aba23b0, clears association-response IEs for AP teardown and retains probe-request cleanup for other modes. Beacon/probe-response cleanup is unchanged. The installed Raspberry Pi 6.12.47 source lacks this correction. Disabling P2P reduced scan IE length from 150 to 24 bytes but did not remove the failure; that diagnostic configuration is not a production fix.
  • NetworkManager translates disabled WPS into wps_disabled=1. Supplicant normally enables WPS for WPA2-Personal APs unless disabled. Existing WPA2-PSK authentication can remain while unused enrollment advertisement is disabled. NetworkManager 1.52.1, wpa_supplicant 2.10 source archive.

docs.title: Application findings and design
docs.text:
Every Bridge startup applies the saved FTP mode. The old hotspot helper modifies the profile and activates it even when the correct AP is already healthy. NetworkManager logs show new-activation, AP-DISABLED/AP-ENABLED, address loss and dnsmasq restart. These correlate with the paired kernel errors. Runtime recovery already has generation/job guards; a Python-only skip based on an IP address would ignore configuration drift.

The helper should retain an AP only after checking exact selected UUID, desired saved and applied settings, live address, NetworkManager owner, activation identity and applied version. Applied settings omit secrets, so a root-private per-boot stamp must bind the desired PSK digest to a successful helper activation. Unknown/untrusted/malformed state or failed probes must use the existing activation/recovery path. Root helper mutations are serialized. Keep radio-off, home transitions, missing-interface driver recovery, SSID/PIN/channel reconciliation and cancellation operational. Disable WPS while retaining the same WPA2-PSK/RSN/CCMP settings.

The independent review identified cancellation ownership lost through a foreground pipeline. Direct stdin redirection keeps the owned child in the main shell. The audit also found that background commands without explicit stdin inheritance read /dev/null, affecting activation stamping and newly generated PIN writes. Validate these with actual Bash/worker/lock tests; mocked command results alone cannot establish shell process ownership.

docs.title: Baseline and controlled WPS experiment
docs.text:
An initial isolated 32 MiB × four-file fixture exhausted the Pi's /tmp tmpfs and could not write its report. Its temporary inputs were cleaned; no production storage fault or result is claimed. The corrected fixture uses SD-backed /var/tmp, storage preflight, streaming checksums and reporting after cleanup.

A separate instance of the installed FTP receiver accepts synthetic 8 MiB JPEG transport files on an alternate port/private root with a checksum-only queue consumer. It cannot dispatch a production print. One unpaced and three paced uploads overlap repeated hotspot calls. This same-Pi hotspot-address path exercises receiver/SD/service behavior, not wireless airtime. Pacing is included in the continuity timing and must not be called camera throughput. Production FTP greeting/NOOP probes run alongside NetworkManager, USB, service and BlueZ observations.

Phase Three helper times, median Errors per call Production FTP probe failures Upload checksums Original helper, default WPS 3.742 s 2 / 2 / 2 9 Four pass Original helper, disabled WPS 3.744 s 2 / 0 / 0 9 Four pass

The first disabled-WPS call tears down the previously advertised WPS AP; subsequent actual reactivations produced no vendor-IE error. This is a measured configuration improvement, not a kernel patch or decoded firmware error. Reactivation still interrupts FTP probes, so WPS alone does not resolve continuity. All four transfers in each corrected phase completed with identical checksums. Unpaced single-transfer timings are retained but are not a radio throughput comparison. Sampling commands are serial; maximum sample spans were about 0.45 s, so no 250 ms gap-detection claim is made.

The Printer stopped advertising at 07:50:18, before the first fixture began at 07:52:49. These early phases do not establish connected Printer retention. The user has powered it on again for the final locked/status-only acceptance checks. Evidence is retained under docs/assets/bridge-audit-090/; raw logs and credentials remain private.

docs.title: Reviewed candidate
docs.text:
The final helper SHA is 736cf4ba661859b16e8f9ebf49cdd289bca7e062b33e91957a6ff925572afed2. Independent review cleared 76 targeted tests, including eight actual Bash cancellation/lock cases and additional PIN creation/preservation/override/permission checks. The implementation agent passed 110 affected tests. PSK preparation now owns its commands in the main shell; value retrieval is read-only. The review record retains both cancellation findings/resolutions.

The first unknown-stamp apply took 6.079 s, including verification; this is not boot timing. Three verified repeat calls had median 2.187 s, retained one activation object path, produced zero vendor-IE errors and zero production FTP probe failures. All four 8 MiB uploads completed/checksummed. All 45 samples kept the Printer connected with fresh status, film 0, camera readiness true, screen locked and board 600 MHz, with no retired status task. Maximum serial monitor span was 0.407 s. Paced transfers took about 7.86 s instead of 9.35 s under AP reactivation; the deliberate pace and local address path preclude radio speed claims. The unpaced single-transfer result (50.54 MiB/s versus baseline 50.11) does not establish a throughput change.

docs.title: Application deployment and residual driver gate
docs.text:
Clean source 982d8c6 was installed, including the separately installed privileged helper. All 67 Python file hashes match committed source; helper copies match the reviewed SHA; native Printer artifacts are unchanged. The complete Bridge suite passed 2,339 tests, Ruff, strict mypy and Bash syntax gates. Strict docs also passed.

The installed helper repeat took 2.144 s with zero vendor errors and production FTP probe outages; two isolated 8 MiB receives passed checksums. The Printer was offline for that trial. Automatic hotspot recovery after external NetworkManager connection-down took 35.020 s with the Printer offline, then 32.349 s with all samples retaining the connected Printer, locked screen, 600 MHz and the same Bridge PID. The healthy-state recovery grace is 30 s. The connected trial still emitted one vendor-IE error after a preceding radio cycle. Status-only Bluetooth disconnect/reconnect passed in 9.547 s with freshness invalidation, one disconnect watch, no retired status tasks, camera readiness and lock retained.

Radio-off/restore recovered functional AP and FTP service, but failed the zero-vendor-error gate. WPS removal resolves the measured paired advertisement errors; it does not correct the wrong probe-request cleanup in the kernel. The scalar trace and P2P diagnostic identify the narrow upstream backport required before claiming this residual driver issue is resolved.

docs.title: Pinned kernel build and review
docs.text:
The matching Raspberry Pi source commit is 359f37f0faefb712add32a39f98751aea67d5c1f. A native two-job GCC 14 build against the packaged 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8 headers preserves CONFIG_BRCMDBG=y's parent -DDEBUG flag. The unchanged rebuild exactly matches stock srcversion FBBF7D1EF3ACBA683834518; the exact upstream patch applies without fuzz (with a 22-line context offset) and produces 2254D80EF43499080344466. An independent read-only hardware review confirms all 254 imported symbol CRCs, all 11 exported CRCs/types/namespaces, vermagic, dependencies, license and AArch64 ELF identity match stock. The independently reconstructed patched source SHA also matches. Candidate module SHA: a2b930a1668775132fa9446d69bc33edc7785aed48bfa6fb35873ae6a14a02c7.

bridge/scripts/brcmfmac-ap-ie-backport.py provides pinned build/attest/install/rollback/verify operations; the unmodified upstream patch, provenance and reproduction instructions live in bridge/patches/. The installer preserves packaged stock, installs only a per-kernel base module override, retains stock companions, stages privately and serializes maintenance. It refuses incompatible source identities/ABIs, existing overrides, unsupported signature enforcement or boot layouts. Failed installation restores stock depmod selection. Rollback does not require build headers. This exact-kernel override is separate from application firmware deployment; future kernels require their own review. No P2P/MBO/firmware change.

Fresh adversarial review identified and corrected candidate identity binding, archive snapshot ownership, failed-install stock selection, rollback header dependence, backup symlink handling and runtime signing checks. Thirty-one focused tool tests pass, including malformed/source/ABI inputs, failed depmod rollback and protected override ownership. Actual installation, loaded module verification, driver trace, recovery and reboot acceptance are recorded below when complete.

docs.title: Loaded-driver acceptance
docs.text:
Actual Pi install → rollback → stock selection/running verification → reinstall passed without replacing packaged stock. A deliberate Wi-Fi-only reload retained USB/g_ether, the same Bridge PID, locked 600 MHz and camera readiness in 6.956 s. The Printer was offline; connected retention is not claimed for that reload. Restarting the supplicant removed the temporary P2P diagnostic. The loaded module's sysfs srcversion and selected file match the candidate. The expected out-of-tree module taint bit was added (1536 → 5632); no kernel/firmware upgrade or initramfs change was performed. This is a local upstream backport, not a vendor-packaged module.

Repeating scalar probes now shows AP teardown clearing association-response IEs (0x4, length 0, return 0), with normal probe-request scan handling (0x10, including 150-byte scan IEs) retained. Every captured management-IE return was 0 across radio-off/on and AP-down transitions. Probe definitions and tracing instance were removed in finally; no payloads or keys captured. Evidence preserves old and new traces; this establishes the changed driver behavior, not merely absence of a log message.

docs.title: Installed connected recovery and policy checks
docs.text:
Clean source a745c9136882283dc7071fabd1f721e2d6b0b186 is installed; all 67 Python source hashes match committed files, privileged helper matches the reviewed hash, backport tool 7a1c34ed…966cc matches independent clearance, and native Printer artifacts remain unchanged. The full normal commit gates passed 2,370 Bridge tests (27 existing warnings), Ruff, strict mypy and operational-script compilation; strict docs and targeted tool formatting passed. The unmodified upstream patch's required context whitespace has a file-specific Git attribute, so its primary-source digest is preserved while source whitespace checking stays enabled.

With INSTAX-52006924 powered on, the installed Bridge automatically obtained fresh Link Square status, film 0, at locked at 600 MHz without a manual Reconnect action. External AP connection-down recovered automatically in 32.693 s; all samples retained the connected Printer, locked at 600 MHz, same PID and finalfresh status/watch1/no retired tasks, with zero vendor-IE errors.

A radio-off fixture initially expected automatic re-enabling and timed out after80.38 s. That expectation contradicts the deliberate-administrative-off policy in plan064 and its existing unit test. Independent review confirmed this is a fixture error, not a software finding; the raw failed report is preserved. All 187 observations kept PrinterConnected, fresh status, locked at 600 MHz, same PID, watch 1 / retired tasks 0/film 0 while radio remained disabled. Explicit helper restoration succeeded with zero vendor-IE errors. This is not automatic radio recovery. The accepted policy and guard remain unchanged.

The Printer shut off before the additional external Bluetooth-disconnect check, which timed out before mutation; that availability failure is retained. Automatic reconnection when it was powered on and connected retention above are verified; a new external-disconnect result is not claimed. An offline UI smoke check passed same-button triple unlock, nonblank LCD and 1000 MHz boost, then relock600 through the shared production queue/physical LCD; GPIO contacts were not actuated. Normal service was restored and its observer/drop-in/socket removed before reboot. Final boot persistence and normal-running log evidence follow below.

docs.title: Final reboot and connected follow-up
docs.text:
A real reboot loaded the selected override with exact 2254D80EF43499080344466 srcversion; stock hash and native artifacts remain unchanged. Normal services started, FTP220/200 and hotspot/USB were available, automatic idle returned to powersave at 600 MHz. When the user powered on INSTAX-52006924 again, normal startup obtained fresh Link Square status automatically.

A short post-boot observer validation repeated external Device1.Disconnect: automatic fresh status recovery passed in 7.170 s, with all samples locked at 600 MHz/camera ready/same PID, immediate stale publication and final watch 1 / retired tasks 0. Uncontrolled advertising timing precludes a transport speedup claim. The earlier Printer-unavailable attempt remains a failed availability fixture; this follow-up resolves the connected disconnect gate. Same-button triple unlock restored nonblank LCD/1000 MHz, relock600 and status pause/resume/watch rearm passed. No image, print, LED/reset or other actuator Printer commands; zero film consumed.

The observer initially inherited host-private0600 scripts during transfer, causing21 failed startup attempts before permissions were corrected to root:ib0640. This audit setup fault and its systemd records are retained/classified separately from production application behavior. The observer was removed again; normal Bridge/manager services are active with0 automatic restarts. Final normal Bridge PID1542 had no warnings/errors, GPIOv2 input/no fallback, FTP220/200, powersave at 600 MHz, 45.084°C/throttle0x0 and no working cache or audit socket/drop-in. The Printer was offline again at final normal capture after its idle period; no current connected-state claim is made. Its reconnect and connected recovery checks above passed.

Fresh boot journals:504 service records / 48 flags, including42 systemd records for the 21 fixture start failures, three expected BlueZ disconnect-cleanup notes and existing configuration/registration/offline-DNS notes. Kernel 397 records / 21 warnings, zero vendor-IE errors. Existing regulator/staging GPU/media/LCD and VCHI initialization findings remain; expected local-module taint is retained. No additional application finding or new HCI fault. Complete raw logs stay private; sanitized evidence is under docs/assets/bridge-audit-090/. Owned build/benchmark/observer artifacts were removed; production per-boot Wi-Fi stamps, installed driver override, its private provenance and stock rollback backup remain.

Boundaries: FTP fixtures used same-Pi hotspot addressing with synthetic files, not wireless airtime or a physical camera. Shared input queue/actual LCD used, not physical button contacts. The kernel override is specific to this kernel and must be reviewed again on kernel changes.

docs.title: Goal and boundaries
docs.text:
Remove the remaining legacy VideoCore media initialization failures, preserve the SPI LCD, camera FTP/HIF handling and automatic Printer reconnect, and measure normal boot milestones. No film or Printer image/actuator commands. Three independent agents cover pinned driver/loader sources, implementation and adversarial review. Root performs hardware changes.

Baseline application source: 966b316; native source b2b6c8c and the reviewed Wi-Fi AP cleanup backport remain unchanged. Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0, ST7789 240 × 240, X306 2300 mAh, Debian 13.2, kernel 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, BlueZ 5.82, Python 3.13.5; Printer Link Square INSTAX-52006924. Current boot uses gpu_mem=16, camera/display autodetect disabled, no KMS overlay, auto_initramfs=0. Camera inputs are external uploads, not a CSI sensor.

docs.title: Cause and candidate
docs.text:
The pinned VCHIQ driver registers legacy camera/codec/ISP/audio/shared-memory children without firmware service discovery. The 16 MB firmware profile uses cut-down firmware. Udev coldplug therefore attempts unused legacy drivers whose services are unavailable, producing VCHI/shared-memory/MMAL errors. They occur at about 8.4–8.6 seconds in the retained baseline boot. No video or vcsm device survives; no detected vchiq consumer.

Use a tracked modprobe profile to blacklist alias loading of only bcm2835_v4l2, bcm2835_codec, bcm2835_isp, vc_sm_cma and snd_bcm2835. Ordinary blacklists keep explicit diagnostic loads available. Retain VCHIQ and shared media, DRM, framebuffer, SPI, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi drivers. The ST7789 staging/SPI-ID messages concern essential LCD drivers and remain visible.

Provisioning installs the owned fragment; boot-diet reports file directives without claiming active enforcement. Reboot is required; rollback restores the previous owned fragment or removes it if initially absent. Do not alter GPU memory, boot overlays, camera/network credentials or service ordering. Reassess alias/dependency/builtin changes when updating kernels.

docs.title: Validation design
docs.text:
• Two baseline and two candidate normal reboots with identical application/native source and instrumentation. Kernel-monotonic timestamps exclude power-button and firmware latency.
  • Record first LCD/FTP/core readiness, hotspot and Bluetooth availability separately; systemd total time is not the product-ready metric. Printer-off results do not measure connected readiness.
  • Dry-run effective modprobe alias blacklisting and essential hardware dependencies, with explicit media loads still allowed; verify actual module census and warnings after reboot and rollback.
  • Compare HIF/JPEG preparation output and LCD data; isolated checksum-only FTP fixture cannot print.
  • Final status-only Printer reconnect while locked, same-button unlock/timeout, normal services, source hashes, Wi-Fi backport and full available running/boot log review.

docs.title: Measured candidate
docs.text:
Two normal baseline reboots versus two candidate reboots, same application/native source:

Kernel-monotonic readiness Baseline median (range), s Candidate median (range), s LCD UI 13.815 (13.725–13.905) 13.681 (13.543–13.819) FTP 13.781 (13.693–13.869) 13.630 (13.530–13.730) Hotspot receive ready 20.005 (19.884–20.127) 19.411 (19.088–19.734)

These small samples overlap for LCD/FTP and do not establish a repeatable boot speedup. Printer was available only in baseline1 (fresh status 20.029 s); other trials had no fresh Printer status, so connected startup times cannot be compared. Software reboots exclude firmware and physical power-on latency.

Both candidate boots removed all 17 modules in the unused media/audio dependency closure (1,122,304 mapped module bytes in baseline), four VCHI service failures and four NULL video unregister messages. This census is not a measurement of total RAM or battery savings. Essential LCD, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and USB dependencies remained unchanged. Effective loader dry-runs passed all five leaf names/aliases and ten essential dependency cases; explicit loads by real module name remain available. Independent adversarial source/loader review passed with no outstanding source findings.

Retained DSC02821.HIF prepared for Mini, Square and Wide before/after: encoded JPEG and decoded RGB hashes, dimensions, selected quality and transport orientation flags were identical. Original identity/content preserved. This CPU fixture used no BLE/image commands or film.

docs.title: Installed acceptance
docs.text:
Clean source 79880bd installed after full normal hooks: 2,374 Bridge tests passed with 27 existing platform/Pillow warnings, Ruff and strict mypy (67 modules). Thirteen focused script/profile tests, Bash syntax, formatting, diff and strict MkDocs checks passed.

Rollback removed only the initially absent owned profile, rebooted, and reproduced all 17 media/audio modules and four VCHI/four NULL unregister messages while preserving LCD/FTP. Reinstall and normal clean-source reboot removed them again; LCD 13.742 s, FTP 13.659 s, hotspot receive readiness 19.920 s. Unchanged native hashes and exact-kernel Wi-Fi backport verified. The module profile is an OS provisioning change, separately installed on this Pi; ordinary source/firmware application updates alone do not activate it on older installations.

Installed shared GPIO action queue/physical LCD checks passed: same-button triple unlock, nonblank framebuffer equal to the independent render reference, active 1000 MHz, relock 600 MHz and 10-second partial-unlock timeout back to 600 MHz. Physical switch contacts were not actuated. Two isolated 8 MiB FTP receives completed with matching checksums and zero production FTP greeting/NOOP failures. This exercises installed receive code over the same-Pi hotspot address, not an actual camera or wireless airtime. No production upload/print queue used.

docs.title: Connected Printer acceptance
docs.text:
An initial 100-second readiness wait expired while the Printer was off; no Disconnect was dispatched. After the user powered on Link Square INSTAX-52006924, installed runtime PID2138 recovered automatically in 6.269 seconds after external BlueZ Device1.Disconnect. Every sample remained locked at 600 MHz, camera-ready and in the same PID. Invalidated timestamps were consistently marked stale; fresh status restored one disconnect watch and zero retired tasks. Radio advertising timing is uncontrolled, so this is reliability validation, not a speedup claim. Film remained zero; no image/print/actuator commands.

Connected same-button triple unlock/exact nonblank pixels/1000 MHz, relock/600 MHz, 10-second partial-unlock abandonment, status pause/resume and fresh single-watch rearm all passed.

Available installed-boot logs initially contained 203 Bridge/manager records and one manager.bind_pending: USB listener was already serving, hotspot listener succeeded one second later. Kernel had 376 records and ten expected regulator/read-only switch/backport taint/LCD staging/SPI-ID notices; no VCHI/media NULL unregister or Wi-Fi vendor-IE errors. Complete raw logs remain private. Offline Pi wall clock can reset on reboot; all boot comparisons use kernel monotonic time, independent of that clock. No film was used.

Connected FTP continuity repeated: both isolated 8 MiB receives/checksums passed, zero production FTP failures; all 17 monitored samples retained connected/fresh Printer, locked 600 MHz and camera readiness. An early normal-health assertion ran 47 seconds after service start and expected idle too soon; active 1000 MHz was correct. Final capture waits for the actual idle policy transition rather than treating that fixture timing as an application bug.

docs.title: Final normal service and log review
docs.text:
Restored normal Bridge PID2626 / manager637, both active with zero automatic restarts, connected Printer, powersave600 MHz/GPIO24 low, FTP220/200, GPIOv2 and no input/network fallback, throttle0x0. Source/native hashes and clean manifest match.

Full final installed-boot logs include five Bluetooth warning records after the observed-to-normal service restart: two missing-write-characteristic connection setup failures plus existing auto-rebond. Normal runtime recovered automatically after 66.480 seconds from its boot-start marker, with fresh film0/battery50% status and connected final health. This remains a connection-setup follow-up (GATT service/cache readiness); the media profile changes no Bluetooth source/dependencies. Do not describe these logs as fault-free or conflate this restoration timing with the successful6.269s external-disconnect test. The expected manager listener wait remained the other flagged service record. No VCHI/media unregister or vendor-IE errors returned.

Owned observer/drop-in/socket and 19 test/helper files removed; only the production root0644 media fragment remains, matching reviewed SHA. User photos and Wi-Fi backport rollback provenance untouched. Clean source deployed with normal services; no firmware publication.

docs.title: Bluetooth GATT readiness after service restart
Goal and boundaries
docs.text:
Fix uncertain GATT setup being classified as a stale bond, keep setup waits bounded, preserve fresh status/automatic reconnect, benchmark real warm restarts and deploy without film. Three subagents cover pinned-source audit, implementation and independent adversarial review. Root owns all hardware mutations. No image, print, reset, LED or actuator commands.

Pi Zero2W Rev1.0/ST7789/X306, Debian13.2/Linux6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8/Python3.13.5/BlueZ5.82; Link Square INSTAX-52006924. Baseline clean application35d8a0c, nativeb2b6c8c/FFI9e31f998…34031. Wi-Fi AP cleanup backport and unused-media profile from plans090/091 retained.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Pinned btleplug0.11.8 discovers GATT by introspecting exported objects. A successful introspection can return an incomplete table; connected state does not prove service resolution. The normal connect path waits for BlueZ ServicesResolved, but reused-link and CLI fallback paths can skip that wait. See the BlueZ Device API and vendored bluez-async await_service_discovery.

The old characteristic loop declared a2s deadline while is_connected/rediscovery I/O remained unbounded inside it. Link-down/state-query failures exited as missing-write-characteristic, which Python treated as stale-key evidence after lookup. Progress retained a prior attempt's highest phase even after a fallback restarted service discovery.

Plan091's two failures ended about0.3s after lookup, before the2s deadline, followed by bond removal/retry and eventual normal recovery66.480s. The retained log lacks HCI reasons/raw readiness properties, so it cannot establish why those radio links dropped. Do not claim a readiness barrier is proven to prevent radio drops.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
Successful ordinary btleplug connect with a complete table keeps its healthy path. Reused and CLI-assisted connections must confirm readiness even for a complete cached table. Otherwise, on incomplete exports the native resolver reads fresh typed Connected/ServicesResolved for the exact Linux device and uses one2s deadline for state queries, rediscovery and waits. Unknown state retains bounded discovery fallback; pending resolution waits. Link loss/unconfirmed readiness produces explicit transient setup detail. Only a freshly resolved incomplete table, confirmed live again in the final poll window, retains the missing-characteristic fingerprint. Genuine subscribe/write/authentication recovery remains.

Python carries terminal progress detail with the generic C ABI error, resets current phase on retry regressions, and excludes anchored transient readiness/link-down errors from bond removal. An explicit org.bluez.Error.AuthenticationFailed from rediscovery retains existing recovery. Legacy native builds without detail keep their compatible phase heuristic. No C ABI/image/model/ transport fragment/pacing/config/sync contract changes.

Review found a Linux plumbing mistake in the initial candidate: btleplug IDs are relative, while BlueZ object paths are absolute. Corrected through the production /org/bluez prefix wrapper and added a Linux test through that same wrapper before build/deployment.

docs.title: Validation and baseline
docs.text:
Two warm observed restarts on unchanged baseline, Printer initially Connected/ServicesResolved: restart→fresh16.314/16.268s, first status attempt→fresh3.461/3.604s; subsequent fresh polls pass. These healthy baseline runs do not reproduce the earlier missing-characteristic failures. Read-only BlueZ metadata/signals and identical observer used for all cohorts; no image data. Warm restart timings include startup pairing/radio/retries and are not cold boot or energy tests.

Source tests exercise delayed export, pending/unknown/live/down state, malformed/wrong device, blocked I/O deadlines, cancellation, genuine missing characteristics, phase regressions and explicit authentication failures. Linux-specific execution and live candidate/installed tests follow before final acceptance. Full running logs are retained privately; sanitized evidence under docs/assets/bridge-audit-092.

docs.title: Additional cached-table finding
docs.text:
BlueZ5.82 GATT client retains exported characteristic objects when its connection client is cleared; the device lifecycle resets ServicesResolved separately. A complete cache is therefore insufficient for reuse or CLI-assisted connections. The provisional b2e4e2a candidate was installed while the Printer was off; it was not accepted as the final live fix. Independent review identified this case before live acceptance. The corrected evidence policy tracks successful btleplug connect versus reuse/assistance and updates after internal reconnect. Unknown or pending state cannot accept cached characteristics on guarded paths. Fifteen independent Mac GATT tests now pass.

Full first-stage Linux core tests227passed on the Pi, including11GATT tests, before this additional guard. Full normal host checks2383Bridge tests/27existingwarnings, Rustworkspacefmt/clippy/tests, Ruff/strictmypy67 and FFIheaderdrift passed. One unchanged HIF descendant-timeout fixture failed under concurrent compilation; four affected cases then full normal gate passed unchanged. Corrected Linux guarded-path execution and live comparisons follow; no film used.

docs.title: Live acceptance
docs.text:
Matched warm restart Baseline (two runs) Corrected candidate (two runs) Dispatch→fresh status 16.314/16.268s (median16.291) 16.127/16.215s (median16.171) First status attempt→fresh 3.461/3.604s (median3.532) 3.556/3.523s (median3.540)

Both cohorts started Connected/ServicesResolved and completed a subsequent fresh periodic poll. These small healthy samples show no established speedup and do not reproduce the earlier intermittent failure. Timings under the observer cannot be compared directly with normal service. Final Linux16GATT tests passed on the Pi, including complete-cache guard and deadline/cancellation; corrected host212core tests and full workspace gates passed. Native/source hashes match clean 6d61384; FFIb91cf3fd…ea1175, CLI f1d325ac…31b21f.

Status-only external Disconnect recovered automatically in 7.191s, all16samples locked600MHz/ samePID5266/camera-ready; invalid timestamps marked stale, fresh status restored watch1/retired0. Same-button triple unlock/exact nonblank LCD1000MHz, relock600,10s abandonment and status pause/resume/watch rearm passed. Physical switch contacts not actuated. Film0 unchanged.

Normal service without observer restarted successfully: dispatch→observed fresh7.204s and boot-start marker→fresh4.811s, no warning/error records. Final PID5618/manager637 active with zero automatic restarts, connected50% LinkSquare,600MHz powersave/FTP220+200/GPIOv2/no fallback, throttle0x0. No cold-boot, physical-camera upload, battery or transport-speedup claim.

Full available boot journals945service/378kernel records: six historical service flags belong to earlier manager/PID2626 scopes; no candidate/normal flags. Ten expected hardware/staging/ backport notices remain, zero VCHI/media-null unregister and Wi-Fi vendor-IE errors. Raw journals private; independent source, Linux and live evidence reviews passed.

Final review preserves canonical native org.bluez.Error.AuthenticationFailed recovery even at connect-stage3: actual authentication can fail before lookup under the readiness barrier. Generic early BLE errors, near-match error names and generic Python exception text do not authorize rebond. This final classifier refinement changes no native/image/healthy-connect path.

docs.title: Final classifier deployment
docs.text: Clean59ef504 installed after the full2388Bridge tests/27existingwarnings, Ruff/strictmypy67 and independent66focused tests. Native6d61384 artifacts remain unchanged. Normal service restarted with latest classifier, healthy FTP220/200/GPIOv2/no fallback,600MHz powersave,0automatic restarts and no current application warning/error records. Printer was offline after its idle shutoff; final power-on request remained unanswered at capture. The connected live comparisons above used6d61384 before this pure failure-classification refinement. Updated early-auth behavior is covered by native-progress/provider tests; no pairing-key corruption was forced on hardware. Post-refinement live connected confirmation remains pending Printer power-on. No film used.

docs.title: Post-refinement connected confirmation
docs.text:
The user powered the Printer on again. Installed runtime 1f9dda2 (classifier 59ef504, native 6d61384) reached fresh film-count status with no setup warnings: restart dispatch to observed fresh status took 18.552 seconds; application boot-start marker to fresh status took 5.523 seconds. The dispatch interval includes stopping the previous runtime; it is not directly comparable with the earlier boot-marker metric. No film was used and no image or actuator commands were sent.

Final normal runtime PID 6758 and manager PID 637 were connected with fresh status at 600 MHz, backlight GPIO 24 low, 45.622°C and throttle flags 0x0. FTP returned 220/200, GPIO v2 was active, and both services had zero automatic restarts. External BlueZ Disconnect dispatch to fresh status took 12.171 seconds; all 22 probes retained 600 MHz, powersave, backlight low, the same PID and FTP 220/200. The native disconnect event was recorded, with no warning/error messages. Internal lock/watch flags were not introspected in this normal-service check; their prior observer validation remains separate. This confirms final classifier deployment; the previously pending power-on acceptance is complete. No pairing-key corruption was forced. Read-only FTP probes used the same-Pi address. The independent confirmation review passed with no outstanding findings or pending acceptance checks.

docs.title: Bridge pairing backups and Pillow cleanup
Scope
docs.text: Remove redundant Pillow RGB mode arguments without changing prepared image pixels. Include the selected Printer's persisted BlueZ pairing information in management backups when it exists, while preserving automatic reconnect and keeping pairing secrets out of logs and diagnostics. Validate on the installed Bridge using status requests only, with no film consumed.

docs.title: Findings and implementation
docs.text:
• Hue and vignette processing supply three-channel uint8 arrays. Pillow infers RGB; the explicit mode argument is redundant and emits deprecation warnings.
  • The management backup paths previously used the installation directory as a filesystem root. The unprivileged management service also cannot read BlueZ's root-only storage. Adding a path alone would not make production pairing backups work.
  • Use a socket-activated, narrowly scoped root backup broker with trusted root-owned code and root-only archives. Keep the management service unprivileged and retain NoNewPrivileges.
  • Select only saved Printer pairing information, reject unsafe paths, and avoid copying unrelated devices or scan caches. Absence of a persistent bond is valid: Instax Link devices can reconnect using the saved Printer selection without an OS-level bond.

Storage layout and reload behavior were checked against the upstream BlueZ 5.82 storage reference. BlueZ loads persisted state during object initialization, so a live bond restore must reload BlueZ while the Bridge runtime is stopped.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The Pillow implementation passed 335 affected imaging/pipeline tests with deprecation warnings treated as errors. Six seeded profiles produce exactly the same RGB pixels as the previous explicit-mode conversion and leave source pixels unchanged.

The independent source review passed 91 focused backup/broker/installer/Pillow tests and two additional adversarial source/restore symlink-swap checks. Review fixes cover descriptor-relative I/O, competing archive creation, private ownership, service recovery on failure, adapter identity conflicts, legacy bundles and HTTP 404 compatibility. Production create/restore and pre-update backups now use the same private broker. The App's existing backup/restore response models were reviewed; their required fields remain unchanged.

Ruff, full formatting (158 files), strict mypy (68 source files), touched shell syntax, broker compilation and strict docs passed. The first full test run passed 2,430 tests and found one offline-provision fixture that lacked a mocked root identity for the new privileged installer. Only eight expected host GPIO fallback warnings remain; Pillow warnings are gone. Final full validation and installed results follow after that fixture is updated.

Real pairing secrets and backup archives remain on the Bridge; committed evidence contains only verification results and measurements. Physical hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0, ST7789 LCD, Debian 13.2, Linux 6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python 3.13.5, BlueZ 5.82 and Link Square INSTAX-52006924. No film, image, reset or actuator commands are permitted in this validation.

docs.title: Installed restore ownership refinement
docs.text:
The corrected offline fixture passed its 20 affected cases. Normal commit gates then passed all 2,431 Bridge tests, with only eight expected host GPIO fallback warnings. Clean 870fb21 was installed along with the root-owned helper, and the manager was restarted to load its client.

Production create/restore ran under an ib systemd sandbox matching the manager restrictions. It verified and restored 28 files in 2.112/16.786 seconds from dispatch to reply; the broker reported 321/14,916 ms for its operation intervals. Configuration, selection and native-library contents remained unchanged. The isolated synthetic LTK/adapter identity roundtrip passed exact bytes, private permissions and unrelated-device exclusion. The physical Printer has no persisted bond, so its live backup correctly included selection and zero BlueZ files.

The subsequent application log check found a real ownership defect: private presets.toml retained mode 0600 but became root-owned, preventing the runtime from loading it. The Bridge was recovered by restoring its ib ownership and restarting. The final code now restores product configuration files as ib:ib while keeping their private modes. Review also required repairing nested product directory access. BlueZ keys and OS configuration outside the product directory retain root ownership. A regression test covers private presets and nested credentials.

The independent ownership refinement review passed 92 focused tests with deprecations treated as errors. Repeat installed restore and normal runtime acceptance follow below; the initial integrity-only live result is preserved separately and is not final acceptance.

Clean ownership refinement 1a0c4b2 passed all 2,432 Bridge tests and was installed. Repeated production backup/restore verified 28 files in 2.978/14.925 seconds from dispatch to reply. Private presets remained ib-owned, readable and mode 0600; contents, selection and native library remained unchanged. Both normal services were active with zero automatic restarts. PID 9078 had zero warnings/errors, locked 600 MHz/backlight low, FTP 220/200, no throttling, and no active backup worker. Isolated synthetic LTK/adapter identity restoration passed again.

The installed Pi Pillow 11.3.0 passed the six-profile exact RGB pixel comparison with warnings treated as errors; no source pixels changed and no film was used.

docs.title: Preserve active firmware provenance
docs.text:
The final review identified another correctness issue: archives contain deployment fingerprints but no matching firmware/native binaries. Applying an older configuration backup must not overwrite the installed build's provenance. The broker now verifies the complete archive, including these contextual metadata files, then omits .deployment entries from the live apply plan. Counts and restored paths describe only applied files. Existing or absent deployment records remain unchanged; modified contextual metadata still fails integrity verification before services stop. Generic isolated-root archive restoration remains available for recovery tooling.

The independent final source review passed 95 focused tests with deprecations treated as errors. The prior ownership live check predates this filter; final installed filtered-restore results follow.

docs.title: Final installed acceptance
docs.text:
Clean 9de0f1b passed all 2,435 Bridge tests, eight expected host GPIO warnings, Ruff and strict mypy, and was installed. Production backup verified 29 files, including selected Printer BlueZ info with real cryptographic key sections. Restore applied 24 files, preserved active deployment metadata and all tracked contents, and retained private presets as readable ib-owned 0600. Create/restore dispatch-to-reply took 2.976/18.854 seconds. BlueZ and the Bridge were reloaded; the real archive and secrets remained root-only on the Pi. Synthetic LTK/adapter-identity roundtrip also passed exact bytes, private modes and exclusion of unrelated devices.

The first reconnect fixture exited before mutation because the device object was not ready when CPU idle settled. The runtime later obtained status automatically. The completed external BlueZ Disconnect check restored fresh status in 7.533 seconds from dispatch, with all 11 samples at 600 MHz, powersave, GPIO 24 low, the same PID 9806 and FTP 220/200. Film count remained zero. This is reliability acceptance, not an established transport speedup. Automatic screen-off idle was verified through frequency/backlight observations; internal manual-lock flags and physical button contacts were not inspected in this round. A health fixture initially expected a manual lock log during automatic idle; that fixture assumption was corrected without product changes.

Final connected health: Bridge PID 9806 and manager PID 8053 active with zero automatic restarts, 600 MHz/backlight low, throttle flags 0x0, FTP responsive, presets loaded, private backup modes intact, manager NoNewPrivileges=yes and zero active backup workers. Trusted broker SHA f7a8b6f988a0a14914358e67c0e8daf057f541991a2b9563bf4118894fe68382 matches the review; native FFI SHA remains b91cf3fdd128b314cbcb952037e686514023371fe960a1c7d8ed4562d9ea1175.

All 93 available current-PID log records were reviewed. Six warning records across three transient Bluetooth episodes, including the forced disconnect, remain in the evidence. Recovery was automatic, with no flags after the latest fresh status and no preset-load failures. These logs are not described as warning-free. No film, image, reset or actuator commands were used.

Four owned hardware helpers and isolated synthetic roots were removed; production socket and private backups were retained. A current verified backup was created after the reconnect check. Source, ownership, provenance and final live review reports are under docs/assets/bridge-audit-093/. The independent final live review passed with no blocking findings or pending acceptance checks.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Investigate the Bluetooth warnings remaining after plan 093. Preserve automatic reconnect, status freshness and authentication recovery; validate on the installed Pi with status requests only and no film. Keep genuine faults visible while removing duplicate reports and incorrect diagnostic claims.

docs.title: Baseline evidence
docs.text:
The six warning records represent three failed connection attempts. Each native terminal callback reported BLE error: BLE link disconnected during GATT setup during characteristic lookup. The first two followed service/BlueZ restoration; the third followed an external Disconnect. All recovered automatically. The backend and controller each emitted a warning for the same attempt, and generic FFI error text obscured the native cause.

The provider also supplied empty scanner diagnostics for BLE setup errors even though it had not performed a separate scanner pass. This incorrectly reported that the selected Printer was absent. Native readiness checks queried fresh BlueZ state and detected an actual dropped connection; the investigation provides no evidence that those checks should be bypassed or weakened.

docs.title: Implementation and validation
docs.text:
Only exact canonical setup-drop evidence qualifies for bounded transient handling. The first two unresolved setup drops are INFO; the third is WARNING. The episode survives session teardown, same-target absence, unknown failures and case variants, clearing only after fresh status or a different target. Unknown and authentication failures remain warnings themselves.

The backend retains native detail and stage in its log signature. A per-exception ownership flag prevents a duplicate controller warning without suppressing failures from other providers. BLE setup errors no longer invent an empty scan. Startup permits the existing two prompt retries after a confirmed setup drop, then returns to normal offline cadence; repeated drops or absent scans do not renew this allowance. A pending disconnect event retains recovery ownership.

Three subagents independently investigated, implemented and adversarially reviewed the work. Review fixed a misplaced failure-reason reset and a logging test fixture; root review also caught an allowance reset after intervening absent scans. All received regression coverage. The final full suite passed 2,450 tests, with eight expected Mac GPIO warnings. Ruff formatting of 158 files, Ruff lint, strict mypy of 68 source files, diff checks and strict MkDocs passed. The producer ran 352 affected tests; the independent reviewer ran 368 broader checks and the final amended 65-test status suite. No Rust, protocol, image, FFI ABI or configuration changes.

Clean aa852e1 installed through the normal deployment script, which restarts BlueZ, manager and Bridge. Loaded source hashes match the independent review; FFI remains b91cf3fdd128b314cbcb952037e686514023371fe960a1c7d8ed4562d9ea1175. Initial installed health: Bridge PID 11373 and manager 11371 active with zero automatic restarts, FTP 220/200, backup socket active and no runtime warnings. Startup was correctly awake at 1,000 MHz. The attempted live baseline timed out before issuing Disconnect because the Printer was offline; historical plan 093 timings are contextual, not a matched speed comparison.

Installed automatic screen-off settled at 600 MHz/powersave/GPIO 24 low. Its full current-PID journal contained 24 records and no warning/error matches. A second 85-second readiness probe also timed out before issuing Disconnect because the Printer remained unavailable. Neither probe issued any Printer command beyond the normal service's discovery/status activity. Live installed reconnect remains pending Printer availability; no physical contact, Printer power-cycle, fresh film-count comparison or reconnect-speed claim is made. No film used. Hardware unchanged: Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0/ST7789/X306, Debian 13.2/kernel 6.12.47/BlueZ 5.82, Link Square INSTAX-52006924.

Public evidence: plan 094 audit assets.

docs.title: Live follow-up after Printer power-on
docs.text:
The normal installed service recovered one exact native setup drop at 15:49:24 EDT and published fresh status at 15:49:28: one detailed INFO record, no duplicate warning. A subsequent external Disconnect completed native connection/status setup again at 15:49:40 while the service stayed at 600 MHz with the screen dark and FTP responsive. Film remained zero.

That first probe timed out because unchanged successful status after a disconnect was DEBUG, so its INFO-only journal observer could not prove controller acceptance. Connected BlueZ and native progress alone were not promoted to a successful fresh-status acceptance result. The follow-up clears the status-log signature only on an accepted current disconnect event: the next accepted fresh status is INFO once, with unchanged later polls returning to DEBUG. Stale watches and replies arriving while a disconnect is pending cannot generate fresh status. This restores the documented recovery logging without adding polls or changing BLE operations.

Clean 7c312ad with that amendment passed 2,451 full Bridge tests, eight expected Mac GPIO warnings, Ruff and strict mypy. Independent review passed 370 affected tests. Installed controller SHA c045cf31684e38857ab54aba213c4bd2e7a29205a629256535db88fa9f803694 matches review; native FFI unchanged.

Two installed status-only external Disconnect checks passed at 11.159 and 7.367 seconds, measured from command dispatch to an accepted fresh controller status record. The first attempt encountered one absent scan; the second encountered an exact setup drop, preserved at INFO with stage 5/detail/streak 1 and recovered automatically. All 21 + 11 observations retained PID 13213, 600 MHz/powersave, GPIO 24 low, FTP greeting 220/NOOP 200 and film 0 → 0. No manual Reconnect, image, print or actuator command. No matched baseline or universal speedup claim.

Final accepted health: Bridge 13213/manager 13211 active, zero automatic restarts, connected Printer with fresh Square/50%/charging status, throttle 0x0, backup socket active and all three reviewed Python hashes matching. The complete current-PID journal contained 132 records and zero warning/error matches, including the successful recovery of the actual setup drop. Initial offline probe timeouts and the rejected INFO-observer timeout remain recorded above; they are not counted as successful checks. These checks validate automatic dark-screen recovery; physical contacts, manual lock-state introspection and Printer power cycles were not exercised. Independent final evidence review passed. Both owned remote helpers were removed afterward; Bridge, manager and the production backup socket remained active. Final documentation-only deployment preserves the accepted runtime process; no additional Bluetooth restart is needed.

docs.title: Screen-based Printer discovery and grouped Settings
Observed problem
docs.text: The physical boot journal confirmed the reported behavior. UI readiness was at 14.854 seconds after boot, the first discovery found no Printer, and the saved 30-second period delayed retry. KEY3 at 39.529 seconds woke that wait; fresh status followed at 43.443 seconds. This establishes an unnecessary awake wait, not a guaranteed radio availability time.

docs.title: Screen-based discovery
docs.text:
Following the user's clarification, offline discovery uses a one-second scan window and one-second target retry period while the screen is visible, including the unlock prompt. The existing configured search interval applies while dark: 30 seconds by default, with a five-second scan window. The minimum awake yield is 50 ms; scans/connections are serialized, so a scan that consumes its whole window or a longer connection attempt can exceed one second. The C ABI accepts integer-second scan windows, so the selected awake setting is one second.

Screen changes interrupt the wait and recompute its deadline. Locking adopts the dark cadence; the first unlock press requests a prompt fresh check without completing the three-press unlock. Repeated requests retain one minimum gap. In-flight work completes without cancellation/replay, and disconnect events retain their existing serialized cleanup and bounded recovery retries. Established-link keepalive/status intervals remain separately configured. Policy changes log once, with screen state, actual scan budget and target interval; unchanged polls do not add INFO noise.

The native provider forwards the new scan budget to the existing FFI API. The diagnostic Bleak provider also adjusts its internal unavailable-scan pacing, preventing that fallback from retaining its old longer wait after wake. No configuration fields, payload shape, protocol or native ABI change. The App's existing search_interval_s control maps to the dark discovery period.

docs.title: LCD copy and Settings
docs.text:
• Empty-film home and error states explain “No film is left in the Printer.” Error recovery asks for a new film pack. No-film testing is confined to its explicit Printer option.
  • Network has four rows: FTP, Wi-Fi, iPhone, Connections.
  • FTP holds Camera link, server, user, PIN and credential reset. Wi-Fi holds the Bridge SSID, Wi-Fi PIN and joined-network address. iPhone holds pairing and token reset. Connections holds Bluetooth and USB status. Destructive confirmations and full credential detail dialogs remain.
  • System groups appearance, text size, language and unlock under Screen. Shutdown, refresh and About stay directly accessible. Child pages return to their parent and remembered cursor.
  • First Printer pairing opens FTP; iPhone QR returns to the page that opened it. Physical and virtual LCDs retain the same controller/render path. English and Simplified Chinese copy is updated.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Focused tests cover screen-based cadence, slow checks without overlap, lock/wake during waits, coalesced requests, in-flight scan-budget ownership, group navigation, credential dialogs, destructive confirmation, both languages and all text sizes. Full checks and installed boot, reconnect and LCD observations will be recorded below. No film or Printer actuator commands.

Clean 92c57e4 installed. Final source gate passed 2,481 Bridge tests with eight expected Mac GPIO warnings, 602 focused checks, Ruff lint/format of 159 files, strict mypy of 68 source files and strict MkDocs. Existing navigation tests were updated for actual submenu routes; the full run caught one remaining old unlock-toggle path, which was corrected before the final gate. The full suite also covers native cancellation, stale watches and lock/unlock behavior.

A controlled on-Pi production controller/provider/Rust FFI probe used an unmatched synthetic Printer and NullDisplay. Normal Bridge was stopped for this probe and restored by an EXIT trap. Real awake gaps were 1.378–1.392 seconds, including one-second scans and driver overhead. Dark start period was 30.002 seconds, with a five-second scan at 600 MHz. The first unlock press woke the next scan in 40.8 ms; CPU reached 1 GHz before that press returned. The native scan can begin during CPU warm-up while the three-press prompt remains visible. Triple unlock completed; no physical button, actual Printer connection, bond change, image or film operation.

Normal service restored at PID 1293 with zero automatic restarts. Its policy records confirm screen=on scan_window_s=1 interval_s=1.0, then screen=off scan_window_s=5 interval_s=30.0. Installed source hashes match the checkout; FFI remains b91cf3fdd128b314cbcb952037e686514023371fe960a1c7d8ed4562d9ea1175. FTP 220/200, 600 MHz/powersave/backlight GPIO 24 low and no runtime warnings verified. The Printer remained offline; normal installed automatic boot-to-connected validation is pending availability.

LCD previews and measurements use synthetic credentials. Previews were visually reviewed with Mac font fallbacks, including English/Chinese large text. Short labels avoid the previous clipped unlock row and exposed token terminology. No hardware panel scanout or physical button contact claim. Pi Zero 2 W/ST7789/X306, Debian 13.2/Linux 6.12.47/BlueZ 5.82 and Link Square INSTAX-52006924; native firmware, camera transfer and image rules are unchanged by this Python/UI update.

docs.title: Installed live follow-up — accepted
docs.text:
With the Printer powered on, clean 2cfd194 booted to UI 14.138 s, FTP/core 14.152 s and fresh Printer status 20.041 s, measured from kernel startup. No button action preceded connection. Film 10→10; no print/image/actuator commands. This excludes firmware startup time and is not a matched availability-controlled improvement claim. The observer initially mistook GPIO initialization for input; checking actual ui.input action= events in the retained journal accepted that same boot without repeating it.

Normal screen-off external BlueZ Disconnect → fresh status passed in 8.885 s. All 14 samples retained Bridge PID 502, 600 MHz/powersave/backlight low and FTP 220/200. One real GATT setup drop was retained at INFO and recovered through prompt retry. Film 10→10; no manual Reconnect. Controlled explicit lock/triple-unlock coverage is recorded above; this live run observes automatic screen-off idle, without introspecting internal manual-lock flags or exercising physical contacts.

Accepted health: Bridge502/manager661 active, zero automatic restarts, connected/fresh Printer, throttle0x0 and backup socket active. Reviewed source hashes match; native FFI unchanged. Full Bridge PID log had 83 records and zero warning/error matches. Wider boot logs retain one manager hotspot-bind warning, which became listening 1.004 s later (HTTP responsive), two BlueZ notices and 22 system warning-priority records. Platform warnings are recorded in evidence, not hidden; there is no whole-system warning-free claim. No further production defect was identified in this scope. Live results supersede the earlier pending availability checkpoint.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Improve boot-to-connected time without changing the LCD state machine, camera FTP admission, image preparation, Printer protocol, automatic reconnect, or screen-dependent discovery cadence. Printer benchmarks use status/discovery requests only; no film or Printer actuators.
