The previous installed run reached UI at 14.138 seconds, core FTP readiness at 14.152 seconds, and fresh Printer status at 20.041 seconds from kernel startup. Those measurements exclude pre-kernel firmware latency and do not establish a matched radio-availability comparison.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Use the agent's fresh BlueZ object snapshot to resolve selected cached identities and trust state. Already trusted devices need no CLI inventory/trust process. Matching untrusted devices retain the existing trust command. An authoritative absent device has nothing to trust; the registered agent authorizes it when discovered. Uncertain properties, provider failure and ambiguous adapter scope retain the original CLI inventory/trust fallback. Cancellation does not launch fallback work. Startup bond reset and live-link protection remain unchanged.

No new configuration field, API payload, native ABI, native artifact or system security policy. The existing service launch, CPU tiers, stop cleanup and LCD/FTP startup dependencies remain.

docs.title: Evidence and review
docs.text:
Three subagents investigated startup, implemented the bounded changes and independently reviewed correctness. The primary agent owns hardware operations. Source validation, adversarial findings, boot/reconnect results and limitations will be recorded after review and hardware acceptance.

A controlled warm-cache fresh-process import probe on the Pi measured 2.584/2.599 seconds with 600 MHz powersave and 1.701/1.688 seconds with 1 GHz performance, in slow/fast/fast/slow order. This includes process/runuser startup, retains the production service and restores its original powersave tier. It isolates import cost; it is not a complete boot speedup measurement.

The primary review found a trust-snapshot freshness race: device revision tracking covered connection and identity changes but omitted Trusted, which the new lookup consumes. A newer trust change/invalidation could therefore leave a pending older Trusted=true reply acceptable. The independent reviewer confirmed the issue. Trust signals now invalidate pending snapshots; two integration regressions require the bounded retry to return the fresh untrusted target while preserving the shared bus. No trust values are added to the compact disconnect-watch cache.

Initial source gate passed 2,495 tests, eight expected host GPIO fallback warnings, Ruff and strict mypy. The race correction additionally passed 137 agent/pairing tests. A controlled normal baseline reboot of 0d79921 reached UI 14.045 s, FTP 14.036 s and core 14.059 s; the Printer was not advertising, so that run establishes no connected-time baseline. The attempted connected baseline timed out before any reboot because no fresh Printer status was available.

docs.title: Rejected early CPU boost
docs.text: The first candidate also tried a nonfatal ExecStartPre call to the existing CPU performance helper before Python imports. The normal reboot comparison showed no clear benefit: UI 14.045→14.306 s, FTP14.036→14.916 s, core14.059→14.930 s and receive-ready20.178→20.437 s. Process-start→import completion improved only 3.350→3.110 s; startup variation and the added pre-start process offset the isolated import result. Existing firmware initial_turbo=30 may also make the hook redundant, but its effect on frequency during imports was not measured. Independent evidence review recommended rejecting this additional startup dependency. The pre-start hook and its two tests were removed; existing application CPU policy is retained.

docs.title: Final installed checks
docs.text:
Clean 4049bcd installed and rebooted with final production changes limited to trust lookup and trust-snapshot freshness. The systemd service is byte-identical to 0d79921; LCD, FTP, runtime power tiers, native artifacts and startup ordering remain unchanged. Final 2,495 tests pass, eight expected host GPIO warnings; Ruff, format160files, strict mypy68files and strict docs pass. Independent final net-diff review found no blocking issues.

Baseline→final kernel-monotonic boot times: LCD14.045→13.742 s, FTP14.036→13.728 s, core14.059→13.756 s, hotspot receive-ready20.178→19.995 s. First discovery policy15.013→14.035 s; FFI-loaded→discovery setup0.722→0.072 s. These single reboots establish reduced setup overhead, not a full connected-time improvement: neither run had an advertising Printer. Firmware startup latency is excluded. No input was injected.

Awake framebuffer contains156 distinct RGB565 values at1GHz/backlight high; normal screen-off idle subsequently returned to600MHz/powersave/backlight low (cleared framebuffer expected). Bridge475/manager639 active with zero automatic restarts, FTP220/200, other services/backup socket active, throttle0x0 and reviewed source/unchanged FFI hashes. Complete current-boot Bridge PID log26records has zero warning/error matches. No physical LCD quality/contact test claim.

An isolated production FTP service on the Pi received a valid JPEG byte-for-byte into its queue, with authenticated STOR226/NOOP200. Temporary directory/credentials/port and no consumer/native backend guarantee no print; no physical camera or normal application dispatch claim. The first fixture's inherited login-home cwd was unreadable by ib; matching production WorkingDirectory resolved it without changing FTP code. Probe resources were removed.

Automatic boot-to-Printer and installed reconnect were pending at the initial handoff. The first readiness probe timed out before reboot. A later readiness observer ended during the repeat reboot before fresh status or Disconnect; neither is a passing Printer test. Source and component validation are complete, with no film or Printer actuator use. Evidence: plan096 measurements.

docs.title: Live acceptance after Printer power-on
docs.text:
Unchanged production4049bcd, clean manifest40e0911, passed automatic reboot→fresh Printer status 19.186 s, LCD13.911 s and core13.924 s. No Bridge button action before connection; film10→10. The earlier plan095 run was20.041 s. This0.855 s lower observation is not a controlled general speedup claim; radio/bond/cache/boot variation remains. Kernel timing excludes firmware startup.

The cached untrusted device correctly retained CLI trust before the guarded startup reset; FFI-loaded→first discovery took0.874 s, versus0.072 s for the earlier absent-target case. Do not generalize the offline shortcut to all connections. Remaining measured costs are interpreter launch→boot marker3.349 s, trust/reset around0.85 s and BLE connect→service discovery1.763 s.

External BlueZ Disconnect→fresh automatic status passed 11.267 s in normal screen-off idle. All21 samples were samePID497/600MHz/powersave/GPIO24low/FTP220+200; film10→10. First sample starts2.273 s after dispatch, so no continuous initial Disconnect-call observation claim. No setup failure, manual Reconnect, physical contacts or internal lock-flag introspection.

Accepted health: Bridge497/manager655 active/zero automatic restarts, connected/fresh Printer, throttle0x0, network/Bluetooth/backup socket active, reviewed source/unit/unchanged FFI hashes. Full current-boot Bridge PID journal91records has zero warnings/errors. Wider service logs retain three notices: BlueZ directory mode and no-matching-connection, plus manager hotspot bind pending which became listening1.007 s later. Independent live evidence review accepted the checks. Initial availability gap is complete. No film or Printer image/print/actuator commands were used.

docs.title: Scope and implementation
docs.text:
Keep the native Bridge startup focused on LCD, camera receive and automatic Printer reconnect. Shared Printer types/errors now live in ble/types.py; image contracts, settings and pure cache metadata live in imaging/models.py. Existing public imports re-export the same objects, including worker serialization and exception identities. Native ABI, protocol/image algorithms, CPU tiers, configuration and service ordering are unchanged.

Diagnostic Bleak imports occur on first use off the event loop. Photo transforms load in the existing preparation process or native/metadata/preview thread. The lightweight image worker still imports at startup. The Post editor awaits an off-loop processing import before entering its first rendered frame, with stale-state and cancellation guards. No startup prewarm is added.

docs.title: Adversarial review and source validation
docs.text:
Three subagents investigated, implemented and independently reviewed the change. Review found an import-lock wait during cleanup after cancelled first use, and a synchronous cold import on the first Post slider render. Both were fixed. Independent final review passed 45 focused tests, verified unchanged algorithm bodies and accepted the source. The serial input queue still waits for the first editor import to finish; tests demonstrate event-loop responsiveness and stale state rejection, not consumption of queued buttons during that wait.

The full Bridge suite passes 2,527 tests, with eight expected Mac GPIO fallback warnings. Ruff lint/format (164 files), strict mypy (70 source files) and whitespace checks pass.

docs.title: Predeployment Pi comparisons
docs.text:
Pi Zero 2 W Rev 1.0, ST7789 240×240 framebuffer, X3062300mAh; Debian13.2, kernel6.12.47+rpt-rpi-v8, Python3.13.5, BlueZ5.82. Installed baseline44e6cb4; candidate frozen source staged in a temporary tree using the installed interpreter/dependencies. Normal Bridge service retained, no CPU policy mutation or Printer operation in these probes.

Counterbalanced fresh-process app imports, two warmups then three samples per tree, precompiled bytecode/warm filesystem cache, all observed600MHz/powersave: baseline median 2.108s (range2.078–2.117), candidate 2.026s (2.019–2.108), about82ms lower. This modest result measures app imports only, not cold power-on or total connected time. Required Pillow LCD and D-Bus imports remain; diagnostic and pixel-processing modules are absent on fresh native import.

Actual Pi image worker comparison uses a retained Sony DSC02821.HIF and an asymmetric EXIF6 JPEG fixture. Square JPEG0.516→0.523s, HIF5.752→5.434s, Mini Link3 JPEG0.435→0.456s and Wide JPEG0.623→0.655s; single observations, no general processing-speed claim. Every output JPEG is byte-identical, with identical dimensions, fit, quality and model-specific flip metadata. No physical film or end-to-end camera dispatch was used. Native transport is unchanged.

An initial temporary BSD archive contained AppleDouble metadata and was replaced with a clean source-only archive before accepted runs. An initial pair of overlapping import/image probes was rejected for timing and rerun sequentially. Neither changed production source/service.

docs.title: Installed acceptance
docs.text:
Clean source 079af5a is installed. Baseline→installed kernel-monotonic reboot measurements: LCD13.822→13.665s, FTP13.810→13.652s, core13.835→13.676s, fresh Printer20.484→18.962s. No button action before connection; film10→10. Process launch→boot marker3.340→3.233s. Single reboots are observations, not a general connected-time speedup or proof that imports caused the entire1.522s difference. Advertising/bond paths differ: candidate retained guarded startup reset (~0.8s), while baseline discovered later. Firmware startup is excluded.

Actual Pi offscreen rendering produced92 exact RGB matches covering all modes and3 Post editors, English/Chinese and light/dark. Live awake framebuffer115200bytes/148distinctRGB565 values, 1GHz/performance/backlight high; later normal idle600MHz/powersave/backlight low/cleared frame. Physical panel quality and button contacts were not observed. Full local UI/input/lock regressions pass; this round changes no input or renderer algorithm.

External BlueZ Disconnect→fresh automatic status passed 12.543s while screen-off. All23samples retained PID482/600MHz/powersave/GPIO24low/FTP220+200; film10→10. Samples start 2.590s after dispatch because Disconnect initially blocks. One absent first scan was logged at INFO; the existing prompt retry then connected successfully, with no manual Reconnect or warning. Normal screen-off idle is verified, not introspection of the internal manual-lock flag.

An isolated installed production FTP service received a JPEG byte-for-byte into ReceivedImage queue, STOR226/NOOP200. Temporary directory/credentials/highport and no consumer/native backend prevent printing. Normal port21 retained; physical camera and normal print dispatch not tested.

Bridge482/manager640 active, zero automatic restarts; Printer connected/fresh, throttle0x0, network/Bluetooth/backup socket active. All17 changed source hashes match the benchmark archive and079af5a; systemd unit and native FFI remain unchanged. Complete current-boot Bridge PID journal101records has no warning/error matches. Broader Bridge/manager/Bluetooth review124records retains BlueZ directory-mode and deliberate-disconnect notices, plus manager hotspot bind pending which resolves1.006s later. No whole-system warning-free claim. Temporary probe resources cleaned.

Three subagents and final independent evidence review cover source, output equality and live acceptance. Evidence: plan097 measurements. No Printer image-transfer, print or actuator command; no film used.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Audit the measured boot graph and improve LCD/FTP/Printer readiness without changing application state, image/protocol code, CPU tiers, camera configuration or system security. Use status-only Printer probes; no Printer image-transfer, print or actuator command and no film.

docs.title: Bounded candidate
docs.text:
The existing Bridge waits for dbus.service to finish activation even though its listening dbus.socket is available earlier. On the installed Debian13.2 system, that socket owns /run/dbus/system_bus_socket and dbus-daemon inherits it through --address=systemd:. Change Bridge ordering to After=dbus.socket with explicit Wants=dbus.socket, allowing Python imports to overlap daemon startup. Keep default sysinit/basic/filesystem/shutdown dependencies, existing parallel network/Bluetooth wants, notify/watchdog behavior and all service security unchanged. The application still awaits the pairing agent before any Printer request.

The previous boot observed socket9.101s, daemon9.678s, Bridge process9.698s/boot marker12.931s; this is an approximately0.58s ordering opportunity, not a promised complete boot improvement. LCD framebuffer appeared9.333s, several seconds before application display construction.

Manager startup is unchanged. Its current network-online ordering does not invoke wait-online on this image. Deferring manager behind Bridge READY could delay the rescue API until the Bridge startup timeout and offers no demonstrated benefit: manager imports already start after LCD/FTP. Global service disabling, CPU boost hooks, default-dependency removal and new socket activation for manager are outside this bounded change.

docs.title: Adversarial requirements
docs.text:
Three subagents investigate, implement and independently review. Verify actual listening socket precedes Bridge launch, pairing agent precedes Printer work and LCD uses the real framebuffer. Removing daemon ordering also removes reverse shutdown ordering. Before acceptance, inspect the previous candidate boot's shutdown journal for cleanup/unregister failures, native worker grace expiry, forced kill or restart. Reject the candidate if shutdown reliability or readiness regresses. No daemon-failure robustness claim is made from normal boot checks; bus authentication remains an existing untimed operation in the Bluetooth startup branch.

Local deployment/ordering/listener tests and on-Pi systemd verification precede installation. Normal reboot comparisons use kernel monotonic timings (exclude firmware startup) and no Bridge button input. Collect LCD/FTP/core/agent/Printer and manager/hotspot milestones, film counts, source/unit provenance, actual framebuffer/CPU state, isolated production FTP receipt, automatic screen-off reconnect, complete application logs and broader service notices. Record observations and rejected experiments with their limits after validation.

docs.title: Candidate rejected; original ordering restored
docs.text:
Clean80c2c8d passed2529tests/eight expected host GPIO warnings, Ruff/format165/mypy70 and strict docs, plus actual Pi systemd-analyze verify. Its actual launch9.398s preceded daemon readiness9.866s, establishing overlap. Baseline→candidate normal reboot: UI13.605683→13.595050s, FTP13.582428→13.593595s, core13.616155→13.609813s. These single reboots show no meaningful readiness gain; the earlier launch did not advance observed readiness. No Printer was advertising in either capture, so no connected-time comparison is claimed. The initial connected observer timed out after reboot; the retained baseline component measurements remain valid.

Full candidate reboot cleanup succeeded6.728s/no forced kill, but D-Bus stopped before Bridge finished. Two shutdown warnings were retained: waiting for native status worker and failed status as BlueZ activation was refused during shutdown. A retained prior baseline shutdown completed6.176s with no Bridge warnings and stopped D-Bus after Bridge. Worker/radio phases were not matched, so this control does not isolate warning causality or shutdown speed; BlueZ already shuts down independently. Removing the daemon lifetime ordering is itself a regression risk. Independent review agreed to reject the change rather than retain it for an11ms LCD observation. No warning was suppressed and no speculative service disabling, priorities or manager serialization were added.

The final Bridge unit is restored byte-for-byte to a815fb1 (After=dbus.service), with regression coverage protecting daemon startup/reverse cleanup ordering and independent manager rescue.

docs.title: Final installed acceptance
docs.text:
Clean1a3a61d restored the exact accepted unit. Full2529tests/eight expected host GPIO warnings, Ruff/format165/mypy70 and strict docs pass. Independent source review accepted the rollback and new lifecycle/manager-regression guards. No runtime performance change is retained.

Normal installed reboot without Bridge input: LCD14.003s, FTP13.982s/core14.016s, pairing agent13.595s and fresh Printer19.476s; film10→10. These are individual kernel-monotonic boot observations, not a speedup versus the earlier offline trial. Actual framebuffer115200bytes/ 148distinctRGB565 values at1GHz/performance/backlight high; later normal screen-off600MHz/ powersave/backlight low/cleared frame. Physical panel quality and button contacts not observed.

Full reboot from the connected restored service stopped Bridge successfully6.320s, then D-Bus; one instantlink.disconnect_failed code=-3 warning occurred as Bluetooth stopped. It remains recorded rather than suppressed; no worker-stuck, grace expiry, forced kill or resource failure. The original daemon ordering is preserved; independent BlueZ shutdown can still remove the link.

External BlueZ Disconnect→fresh automatic status 11.004s during normal screen-off idle. All21samples samePID501/600MHz/powersave/GPIO24low/FTP220+200; film10→10. Samples start1.834s after dispatch. One initial absent scan/INFO recovered through the existing prompt retry; no manual Reconnect or warning/error. Internal manual-lock flag/physical contacts not introspected.

Isolated installed production FTP received an886byte JPEG into its ReceivedImage queue with exact SHA, STOR226/NOOP200. Temporary directory/credentials/highport and no consumer/native backend prevent printing. Normal port21 retained. Physical Sony camera and normal print dispatch not tested.

Bridge501/manager service active/zero automatic restarts, Printer connected/fresh, throttle0x0, network/Bluetooth/backup socket active; reviewed source/unit/native hashes. Complete current-boot Bridge PID journal97records/zero warnings-errors; broader five-service review128records retains BlueZ directory-mode/no-matching-connection notices and manager hotspot bind pending (resolved about1s later). No global warning-free claim. Private raw journal reviewed and remote copy removed.

Final independent evidence review accepted the rejected experiment and restored live validation. Measurements. No Printer image/print/actuator commands or film used. No application code, native artifact, CPU tier, config or driver change retained.

docs.title: Later handoff availability
docs.text: After the passing boot/reconnect checks, the Printer link dropped and a subsequent automatic scan reported not advertising. No physical power-state observation was made. The Bridge handled the disconnect without warning/error and remained PID501/600MHz/powersave, FTP220/200, manager659 active/zero automatic restarts, accepted source/unit hashes and clean manifestad72ada. The evidence handoff snapshot records this later snapshot; it does not replace or invalidate the earlier passing tests. Do not describe the Printer as connected at final handoff. No further Printer availability is needed to complete the already accepted unit audit; no film used.

docs.title: Bridge management configuration
docs.text: The Bridge manager exposes authenticated configuration at /v1/config. The App loads this configuration, validates a draft and applies a field diff. The independent Printer correction section is additive; older configurations and older responses without it default to zero.

docs.title: Local backups and Printer pairing
docs.text:
Authenticated POST /v1/backup/create creates a verified on-device configuration backup. POST /v1/backup/restore accepts its backup_id and restores that local archive. Pre-update backups use the same private backup service. Backup response identifiers and restore payloads retain their existing contract; archive download/upload is not provided by these endpoints.

Backups include the saved Printer selection and its persisted BlueZ info file, when present. An adapter identity file is included when the selected device has a stored bond. Unrelated devices, adapter settings and scan caches are excluded. A Printer without an OS-level bond is normal and still has its saved selection backed up. Ambiguous adapter or device selection is rejected rather than including unrelated pairing data.

The manager remains ib with NoNewPrivileges=yes. A socket-activated root helper accepts only local backup create/restore requests from ib or root. Its code is a separate root-owned stdlib-only copy under /usr/local/libexec/instantlink-bridge-backup, loaded with isolated system Python. Deploy, provisioning and current firmware installation refresh this helper.

Archives and manifests reside in /var/lib/InstantLinkBridgeBackups, root-owned with directory mode 0700 and file mode 0600. Keep the latest three verified backups. Pairing secrets remain inside these private archives and are excluded from responses and diagnostic logs.

Restore validates archive hashes, allowed product paths and private pairing-file modes before writing. Pairing restoration requires the same active Bluetooth adapter. A conflicting adapter identity is rejected if another saved device could be affected. The Bridge runtime stops for restore; BlueZ also stops and reloads when pairing state is restored. Previously active services are started again on completion or failure. Restored Bridge state remains writable by ib, while pairing files remain root-only. Old archives without pairing data remain supported. Deployment records are retained in the archive for context and integrity checks but are not applied during configuration restore: the current firmware and native fingerprints stay intact.

docs.title: Listener recovery
docs.text:
The manager binds configured device addresses individually. If USB is available before the hotspot address, it serves USB immediately and retries only the missing address, with backoff from 1 to 10 seconds. Once all listeners bind, retries stop. A missing address does not widen the bind to a wildcard or change USB-local authentication. If no configured address can bind, the service fails for its existing systemd restart policy. API payloads are unchanged.

Hello/status collection runs outside the HTTP event loop. Stable system identity and versions are cached for at most 60 seconds and invalidated after firmware install/rollback attempts. Configuration, pairing state and system metrics are collected for each response.

docs.title: Print review delay
docs.text:
workflow.auto_print_delay_s defaults to 1 second when absent. Management updates accept 1 (Review 1s), 5 (Review 5s), 0 (Print immediately) or "off" (Confirm each). Boolean, negative, non-finite and other numeric values are rejected by the management API. Stored legacy positive delays outside these choices map to the 1-second review; explicit 5-second, immediate and manual settings are preserved. The App and Bridge settings expose all four choices.

The countdown begins after preparation displays the photo. Editing or choosing a tool switches that photo to manual confirmation. Changing the review delay does not alter active print speed.

docs.title: Printer correction
docs.text:
A configuration response includes:

{"correction": {"saturation": 0}}

A configuration update/validation diff may include:

{"correction": {"saturation": 50}}

correction.saturation must be an integer between −100 and +100. Boolean, floating-point, string and out-of-range values are rejected with a field error for correction.saturation. It persists under [correction] in /etc/InstantLinkBridge/config.toml:

[correction]
saturation = 50

Correction compensates Printer output independently of the creative [adjustments] Look. It runs at print resolution after the Look, before JPEG encoding. Zero preserves existing output. It applies to Bridge print output and its final LCD preview; Sync originals are unchanged. The App exposes this section separately and preserves correction when Looks change.

docs.title: Unlock input guard
docs.text:
Configuration responses include the UI setting:

{"ui": {"unlock_requires_three_presses": true}}

The field defaults to true when absent in stored configuration or older responses. The App preserves that default when loading an older Bridge response. A configuration update/validation diff can toggle it:

{"ui": {"unlock_requires_three_presses": false}}

Only JSON booleans are accepted. Strings, numbers and other types produce a field error for ui.unlock_requires_three_presses. The value persists in /etc/InstantLinkBridge/config.toml:

[ui]
unlock_requires_three_presses = true

The LCD exposes the same setting at Settings → System → Unlock: 3 presses.

When enabled, either manual lock or automatic screen-off requires three consecutive presses of the same physical button to unlock. The first input wakes the prompt and starts the awake CPU tier; the second advances its count; the third restores the latest live screen. A different button resets progress to one for that button. Every accepted press restarts the 10-second inactivity timer, whether it advances or resets the count. KEY1 and joystick press remain distinct, despite both normally generating Select. Physical buttons must be released between presses.

For virtual input, repeat the same action three consecutive times. A different action resets progress to one; remote and physical inputs have separate identities and cannot combine their presses. All inputs are consumed until unlocking completes, so the next input performs a normal action. An incomplete sequence expires 10 seconds after its last accepted press and returns to dark locked idle, with its count reset. FTP, status activity and screen polling do not restart the unlock timer. Active preparation/printing remains boosted; background receive, Sync and Printer reconnect remain operational.

When disabled, one input wakes and repaints the screen without executing its normal action. The Linux framebuffer packs exact little-endian RGB565 with local NumPy vector buffers when available, keeping the same channel quantization and pixel ordering. The first frame uses Pillow and finishes painting before one background task loads the faster backend; unavailable NumPy or standalone boot-splash operation keeps the exact Pillow path. Closing the display prevents a delayed backend switch. Frames are drawn and written synchronously; wake restores pixels before enabling the backlight. Text measurements and grayscale glyph masks use bounded in-memory caches keyed by the resolved font and text. Each frame still resolves current layout, theme and animation state; unsupported drawing/font cases keep the original Pillow path.

The physical and virtual LCDs share this behavior and the existing abstract input API. This input guard prevents accidental button actions; it is not an authentication mechanism.

docs.title: Service startup
docs.text: The Bridge orders startup after the system D-Bus daemon, preserving the reverse shutdown order for cleanup. Default systemd initialization and filesystem dependencies remain enabled. Network, DHCP and Bluetooth start independently; LCD and FTP do not wait for network-online. Printer requests still wait for the application pairing-agent readiness gate. The manager retains independent startup/recovery and its exact USB/hotspot listener bindings. Ordering the Bridge only after the bus socket was benchmarked and rejected; it showed no meaningful readiness gain and removed daemon shutdown ordering.

docs.title: Python startup imports
docs.text:
The native Bridge startup loads LCD, input, camera receive and reconnect infrastructure while keeping diagnostic Bleak protocol code and photo processing out of the eager import graph. Transport-neutral Printer records and image settings live in lightweight shared modules; their existing public import paths remain aliases. The image worker itself is lightweight and still loads during startup. No extra background prewarm runs beside Bluetooth connection.

First-use processing imports run in existing image processes, native preparation/metadata threads or an awaited editor preload before its first frame. Cleanup joins any in-progress fallback import off the event loop. The Post editor may wait for this first import before consuming the next queued button action; normal network, power and render callbacks continue. Image algorithms, model orientation, CPU tiers and screen-dependent reconnect cadence are unchanged.

docs.title: Runtime maintenance and diagnostics
docs.text:
When the screen is dark, display maintenance waits up to five seconds rather than polling every 0.35 seconds. Printer-readiness and iPhone-activity expiry deadlines shorten that wait; display transitions interrupt it immediately. About-page version/metrics collectors are not started while the screen is dark. Camera receive, network recovery, Printer polling and the configured CPU tiers continue independently.

Physical buttons use a Linux GPIO v2 event descriptor on supported Raspberry Pi controllers. The kernel applies the existing 50 ms stable debounce; asyncio reads only when an edge is ready. This removes the input alert thread's frequent idle wakeups. All eight mappings, physical button identities, held-press behavior and lock/unlock rules are preserved. If requests or event reads fail, input falls back to GPIO Zero/lgpio. Lost event sequences resynchronize current levels and discard uncertain presses, preventing a partial sequence from accidentally unlocking. Startup logs identify the backend and any fallback.

At the default INFO log level, successful Printer status is recorded on first observation, value/recovery changes and a five-minute heartbeat. Unchanged intermediate observations and routine scan progress are DEBUG. Expected Printer absence is recorded once at INFO until its state changes. An exact native GATT setup disconnect is INFO for the first two failures in an unresolved episode; the third and later failures retain rate-limited warnings. Fresh status or a different selected Printer resets that budget. Authentication and unknown failures remain warnings. Native stage/detail are retained, and the UI does not duplicate a failure already reported by the backend. BLE setup failures carry unconfirmed scan diagnostics rather than incorrectly claiming the Printer is absent. Use the Bridge executable's --log-level DEBUG option when detailed poll/scan records are needed.

Cancelling a native operation retains serialization until its blocking worker has finished or the existing stuck-worker deadline triggers recovery. Completed worker/sender failures are distinguished from watchdog deadline expiry, and obsolete status results cannot initiate recovery or alter the current UI. Retired status tasks remain owned through shutdown cleanup.

Printer polling checks the saved bond before its first fetch after startup. The existing BlueZ guard removes only disconnected identities and preserves the saved selection; a live Printer keeps its bond. Polling waits for active rebond and silent-link recovery before connecting again.

Offline Printer discovery uses one-second scan windows and a one-second target period while the LCD is visible. Long scan/connection work completes before another attempt; a 50 ms minimum yield prevents a tight retry loop. While the screen is dark, the saved printer.search_interval_s applies (30 seconds by default), with five-second scan windows. Locking reschedules the wait; the first unlock press interrupts it and requests a prompt check. The Screen-off search option controls the dark period; connected keepalive/status timing remains separate.

After a previously responsive Printer stops responding, the Bridge permits two prompt status/reconnect retries with at least 250 ms between attempts. If they fail, it resumes the configured offline search period. An exact native setup disconnect also permits this bounded burst at startup, once until fresh status; repeated drops or intervening absent scans do not replenish it. An absent Printer follows the screen-based cadence, including at startup. Confirmed native session closure retires a cached link immediately; uncertain status failures retain the existing two-failure tolerance.

Linux address probes read fresh bounded kernel snapshots, avoiding repeated ip launches. Scope, prefix, administrative state and polling/recovery timing are preserved. Incomplete, interrupted or unavailable snapshots use the existing bounded ip fallback; there is no address cache.

Silent Printer recovery reads current connected identities through the existing BlueZ agent connection. Exact addresses and normalized Alias matching are preserved; ambiguous adapter topology or unavailable/invalid data uses the existing CLI lookup. Empty/offline snapshots require no discovery commands. Disconnect rules, scan cadence and recovery cooldown are unchanged; cancellation does not disconnect the shared agent.

Before a proactive bond reset, the Bridge checks all matching connected identities using a fresh, bounded snapshot on that same agent bus. Exactly one known adapter is required; unknown connection state, incomplete scope, ambiguous topology or unavailable data uses the established CLI gate. A live identity prevents bond removal. Removal commands and their ordering are unchanged.

With native libraries providing instantlink_connect_named_with_status, a fresh status request uses the successful connection's initial Printer read directly. It is a handoff within that request, with no retained status cache or TTL. Every later poll queries the Printer again. Older libraries use the established connect-and-status path; an error from the new function does not trigger another connect API. Print setup retains its existing connection path.

After a disconnect event, the serialized loop finishes guarded bond cleanup before its first fresh scan. Recovery owners are joined before reconnect or print handoff; CLI subprocesses are killed and reaped on cancellation. Printing aborts if mutating cleanup cannot finish within six seconds, while unfinished owners remain retained for recovery. Periodic fallback and the existing bounded reconnect burst are preserved.

Native notification setup overlaps the read-only MTU lookup with its existing 200 ms settling interval. Missing metadata or the default ATT MTU is refreshed after settling within the original total budget; known small limits are retained on refresh failure. No initial command can start before settling, and fragment fallback, print bytes and command pacing are preserved.

Native Linux discovery uses fresh bulk BlueZ metadata to skip clearly unrelated cached devices. Possible Printers retain their existing property and connection checks. Invalid or unavailable metadata falls back to those checks; scan cadence, unfiltered advertisements and saved-Printer reconnect behavior are preserved. The extra reader has a bounded query budget and owns its separate bus resource.

The selected Printer also has a disconnect watch on the existing agent bus. After successful status, a complete signal-maintained Device1 identity snapshot can identify a unique live physical path without another bus request. It is seeded by existing authenticated reads, bound to the current agent lifecycle/BlueZ owner and used only while the shared bus is connected. Missing, invalidated or ambiguous state retains the bounded fresh-snapshot fallback. The identity cache is capped at 512 device rows, adds no startup task or query, and is never used for the fresh bond-removal gate. Stale iOS/Android identities are ignored and ambiguous identities retain polling. Authenticated connection-loss, device/adapter-removal and BlueZ-owner events wake the serialized status loop, including its ordinary waiting gap. Callbacks do not issue Printer commands or change CPU tiers. Printing pauses and selection/generation changes disarm the watch. A delayed registration must still own its token and selected address/name before its result can retain a subscription.

Signals arriving during status or watch setup remain pending, so an earlier reply cannot restore readiness after the link has dropped. A 250 ms recovery gap bounds repeat cycles; bond cleanup and existing two-retry/offline cadence remain. Ten-second periodic status checks remain the fallback. An arming failure is tried/logged once per connected episode, then a new status generation or offline/reconnect transition permits another attempt. There are no per-poll watch snapshots or new idle queries.

The pairing agent tracks BlueZ owner changes on its existing bus and registers again after a daemon restart. If the agent manager or selected adapter appears late, its interface-added event retries registration. These watches do not poll while ready. Owner changes invalidate stale registration and snapshot results; shutdown removes its matches and waits for owned tasks to finish.

Network readiness uses addresses from administratively enabled interfaces. An interface that is down can retain its IPv4 address; that address no longer suppresses hotspot recovery or appears in Bonjour advertisement candidates. Carrier is not required for dormant interfaces.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text: Flag Description --device <NAME> Target a specific printer by BLE name --json Structured JSON output where implemented (scan, info, status). The flag is global, so it also appears in print and led help even though those commands still use human-readable output. --help Show help --version Show version

docs.title: instantlink scan
docs.text:
Scan for nearby Instax Link printers over BLE.

instantlink scan
instantlink scan --duration 10
instantlink scan --json
Option Default Description --duration <SECS> 5 BLE scan duration in seconds

JSON output is an array of printer names.

docs.title: instantlink info
docs.text:
Show battery, film, charging, model, and print-count data.

instantlink info
instantlink info --device "INSTAX-12345678"
instantlink info --duration 10
instantlink info --json
Option Default Description --duration <SECS> 5 BLE scan duration in seconds

JSON output:

{
  "name": "INSTAX-12345678",
  "model": "Instax Mini Link",
  "battery": 85,
  "is_charging": false,
  "film_remaining": 8,
  "print_count": 42
}

docs.title: instantlink print <IMAGE>
docs.text:
Print an image file to the connected printer.

instantlink print photo.jpg
instantlink print photo.png --quality 90 --fit contain
instantlink print photo.jpg --color-mode natural
Option Default Description --quality <1-100> 97 JPEG compression quality --fit <mode> crop crop, contain, or stretch --color-mode <mode> rich rich or natural

Fit modes:

  • crop resizes to fill, cropping edges when needed
  • contain preserves the full image and adds white bars
  • stretch warps to exact printer dimensions

The printer model determines the final pixel size and maximum JPEG size. Current limits are Mini 105KB, Mini Link 3 55KB, Square 105KB, and Wide 225KB.

docs.title: instantlink led set <COLOR>
docs.text:
Set the printer LED color and pattern.

instantlink led set "#FF0000"
instantlink led set "#00FF00" --pattern breathe
Option Default Description --pattern <type> solid solid, blink, or breathe

Color format: #RRGGBB or RRGGBB.

docs.title: instantlink led off
docs.text:
Turn off the printer LED.

instantlink led off

docs.title: instantlink status

Combined connectivity check and printer status.

instantlink status
instantlink status --json

JSON output when connected:

{
  "connected": true,
  "name": "INSTAX-12345678",
  "model": "Instax Mini Link",
  "battery": 85,
  "is_charging": false,
  "film_remaining": 8,
  "print_count": 42

  "connected": false

docs.title: FFI Reference
docs.text: instantlink-ffi exposes the Rust core through a C ABI for Swift, C, and other native callers.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
cargo build --release -p instantlink-ffi

Artifacts:

  • target/release/libinstantlink_ffi.dylib
  • target/release/libinstantlink_ffi.a

By default, cbindgen writes the generated header into Cargo's OUT_DIR. To refresh the checked-in header at crates/instantlink-ffi/include/instantlink.h, build with:

INSTANTLINK_UPDATE_HEADER=1 cargo build --release -p instantlink-ffi

To verify that the checked-in header matches the generated ABI without leaving drift behind, run:

bash scripts/check-ffi-header.sh --release

Release CI runs this drift check before packaging the FFI zip, so InstantLink-FFI-*.zip only ships with a header that matches the generated bindings.

docs.title: Status Codes
docs.text:
All exported functions return i32 status codes:

Code Meaning 0 Success -1 Printer not found or no device connected -2 Multiple printers found -3 BLE/protocol/internal error or panic caught -4 Timeout -5 Invalid argument -6 Image processing error -7 Print rejected or unexpected device response -8 No film remaining -9 Battery too low -10 Printer cover is open -11 Printer is busy

docs.title: Connection Progress Callbacks
docs.text: Specific reconnect/pairing flows can use instantlink_connect_named_with_progress(...) or instantlink_connect_named_with_progress_ctx(...) to receive connection-stage events.

docs.title: Base Callback (without context)
docs.text: typedef void (*instantlink_connect_stage_cb)(int32_t stage, const char *detail);

docs.title: Context Callback (macOS app preference)
docs.text:
typedef void (*instantlink_connect_stage_cb_ctx)(int32_t stage, const char *detail, void *context);

The _ctx variant allows passing an opaque context pointer that is returned unchanged to each callback invocation, enabling stateful per-call tracking without global state.

Stage Code Meaning scan_started 0 BLE scan started scan_finished 1 BLE scan finished device_matched 2 Matching printer advertisement found ble_connecting 3 CoreBluetooth connection starting service_discovery 4 GATT service discovery characteristic_lookup 5 Write/notify characteristic resolution notification_subscribe 6 Notification subscription model_detecting 7 Printer model detection status_fetching 8 Initial status fetch connected 9 Connection is ready for use failed 10 Connection failed

detail is optional stage-specific context and is only valid during the callback invocation. Like the print progress callback, the connect-stage callback is invoked from the runtime thread, so UI callers must marshal updates back to the main thread.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
void instantlink_init(void);
int32_t instantlink_connect(void);
int32_t instantlink_connect_named(const char *name, int32_t duration_secs);
int32_t instantlink_connect_named_with_progress(const char *name,
                                                int32_t duration_secs,
                                                instantlink_connect_stage_cb progress_cb);
int32_t instantlink_connect_named_with_progress_ctx(const char *name,
                                                    int32_t duration_secs,
                                                    instantlink_connect_stage_cb_ctx progress_cb,
                                                    void *context);
int32_t instantlink_disconnect(void);
int32_t instantlink_is_connected(void);
int32_t instantlink_shutdown(void);
int32_t instantlink_reset(void);
  • instantlink_is_connected returns 1 for a cached session not known closed, 0 for no session or a terminally closed session, or a negative error code. It is a cheap read-only check: it does not poll hardware or guarantee that a physical link is live.
  • instantlink_connect_named_with_progress is the base entry point for UI-driven reconnect flows; exposes real connection stages
  • instantlink_connect_named_with_progress_ctx is the preferred variant (used by macOS app) because it accepts an opaque context pointer, allowing per-call state without global side effects. The context is passed unchanged to each callback invocation.
  • Context Pointer Contract: The context pointer is cast to usize internally and back; the FFI does not dereference it. The caller is responsible for ensuring the pointer remains valid for the entire duration of the connect operation and properly life-managing the backing object.
  • Callback Invocation: The connect-stage callback is invoked from the tokio runtime thread. Native (UI) callers must marshal updates back to the main thread (e.g., via Grand Central Dispatch on macOS).
  • Thread Safety: Multiple concurrent calls with different context pointers are safe; the FFI serializes internal device state but allows independent progress tracking per call.
  • instantlink_shutdown powers off the connected printer
  • instantlink_reset resets the connected printer

docs.title: Scanning
docs.text:
int32_t instantlink_scan(int32_t duration_secs, char *out_json, int32_t out_len);

Writes a JSON array of printer names into out_json and returns the number of bytes written.

docs.title: Status Queries
docs.text:
int32_t instantlink_battery(void);
int32_t instantlink_film_remaining(void);
int32_t instantlink_film_and_charging(int32_t *out_film, int32_t *out_charging);
int32_t instantlink_print_count(void);
int32_t instantlink_status(int32_t *out_battery, int32_t *out_film,
                           int32_t *out_charging, int32_t *out_print_count);
int32_t instantlink_device_name(char *out, int32_t out_len);
int32_t instantlink_device_model(char *out, int32_t out_len);

docs.title: Printing
docs.text:
int32_t instantlink_print(const char *path, uint8_t quality,
                          uint8_t fit_mode, uint8_t print_option);
int32_t instantlink_print_with_progress(const char *path, uint8_t quality,
                                        uint8_t fit_mode, uint8_t print_option,
                                        void (*progress_cb)(uint32_t sent, uint32_t total));
int32_t instantlink_print_with_progress_ctx(const char *path, uint8_t quality,
                                            uint8_t fit_mode, uint8_t print_option,
                                            instantlink_print_progress_cb_ctx progress_cb,
                                            void *context);

The print-progress callback type:

typedef void (*instantlink_print_progress_cb_ctx)(uint32_t sent, uint32_t total, void *context);

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• fit_mode: 0 = crop, 1 = contain, 2 = stretch
  • print_option: 0 = Rich, 1 = Natural
  • progress_cb is optional and receives acknowledged chunk progress

docs.title: Progress Context Variant
docs.text:
instantlink_print_with_progress_ctx is the preferred variant (used by macOS app) for the same reasons as its connect counterpart:

  • Context Pointer Contract: The context pointer is cast to usize internally; the FFI does not dereference it. Ensure the pointer remains valid for the entire print operation.
  • Callback Invocation: Progress callbacks are invoked from the tokio runtime thread after each chunk is acknowledged. UI callers must synchronize state updates (e.g., via Grand Central Dispatch).
  • Thread Safety: The context pointer is thread-safe by design since it is passed opaque and unchanged to each callback.

docs.title: Prepared JPEG Printing
docs.text:
Callers that already perform model-specific image preparation can send their final JPEG without another resize, flip or JPEG encode:

int32_t instantlink_print_prepared_jpeg(const uint8_t *data, uint32_t data_len,
                                        uint8_t expected_model,
                                        uint8_t transport_flip_applied,
                                        uint8_t print_option);
int32_t instantlink_print_prepared_jpeg_with_progress(const uint8_t *data,
                                                      uint32_t data_len,
                                                      uint8_t expected_model,
                                                      uint8_t transport_flip_applied,
                                                      uint8_t print_option,
                                                      void (*progress_cb)(uint32_t, uint32_t));
int32_t instantlink_print_prepared_jpeg_with_progress_ctx(const uint8_t *data,
                                                          uint32_t data_len,
                                                          uint8_t expected_model,
                                                          uint8_t transport_flip_applied,
                                                          uint8_t print_option,
                                                          instantlink_print_progress_cb_ctx progress_cb,
                                                          void *context);
Model expected_model Dimensions Maximum bytes transport_flip_applied Mini 0 600×800 105,000 0 Mini Link 3 1 600×800 55,000 1 Square 2 800×800 105,000 0 Wide 3 1260×840 225,000 0

The exact detected model must match, including Mini versus Mini Link 3. JPEG data must be a complete 8-bit, three-component baseline JPEG with exact dimensions, within the model's byte budget and without trailing data. Progressive, grayscale, CMYK, arithmetic/lossless JPEG and recognized non-neutral EXIF orientation are rejected. Raw pixel orientation is authoritative. Mini Link 3's vertical transport flip must be applied before encoding; the native path validates the declaration and transmits those bytes unchanged. It cannot infer orientation from arbitrary pixel content, so the caller must uphold that declaration.

The core performs a bounded full decode with warnings treated as errors to detect incomplete entropy scans; it discards validation pixels and performs no new encode. Validation failure returns -6 before any Printer write. Null/empty input, unknown model or flip values outside 0/1 return -5; no connected device returns -1. No legacy retry occurs after a failed send.

data must remain readable and unchanged for the entire synchronous call. Callbacks/context must stay alive until return; callbacks occur after acknowledged chunks and never afterwards. The global device mutex is released before callbacks, while the per-Printer operation lock serializes the transaction. Callbacks must not synchronously start another serialized Printer operation; identity getters are safe. Marshal UI work to the UI thread. All three exports catch Rust panics; the existing file-based functions remain available.

The Bridge detects this optional export in its FFI wrapper. Compatible native builds use an in-memory byte buffer and correctly oriented prepared JPEG; older builds use the legacy unflipped preparation/file path. Physical and virtual LCD previews reverse the transport flip only when rendering. No management or sync API field is added.

docs.title: LED Control
docs.text:
int32_t instantlink_set_led(uint8_t r, uint8_t g, uint8_t b, uint8_t pattern);
int32_t instantlink_led_off(void);
  • pattern: 0 = solid, 1 = blink, 2 = breathe

docs.title: Keepalive
docs.text:
int32_t instantlink_keepalive(void);
int32_t instantlink_set_keepalive_interval(int32_t seconds);
  • Missing native replies trigger a bounded link-state check after one second. Confirmed disconnection closes the old session; inconclusive checks retain the original command deadline. Normal acknowledgements and idle sessions add no checks. Commands are never replayed.
  • instantlink_keepalive sends one status/keepalive request to the connected printer (0 on success)
  • instantlink_set_keepalive_interval configures the background keepalive: 0 disables it, positive values are seconds; a negative value returns -5

docs.title: Swift Usage
docs.text:
The macOS app loads the dylib via dlopen and resolves the exported symbols in InstantLinkFFI.swift (located at macos/InstantLink/InstantLinkFFI.swift). This file demonstrates:

  • Bridging the C FFI functions into Swift async/await methods
  • Using instantlink_connect_named_with_progress_ctx with a boxed Swift closure to deliver connection-stage updates
  • Using instantlink_print_with_progress_ctx with a boxed Swift closure to deliver print-progress updates
  • Dispatching FFI calls onto a dedicated serial queue to prevent race conditions

Example pattern for context-boxed callbacks:

let boxPtr = Unmanaged.passRetained(CallbackBox(closure: { /* ... */ }))

let callback: @convention(c) (Int32, UnsafePointer<CChar>?, UnsafeMutableRawPointer?) -> Void = {
    stage, detail, context in
    guard let context else { return }
    let box = Unmanaged<CallbackBox>.fromOpaque(context).takeUnretainedValue()
    box.closure(stage)
}

// Call FFI with boxPtr.toOpaque() as context
boxPtr.release()  // when done

docs.title: Thread Safety
docs.text:
The FFI layer owns:

  • a global tokio runtime via OnceLock<Runtime>
  • a Mutex-protected connected device handle
  • catch_unwind guards on all exported functions

The macOS wrapper serializes FFI calls on a dedicated serial dispatch queue so reconnect, status, and print operations do not race each other.

Callback Threads: Progress callbacks (connect-stage and print-progress) are invoked from the tokio runtime thread, not the main thread. Native callers must marshal updates back to the main thread (e.g., via DispatchQueue.main.async on macOS).

Context Pointer Safety: The _ctx variants pass the context pointer opaque and unchanged; the FFI does not dereference or copy it. Callers are responsible for lifetime and thread safety of the backing object during the operation.

docs.title: BLE Protocol Reference
docs.text: This documents the Instax Link BLE packet protocol that InstantLink currently implements over BLE GATT.

docs.title: BLE Service
docs.text: Item UUID Service 70954782-2d83-473d-9e5f-81e1d02d5273 Write Characteristic 70954783-2d83-473d-9e5f-81e1d02d5273 Notify Characteristic 70954784-2d83-473d-9e5f-81e1d02d5273

docs.title: Packet Format
docs.text:
[0x41 0x62] [length:2B] [opcode:2B] [payload...] [checksum:1B]
Field Size Description Header 2 bytes Request: 0x41 0x62 (from HEADER constant), Response: 0x61 0x42 (from RESPONSE_HEADER constant) Length 2 bytes Big-endian packet size including header and checksum Opcode 2 bytes Command identifier Payload variable Command-specific data Checksum 1 byte (255 - (sum_of_preceding_bytes & 255)) & 255

docs.title: Query Commands
docs.text:
All status queries use opcode 0x0002 with an InfoType selector byte.

Opcode Name Payload Description 0x0001 Device Info Service SubIndex(1B) Query a device-info string 0x0002 Support Function Info InfoType(1B) Query printer capabilities or status

docs.title: Device Info Sub-Indices
docs.text:
Sub-index Field Example 0x00 Manufacturer FUJIFILM 0x01 Model SP-4 0x02 Serial Number 10458647 0x03 Unknown version 0000 0x04 Hardware version 0102 0x05 Firmware version 1.00

Response format: [return_code] [sub_index] [string_length] [ASCII bytes...]

docs.title: InfoType Values
docs.text:
InfoType Name Response Data 0x00 Image Support Info Width(2B), Height(2B) 0x01 Battery Status State(1B), Level(1B) 0x02 Printer Function Info Film remaining in bits 0...3, charging in bit 7 0x03 Print Count Exact 2B legacy count, or observed Square 8B data: count(4B, big-endian) + 4B uninterpreted

The Square Link's observed history data is eight bytes: a leading big-endian 32-bit counter followed by four bytes whose meaning is unverified. For example, 00 03 00 00 00 43 00 00 00 12 (including status and InfoType) reports 67. The exact two-byte legacy count remains supported. The core's public count remains u16 (0–65,535); larger counters and ambiguous payload lengths are rejected, rather than truncated. The diagnostic Python backend applies the same limit. No FFI signature changes.

docs.title: Status Response Payload Format
docs.text:
All status queries return a packet with response header 0x61 0x42 (see crates/instantlink-core/src/protocol.rs), followed by this payload:

Offset Field Size Description 0 Return Code 1 B 0x00 for success 1 InfoType 1 B Echoes the requested info type 2+ Data variable Type-specific payload (see table above)

Printer Function Info (InfoType 0x02) bit layout:

Bit(s) Field Range Notes 0–3 Film Remaining 0–15 Number of exposures left 4–6 Reserved — Not used 7 Is Charging 0 or 1 1 if printer is on charger

docs.title: Image Transfer
docs.text:
Opcode Name Payload Response 0x1000 Download Start PictureType + PrintOption + PrintOption2 + Zero + ImageSize(4B) ACK status 0x1001 Data ChunkIndex(4B) + chunk data ACK status 0x1002 Download End none ACK status 0x1003 Download Cancel none ACK status 0x1080 Print Image none Print status

Success is model-aware. InstantLink accepts status 0 and each model's success code:

  • Mini: 0
  • Mini Link 3: 16
  • Square: 12
  • Wide: 15

Rejection codes currently mapped in the core:

  • 178 no film
  • 179 cover open
  • 180 low battery
  • 181 printer busy

docs.title: Power and LED Commands
docs.text:
Opcode Name Description 0x0100 Shut Down Power off the printer 0x0101 Reset Reset the printer 0x3000 XYZ Axis Info Query accelerometer/orientation 0x3001 LED Pattern Settings Set LED color or animation 0x3010 Additional Printer Info Query additional printer info

LED payload format:

[when:1B] [frame_count:1B] [speed:1B] [repeat:1B] [B,G,R per frame...]

Colors are sent in BGR order.

docs.title: Print Flow
docs.text:
1. Connect to the printer over BLE
  2. Discover services and subscribe to notifications
  3. Query Image Support Info
  4. Detect the model:
  5. match the reported width and height
  6. use exact DIS model number FI033 to distinguish Mini Link 3 at 600 × 800
  7. reject known DIS numbers that conflict with the reported dimensions
  8. Resize and JPEG-encode the image for the detected model
  9. Apply vertical flip if required by model (see Mini Link 3 section below)
  10. Send Download Start and wait for ACK
  11. Send Data chunks, waiting for ACK after each chunk
  12. Send Download End and wait for ACK
  13. Send Print Image and accept 0 or the model-specific success code
  14. Disconnect

The native BLE transport may resend the read-only Image Support Info query once if no matching ACK arrives within one second. Both writes and response waits share the original ten-second deadline and retain command serialization. Write failures, link errors and malformed responses do not trigger a resend. A failed model query retires the connection; this retry does not apply to image transfer or print commands.

docs.title: Mini Link 3 Vertical-Flip Behavior
docs.text:
The Mini Link 3 printer requires a vertically flipped image upload. This is the only printing difference between the Mini Link 3 and the standard Mini Link.

Detection

Mini Link 3 is detected via the BLE Device Information Service (DIS) model number characteristic:

  • After trimming ASCII whitespace, the DIS model number must equal FI033 and the image support dimensions must equal 600 × 800 to select PrinterModel::MiniLink3.
  • Both Mini Link and Mini Link 3 report 600 × 800, so the DIS hint is necessary to distinguish them.
  • Strings containing FI033 with other characters are rejected rather than selecting Mini with a different upload orientation. Exact FI017 requires Square dimensions (800 × 800).
  • Other unknown or missing DIS hints use the reported dimensions. Unknown dimensions are rejected.

See crates/instantlink-core/src/device.rs, detect_model().

Flip Application

The JPEG image payload is flipped vertically before fragmentation and transmission:

  1. Load and resize the image to printer dimensions (600 × 800)
  2. Apply vertical flip via image.flipv() if the model spec has flip_vertical: true
  3. JPEG-encode the flipped image
  4. Chunk and send the resulting bytes with standard ACK-based flow

See crates/instantlink-core/src/image.rs, prepare_image() and prepare_image_from_bytes() functions (lines 162–164 and 186–188).

Printer-Side Expectation

The printer expects the entire image to be flipped once at upload time. Chunking and acknowledgement protocol are otherwise identical to other models. The flip is applied only to the JPEG row order, not to the wire framing or packet structure.

docs.text: Model Width Height Chunk Size Max Image Size Success Code Notes Mini Link 600 800 900 B 105 KB 0 Standard Mini behavior Mini Link 3 600 800 900 B 55 KB 16 Uses DIS hint FI033, vertically flipped upload Square Link 800 800 1808 B 105 KB 12 Adds packet and pre-execute delays Wide Link 1260 840 900 B 225 KB 15 Wide-format image limit

Transport Status in InstantLink Notes BLE GATT Implemented Primary transport in transport.rs RFCOMM/SPP Not implemented Protocol-level background only USB CDC ACM Not implemented Protocol-level background only

docs.title: Negotiated BLE Fragment Size
docs.text:
Protocol packets and model JPEG chunks are distinct from individual GATT writes. Their bytes, checksums, indexes, padding and ACK order do not change when the write payload limit changes.

On Linux, each new connection performs a bounded one-second BlueZ query for the exact connected device, unique Instax service and write characteristic. The characteristic must advertise write-without-response and expose a valid 23–517-byte MTU. The selected payload is MTU − 3, capped at 236 bytes. The diagnostic download/cancel probe can explicitly compare up to 244 bytes. The 236-byte production ceiling avoids extra HCI fragmentation on the tested Pi controller. A known smaller MTU is honored (23 selects 20). Missing, malformed, ambiguous or unavailable metadata uses the existing 182-byte path. Other platforms retain 182 bytes. BlueZ 5.82 characteristic API.

The query has no per-fragment shell or D-Bus lookup. At most one blocking bus open may be outstanding; late results own their unspawned resources, and live query/listener tasks have cleanup guards. Every connection discovers its own capability again. Raw sends and complete send/ACK transactions share the transport command lock.

A failed, timed-out or cancelled delivery poisons the session. No uncertain packet or print job is replayed. Before reuse, a new transport requires a bounded disconnect and an authoritative disconnected result. If an actual enlarged fragment was attempted, that exact device uses conservative fragments on its next connection for the process lifetime. A tiny status failure requires link reset without disabling larger writes. Known smaller MTUs still clamp conservative fragments. The recovery cache holds at most 128 device identities; saturation selects conservative fragments and reset for all new connections, preserving safety without unbounded growth.

Disconnect immediately closes the transport to new commands and marks uncertain teardown for fresh-link reset. Physical disconnect is attempted before querying connection state; an authoritative disconnected result permits idempotent cleanup even when the disconnect RPC reports an error. Cancellation or an unknown/still-connected result retains the reset requirement. Linux allows five seconds for physical disconnect and the FFI allows eight seconds for full teardown, covering BlueZ's delayed disconnect. State queries retain their two-second budget. Other platforms retain the existing two-second action / three-second FFI budgets.

This does not reduce protocol chunk pacing or pre-execute waits. Printer firmware acceptance of larger fragments requires physical validation in addition to a negotiated ATT MTU.

docs.title: Print-history replies
docs.text: The observed Square reply body has eight bytes: the leading four form a big-endian print counter, followed by four uninterpreted bytes. Exact two-byte legacy counters are also accepted. The current public count type remains u16; larger counters and malformed lengths are rejected rather than truncated. The no-film probe compares before/after counts as well as film remaining.

docs.title: ACK correlation and chunk pacing
docs.text:
Square Data replies with a five-byte payload must echo the current big-endian chunk index after the status byte. Stale/future or malformed indexed replies do not advance the transfer and share the original transaction deadline. Exact one-byte legacy status replies remain supported. Other models retain their existing response-tail compatibility until their format is verified.

Validated Linux Square connections using the 236-byte payload use a 25 ms intermediate gap after an indexed ACK. Other platforms/models, smaller/unknown payloads and conservative sessions retain model pacing (Square 150 ms). The last chunk retains its model settling delay, and pre-execute waits are separate. Legacy replies cannot authorize a shorter gap. A full-transfer guard handles interrupted Start/Data/End/handoff/execute, including cancellation between ACKs: require a fresh link, never replay the uncertain image, and restore baseline pacing after accelerated uncertainty. Pacing and fragment fallback are separate flags in the bounded device cache. Known NoFilm/CoverOpen/LowBattery rejections require reset without penalizing pacing; busy/unknown/transport errors stay conservative.

The download-only diagnostic can sweep intermediate delays and can exercise the same production transfer loop followed by checked DownloadCancel. Its wrapper rejects LED/PrintImage/reset/shutdown commands; the helper fixes print option 0. No-film tests establish outbound bytes, ACK acceptance, unchanged counters and reconnects, rather than developed-film or mechanical-print measurements.

docs.title: Linux discovery records
docs.text: BlueZ retains names and service UUIDs for saved Printers after they are powered off. Linux discovery excludes a matching record with neither RSSI nor a confirmed connected link. Connected-state queries share a 250 ms budget per collection. Connected Printers remain usable without an advertisement. RSSI may persist after a prior scan, so this is an inactive cache guard rather than proof that every returned Printer is currently reachable.

docs.title: Bridge Sync HTTP API Reference
docs.text: The Bridge exposes a small HTTP API that an iOS app (or any client) uses to pull received camera photos and, on screenless SKUs, to drive the LCD remotely. It is implemented by SyncService (bridge/src/instantlink_bridge/sync/server.py) and runs only when [sync].destination = "iphone" (the Bridge's Sync mode).

docs.title: Endpoint & discovery
docs.text:
Item Value Bind 0.0.0.0:8721 ([sync].port) Discovery Bonjour _instantlink._tcp.local., TXT device, proto Advertised addresses non-loopback IPv4 on wlan0 + usb0, refreshed every 30 s Protocol version 1 (proto field)

The service is reachable over any active IP transport: the Bridge hotspot (192.168.8.1), Same Wi-Fi, or the USB gadget link (192.168.7.1).

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every endpoint requires Authorization: Bearer <token>, compared with hmac.compare_digest. The token is 32 hex chars in /etc/InstantLinkBridge/sync.token (0640), created on first use and rotatable from Settings ▸ Network ▸ Reset sync token (which restarts the service so the new token takes effect; all paired clients must re-pair).

Missing/invalid token → 401 {"error": "unauthorized"} with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.

docs.title: Photo sync endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Response GET /v1/status {"device", "proto", "outbox_depth"} GET /v1/queue {"items": [OutboxItem, …]} oldest first GET /v1/photos/{id} file bytes; Range / 206 supported for resume POST /v1/photos/{id}/ack {"ok": true}; deletes the spool file

OutboxItem fields: item_id (hex), file_name, size_bytes, sha256, received_at (epoch seconds), source_remote_ip.

Queued originals retain their own bytes and checksum when a camera reuses the same upload filename. New spool files use independent inodes; upgrades detach older shared files before they can be changed by a subsequent FTP write.

Unknown id → 404 {"error": "unknown_item", "item_id": …}.

Typical pull loop: GET /v1/queue → for each item GET /v1/photos/{id} (resume with Range if a partial exists) → verify sha256 → save → POST /v1/photos/{id}/ack. Content-Type on the download is guessed from the file name (defaults to image/jpeg); note Sony writes HEIF as .HIF, which clients must map to HEIF when saving.

docs.title: Virtual-LCD endpoints (plan 054)
docs.text:
Present only when [sync].remote_ui = true (default). They let a phone act as the Bridge's screen on screenless SKUs — the same pure renderer that drives the physical LCD.

Method Path Response GET /v1/screen current 240×240 frame as image/png POST /v1/input {"action": "<a>"} → {"ok": true, "action": "<a>"}

action ∈ up, down, left, right, select, back, help, pair — injected into the same action queue as the physical joystick/keys, so all input handling (settle window, power activity) applies.

When the LCD is locked or automatically dark, repeat the same action three consecutive times to unlock it by default. For example, three separate {"action": "select"} requests progress through 1 / 3, 2 / 3 and the restored live screen. A different action resets progress to 1 / 3 for that action. All inputs are consumed until unlocking completes.

The first input wakes the prompt and starts the awake CPU tier. An incomplete sequence expires 10 seconds after its last accepted input. Every accepted action restarts this inactivity timer, including an action change that resets the count. Rejected input requests and screen polling do not restart the unlock timer. Remote actions use internal remote:<action> identities, distinct from physical GPIO buttons, so remote and physical inputs cannot combine to finish a sequence. No new request field is required. Physical unlock likewise requires the same physical button three consecutive times: KEY1 and joystick press have separate identities even though both normally produce Select.

The Bridge's ui.unlock_requires_three_presses setting can restore single-action wake, which consumes that action without executing it. The screen endpoint renders the shared unlock prompt; receiving photos and Printer operations retain their live state.

Errors: remote_ui = false → 404 {"error": "remote_ui_disabled"}; no snapshot/injector wired → 404 {"error": "remote_ui_unavailable"}; bad action → 400 {"error": "invalid_action", "allowed": [...]}; queue full → 400 {"error": "input_rejected"}; render failure → 500.

A full shared input queue discards its uncertain buffered actions and resets an incomplete unlock attempt. Kernel event loss or input-backend recovery does the same. Subsequent accepted input starts a new sequence; no wire action or field is added.

/v1/screen is CPU-guarded on the Pi Zero 2 W: frames are memoized by snapshot identity and re-rendered at most every ~0.3 s, so a fast-polling client cannot peg the CPU.

docs.title: Security posture (v1)
docs.text: The WPA2 hotspot provides L2 encryption and the bearer token gates access; TLS with a pinned self-signed cert is a v1.5 hardening item. See docs/plans/050-iphone-auto-sync.md and 051-sync-ux-audit.md for the threat model and token-rotation story.

docs.title: Outbox concurrency
docs.text:
Copying and checksumming a new camera file does not block status/queue reads, existing-photo lookup or acknowledgements. Additions remain ordered; a new item becomes visible only after its checksum is complete and its metadata commit is protected by the index lock. Existing range/download and authentication contracts are unchanged. Cancellation of the receive task joins the filesystem transaction before runtime teardown (plan 068).

Index publication precedes the visible queue update and deletion of evicted/acknowledged originals. If publication fails, the committed queue and its originals remain available; unpublished arrivals are cleaned up. Readers continue using the committed snapshot while publication runs.

docs.title: 047 — Core Image / Metal Implementation Mapping
docs.text: Practical implementation reference for the Photos-style editor rebuild (see docs/plans/047-photos-style-editor-audit.md §2.2). Pairs every UI slider to a CIFilter (or custom kernel), names the input parameter, gives the range mapping from Photos' −1..+1 slider to Core Image native ranges, and notes color-space caveats. Sections 2–7 cover pipeline order, live-preview architecture, undo/redo, histograms, crop/perspective, and the eyedropper.
